title: VIT Bhopal University to Host Health Hackathon 3.0 in January 2027
problem_statement:
VIT Bhopal University will host Health Hackathon 3.0 on 28 and 29 January 2027. A pre-event workshop will take place on 27 January 2027.

VIT Bhopal is collaborating with the Whiting School of Engineering at Johns Hopkins University for this event. Its full title is “Health Hackathon 3.0: Global Health Access Innovation Challenge – Next Generation.”

New Ideas for Better Healthcare

The event has a clear aim: it seeks innovative ideas that can improve healthcare accessibility for more people, reduce costs, and enhance overall efficiency. Participants are invited to propose actionable solutions to real-world healthcare challenges.

Key focus areas for submissions include:

  • Low-cost tools and technologies for healthcare delivery.
  • New ways and platforms to support mental health.
  • Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare solutions.
  • Tools leveraging health data analytics to identify and predict health risks.

A Chance to Share and Build Ideas

Health Hackathon 3.0 invites innovators, students, and researchers to present their concepts and refine them further. The emphasis is on practical, high-impact solutions designed to reach underserved communities and individuals facing healthcare access barriers.

Event Overview & Key Dates

• Pre-Event Workshop: 27 January 2027

• Main Hackathon: 28 & 29 January 2027

• Venue: VIT Bhopal University, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh

• Total Prize Pool: ₹2 Lakh

 

 

Registration & Submission

Registration is now open. Interested teams and individuals must submit their project proposals by 31 October 2026. To learn more, view participation guidelines, and complete registration, please visit the official Health Hackathon 3.0 event website
prizes_summary: Cash prizes, certificates, official mentorship, and PPI hiring opportunities.

title: DoomForge
venue_address: Vit Chennai, Kelambakkam - Vandalur Rd, Chennai, Keelakottiyur, Tamil Nadu 600127
problem_statement:
About DOOMFORGE

DOOMFORGE is a two-round business and engineering hackathon that challenges participants to combine strategic thinking, market analysis, and practical software engineering.

The competition is designed to take participants beyond conventional coding challenges. It begins with identifying real-world business problems and market opportunities, followed by hands-on engineering challenges involving existing codebases and open-source development.

Participants will have the opportunity to demonstrate their analytical thinking, technical expertise, creativity, and ability to build practical solutions.

Eligibility and Team Formation

  • Open to college students.
  • Team size: 1 - 3 members.
  • Inter-college teams are allowed.
  • Participants from different academic specialisations are welcome to collaborate.
  • Each participant can be part of only one team.
  • All team members must complete the registration process.

Competition Structure

Round 1: Market Analysis

Duration: 4 December – 6 December 2026

Round 1 focuses on business strategy, market research, and problem identification.

Participants will be presented with a business-oriented problem or scenario. They must analyse the problem, understand the market landscape, identify opportunities, and propose a feasible solution.

What participants need to cover:

  • Problem identification and understanding.
  • Target audience and market analysis.
  • Competitor research and existing solutions.
  • Identification of market gaps and opportunities.
  • Proposed solution, its feasibility, and potential impact.

Submission Format:

Teams must submit a one-minute video explaining their market analysis, identified opportunity, and proposed solution through Unstop.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Depth of market research.
  • Understanding of the problem.
  • Originality and innovation.
  • Feasibility of the proposed solution.
  • Clarity and effectiveness of presentation.

Based on their submissions, selected teams will qualify for the second round.

Round 2: Engineering Arena – Open-Source Development

The second round is a hands-on engineering challenge in which shortlisted teams will work on one of four dedicated GitHub repositories.

Each repository represents a distinct engineering track with its own technical problem space. Participants will be expected to understand the existing codebase, identify areas for improvement, and implement meaningful technical contributions.

Potential engineering challenges include:

  • Developing new features and functionalities.
  • Identifying and fixing bugs.
  • Improving application performance and scalability.
  • Implementing security enhancements.
  • Writing automated tests and improving test coverage.
  • Integrating AI/ML-based capabilities.
  • Improving code quality, maintainability, and documentation.

Submission Format:

All development contributions must be submitted through GitHub Pull Requests (PRs) to the respective repositories.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Functional correctness and completeness.
  • Code quality and maintainability.
  • Technical implementation.
  • Security and reliability.
  • Testing and validation.
  • Innovation and practical impact.

Engineering Tracks

  • DOOMFORGE features four specialised engineering tracks, each backed by a dedicated GitHub repository.
  • Participants will work on the repository and technical challenge specified by the organising team. Further details regarding the repositories, technical requirements, and challenges will be communicated to qualified participants.

Rules and Regulations

  • Teams must consist of a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 3 members.
  • Inter-college participation is permitted.
  • Each participant may register as part of only one team.
  • Round 1 submissions must be submitted within the specified deadline, from 4 December to 6 December 2026.
  • Round 1 submissions must follow the prescribed one-minute video format.
  • Only shortlisted teams will advance to Round 2.
  • Participants must work on their designated GitHub repository and follow the respective technical guidelines.
  • All technical contributions must be submitted through GitHub Pull Requests.
  • Participants must ensure that their submissions are original and that all external resources or third-party contributions are appropriately acknowledged.
  • Plagiarism, unauthorised copying, and misrepresentation of work are strictly prohibited.
  • Attempts to manipulate automated evaluation systems or bypass repository checks may result in disqualification.
  • Participants must adhere to all deadlines and instructions communicated by the organising committee.
  • The organising committee reserves the right to disqualify teams for misconduct or violations of competition rules.
  • The decision of the judging panel and organising committee will be final.

What You Gain

  • Hands-on experience with real-world business and engineering challenges.
  • Exposure to open-source development and collaborative GitHub workflows.
  • An opportunity to demonstrate strategic thinking and technical problem-solving.
  • Experience working with existing codebases and modern software engineering practices.
  • A platform to showcase your engineering capabilities and creativity.

Think strategically. Build relentlessly. Enter DOOMFORGE.

Follow us at https://www.instagram.com/180dc.vitc/

title: Agentic AI Hackathon
problem_statement:
Overview:

  • Date: 14th & 15th Nov, 2026
  • Registrations: Now Open
  • Kickoff Session: 14th Nov (Saturday), 2026

This is a hands-on, build-first hackathon created for individuals who want to launch a real AI product, not just present ideas or mockups.

What You’ll Do:

During this one day, participants will:

  • Conceptualize, build, and launch a complete agentic AI solution
  • Work on practical, real-world challenges
  • Go through the entire product journey:
    • Identifying the problem
    • Designing system architecture
    • Integrating tools and APIs
    • Delivering a functional end product

The core focus is on building AI agents ready for real-world use that can:

  • Think and make decisions.
  • Interact with tools.
  • Execute tasks independently.

By the end, you’ll walk away with a working AI product that can be:

  • Added to your portfolio.
  • Demonstrated in interviews.
  • Expanded into real-world use cases.

Participation Guidelines:

  • You can join individually or in teams (up to 2 members recommended).
  • All development must happen within the hackathon timeframe.
  • You are free to use AI tools, APIs, and frameworks.
  • Participants must clearly document their process (problem → solution → architecture).
  • A functional prototype or live demo is required.

Submission Requirements:

  • A demo video or live working product.
  • Access to the codebase (GitHub or equivalent).
  • A brief explanation of your solution.

Rules & Evaluation:

️ Rules:

  • Fully pre-built solutions are not allowed (starter templates are acceptable).
  • Any form of copying or plagiarism will result in disqualification.
  • Teams must clearly specify their actual contribution vs. AI-generated output.
  • Submissions must be fully working products, not just designs or presentations.
  • All entries must be submitted before the deadline.

The competition will consist of 10 questions to be completed within a total time limit of 100 minutes.

  5. Participants must not share solutions, collaborate with other participants or engage in any unfair practices during the competition.

  6. The use of external assistance or AI tools during the competition is not permitted.

  7. Participants must ensure a stable internet connection throughout the challenge.

  8. Tie-breaker: If two or more participants achieve the same score, the participant who completes the assessment in the shortest time will be ranked higher. For example, if two participants achieve the same score, but Participant 1 finishes at 10:00 AM and Participant 2 finishes at 11:00 AM, Participant 1 will be ranked higher.

title: Madlab - The Ultimate Innovation Hackathon

problem_statement:
MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution.

A Multidisciplinary Innovation Hackathon

About the Opportunity

MADLAB is a high-energy, multidisciplinary hackathon designed for individuals who dare to think differently, communicate confidently, build creatively, and execute ideas into practical solutions. The competition brings together software developers, marketing enthusiasts, sales strategists, business students, designers, and aspiring entrepreneurs to solve challenges through innovation, teamwork, and strategic thinking.

This is not just a coding competition. Participants will be evaluated on their creativity, technical and practical skills, communication, problem-solving, marketing strategies, sales approach, and ability to present and execute ideas.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to college students and aspiring professionals with an interest in technology, business, marketing, sales, design, or entrepreneurship.
  • Participants from all academic streams and specializations are welcome.
  • Students from different colleges can form a team together (inter-college participation is allowed).
  • Participants from different specializations can collaborate in the same team (inter-specialization participation is encouraged).
  • No advanced coding experience is mandatory. Creativity, communication, business thinking, and execution matter just as much as technical skills.
  • Participants must provide accurate registration details and follow the event organizers' instructions.

Team Formation

  • Participants may register individually or in teams of 2–5 members.
  • Teams may include developers, marketers, sales representatives, designers, presenters, and business strategists.
  • Each team should distribute responsibilities effectively and ensure that every member contributes.
  • Each team must nominate one member as its primary point of contact.
  • Team changes after registration require approval from the organizers.

Competition Format and Rounds

Round 1: The Spark — Problem-Solving and Ideation (30 minutes)

Teams receive a problem statement and identify the problem, target audience, and potential solution. They must demonstrate original thinking, practical reasoning, and a clear understanding of the challenge.

Round 2: The Build Lab — Creation and Strategy (90 minutes)

Teams develop a working prototype, business concept, marketing campaign, sales strategy, or another relevant solution according to the assigned challenge. Developers can build prototypes, marketers can design campaigns, and sales-oriented participants can develop pitches and customer acquisition strategies.

Round 3: The Pitch Arena — Presentation and Communication (5–7 minutes per team)

Each team presents its solution to the judges, explaining the problem, proposed solution, target audience, implementation strategy, and expected impact. Teams must communicate their ideas clearly and confidently.

Round 4: The Crossfire — Judges' Q&A (3–5 minutes per team)

Judges question teams about their decisions, originality, feasibility, technical implementation, marketing approach, sales strategy, and scalability. Participants must demonstrate ownership of their work and respond professionally.

Total estimated competition duration: 2.5–4 hours, depending on the number of teams and event scheduling.

Problem Statements

Participants will receive one assigned problem statement or challenge from the organizers. Challenges may cover the following areas:

  • Technology and Development: Build a prototype, tool, website, application, or automation that solves a real-world problem.
  • Marketing and Creativity: Develop a creative marketing campaign, brand strategy, social media concept, or customer engagement plan.
  • Sales and Business Growth: Create a sales pitch, customer acquisition strategy, conversion plan, or business growth model.
  • Communication and Innovation: Present an original idea, demonstrate persuasive communication, and turn a concept into an actionable solution.

The final problem statement, required deliverables, and evaluation criteria will be communicated to participants before the relevant round begins.

Evaluation Criteria

Participants will be evaluated on the following criteria:

  • Creativity and originality — 20%
  • Problem-solving and practical execution — 20%
  • Technical or domain-specific skills — 20%
  • Communication and presentation — 15%
  • Marketing, sales, and business thinking — 15%
  • Teamwork, adaptability, and Q&A performance — 10%

Judges' decisions will be final, subject to the event's published rules.

Competition Rules

  • All submissions must be created or substantially developed by the participating team during the competition, unless the organizers explicitly permit pre-existing resources.
  • Pre-existing code, templates, AI tools, and third-party resources may be used only as permitted by the organizers. Teams must disclose significant external contributions.
  • Plagiarism, copied submissions presented as original work, fabricated results, impersonation, and misrepresentation of contributions are prohibited.
  • Every team member must contribute meaningfully to the competition.
  • Participants must respect fellow competitors, judges, mentors, volunteers, and organizers.
  • Teams must submit their deliverables before the announced deadline. Late submissions may be penalized or disqualified.
  • Participants must not attempt unauthorized access to systems, misuse personal data, or engage in unethical or illegal activities.
  • All presentations must be professional, relevant to the assigned challenge, and completed within the allocated time.
  • Participants must follow the venue's safety requirements and the organizers' instructions throughout the event.
  • Any disputes, rule violations, or exceptional circumstances will be reviewed by the organizing committee.

Deliverables

Each team must submit the relevant deliverables for its assigned challenge, which may include:

  • A working prototype, demonstration, campaign concept, sales pitch, or business solution.
  • A short explanation of the problem and the proposed solution.
  • A presentation outlining the approach, target audience, execution plan, and expected impact.
  • Supporting materials such as designs, mock-ups, code, campaign creatives, or a business model, where applicable.

Final Note

MADLAB is an opportunity to move beyond ideas and demonstrate what you can create, communicate, build, market, and sell. Whether you are a developer, marketer, salesperson, designer, or business thinker, your skills have a place in the lab.

Bring your creativity. Challenge the ordinary. Execute the extraordinary.

MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution.

title: SHAASTRA 2027
problem_statement:
Event Description

Abstract Submission Round
Participants must submit an aircraft abstract in A4 format, with 1.5 line spacing and a maximum of 15 pages, along with a ZIP file containing 5–10 construction photographs. The abstract should cover the aircraft design, including dimensions, wing area, estimated flight speed, reservoir and mounting, release mechanism, leakage prevention, centre-of-gravity management, and safe operation. The prescribed format must be downloaded from the respective IIT website and submitted by email at least 20 days before the competition. Shortlisted teams will be announced 15 days before the competition. If multiple teams participate from the same institution, their aircraft designs must be distinct, with at least a 2.5% difference in wingspan, chord, and fuselage length; otherwise, the teams will be disqualified.

Qualifier Round
The Qualifier Round aims to select the top 30 teams with lightweight aircraft capable of safe, controlled flight carrying a 1,000 mL water payload. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds with the full payload, with no water release required. The water must be stored in a sealed, securely mounted, removable reservoir, with the reservoir and release mechanism included in the aircraft’s empty weight. Judges will inspect the system before takeoff, and there must be no visible leakage. Each attempt must be completed within 3 minutes. Failure to maintain 30 seconds of safe flight or any visible leakage before landing results in a zero score. Each team gets two attempts, with the higher score counted, and only teams that safely complete the loaded flight can advance. The top 30 teams qualify for the Main Round and receive ₹5,000 towards material costs, subject to providing the bank details of one designated team member.

Main Round
In the Main Round, the aircraft must carry 1,000 mL of water in an inspected, sealed, removable reservoir and release it while flying over the designated simulated fire/release zone. The aircraft must fly safely for at least 30 seconds before release, which must be manually triggered by the pilot using a single transmitter channel; automatic or programmed release is not allowed. Judges will verify that the release begins within the marked zone, which is approximately 40 m from the take-off/landing area, though its location and dimensions may be adjusted based on venue and wind conditions. The amount of water released will be determined by weighing the reservoir before and after the attempt; if leakage before the commanded release cannot be distinguished from the actual release, the attempt scores zero. Each team gets two attempts, with the better score counted, and each attempt must complete the release and landing within 3 minutes.

Rules and Regulations
The same aircraft must be used throughout all rounds and must match the submitted design; repairs are allowed, but replacement aircraft are not. Teams should carry spare components and be ready when called, or risk losing their attempt or flight time. A 2.4 GHz radio is required unless another frequency is approved in advance, receivers must remain in receiver mode only, and metal propellers are prohibited. All systems will be inspected before the competition, and non-functional equipment can lead to dismissal. Teams must carry their own equipment and cannot share components with other teams. Aircraft may use powered take-off with landing gear or manual launch. A team member cannot participate in more than one team. Teams must be ready to fly after the 120-second interval following the previous attempt or lose their turn. Reimbursement will only be made to a registered team member whose bank account name matches the registration details. Flying outside the designated zone will result in disqualification, and the aircraft must immediately return and land safely. The take-off, landing, and release zones may vary depending on venue and wind conditions. Teams may participate in only one zonal event, and the same team members must participate in the finals if they qualify.Any attempts to unfairly influence the scoring or disrupt the competition by teams or individuals associated with them, such as parents, professors, trainers, etc., will result in immediate disqualification of the teams. 

Eligibility
Teams must design and fabricate a fixed-wing RC aircraft; ready-made models such as RTF, ARF, and BNF are not allowed. The aircraft must have a thrust-to-weight ratio of ≤1.5 without payload, a maximum propeller diameter of 13 inches, and a wingspan of ≤1 m. Only electric motors are permitted, while IC engines, gyros, receiver programming, mission automation, FPV, and other flying-support systems are prohibited. Teams must consist of 2–4 students, with members from institutions within the same zone; an additional mentor may accompany the team but cannot assist during participation. Only students are eligible, and participants must carry a bona fide certificate signed by the HoD/Dean/Principal along with their college/school ID. Build your portfolio using your preferred technologies and deploy it on a supported platform: Vercel, Netlify, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Railway, Render, or Fly.

Visit https://isonewho.codes/, sign in with GitHub, choose your name, and connect your deployed portfolio URL.

Your portfolio will be accessible through an address such as:

yourname.isonewho.codes

3. Create Your Competition Entry Link

Open the Applications section in your ONEWHO dashboard and add an application with the company name “Unstop.”

This creates your submission link:

https://yourname.isonewho.codes/a/unstop

The application link lets you view recorded judging visits and tracked page activity in your ONEWHO dashboard.

Complete your registration and submit both of the following before the deadline:

  • Your ONEWHO application link ending in /a/unstop.

Creating a ONEWHO name alone does not complete your competition entry. Your submission must also be completed on Unstop.

Judging Criteria

Rules and Guidelines

Judging rewards your original contribution; changing only the name on a template will not score well on creativity.

problem_statement:
AGENTX 2.0 is a national-level hackathon organized by HackQube, bringing together students, developers, AI enthusiasts, and innovators to build intelligent, technology-driven solutions to real-world challenges.

The hackathon focuses on Artificial Intelligence, AI Agents, Agentic AI, Generative AI, and intelligent automation. Participants will have the opportunity to transform ideas into functional prototypes that demonstrate innovation, technical excellence, practical applicability, and real-world impact.

Participants must select one of the official problem statements and develop a solution that addresses the specified challenge.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Students enrolled in recognized colleges or universities are eligible to participate.
  • Developers, AI enthusiasts, and aspiring innovators may participate, subject to the registration requirements.
  • Participants must provide accurate information during registration.
  • All participants must comply with the hackathon rules and submission guidelines.

Team Formation Rules

  • Team Size: 2–4 members per team.
  • Inter-college Teams: Allowed. Team members may belong to different colleges or universities.
  • Inter-specialization Teams: Allowed. Members from different academic disciplines and technical specializations may collaborate.
  • Each participant may be part of only one team.
  • Teams must provide accurate details for all members during registration.
  • One team must submit only one project for evaluation.

Official Problem Statements

Teams must select one of the following eight problem statements and develop a solution aligned with its objectives.

  • PS01: Agentic Workflow Automation
    • Build an AI agent that automates repetitive tasks by planning multi-step workflows, integrating external tools and APIs, executing actions, and verifying task completion.
  • PS02: Autonomous AI Software Engineer
    • Develop an AI agent that analyzes codebases, identifies bugs, proposes fixes, runs tests, and generates actionable reports to improve software development workflows.
  • PS03: Multi-Agent Research & Fact-Checking
    • Create a multi-agent system that researches complex topics, verifies information using reliable sources, identifies conflicting claims, and generates evidence-backed reports.
  • PS04: Personalized AI Learning Agent
    • Build an intelligent learning agent that identifies knowledge gaps, creates personalized learning paths, generates assessments, and adapts recommendations based on student progress.
  • PS05: AI Operations Agent for Businesses
    • Develop an AI agent that streamlines business operations by analyzing data, managing routine workflows, identifying exceptions, and recommending actions with appropriate human oversight.
  • PS06: AI-Powered Cybersecurity Triage
    • Create a defensive AI agent that analyzes security logs, correlates alerts, detects suspicious activities, and recommends safe remediation steps.
  • PS07: Smart Energy & Sustainability Agent
    • Build an AI agent that analyzes energy consumption data, identifies inefficiencies, predicts potential wastage, and recommends actionable sustainability improvements.
  • PS08: Startup Co-Pilot Agent
    • Develop a multi-agent system that assists early-stage founders with market research, competitor analysis, customer profiling, idea validation, and execution planning.

Competition Format

The competition will follow the official schedule and format announced by HackQube.

The proposed process includes:

  • Registration: Eligible participants register through Unstop in teams of 2–4 members.
  • Problem Statement Selection: Each team selects one official problem statement from PS01 to PS08.
  • Solution Development: Teams design and develop their solutions using appropriate technologies, APIs, frameworks, and AI tools.
  • Project Submission: Teams submit the required project details and demonstration materials before the official deadline.
  • Evaluation: Judges assess projects according to the published evaluation criteria.
  • Final Results: Winners are determined based on evaluation scores and the final decision of the judging panel.

The round-wise schedule, duration, submission deadline, and grand finale details will be communicated through official event announcements.

Project Submission Guidelines

Each team must submit the materials specified by the organizers. These may include:

  • Project title and selected problem statement.

  • Key features and explanation of the approach.
  • Working prototype or functional demonstration.
  • Source-code repository link, if required.
  • Presentation or pitch deck, if required.
  • Technology stack, APIs, frameworks, and AI tools used.
  • Explanation of the solution's feasibility, impact, and scalability.

All required submissions must be completed before the official deadline. Late or incomplete submissions may be disqualified.

Judging Criteria

Projects may be evaluated on the following parameters:

  • Innovation: Originality and creativity of the proposed solution.
  • Technical Implementation: Quality, functionality, and effective use of AI and other technologies.
  • Problem Relevance: Effectiveness in addressing the selected problem statement.
  • Feasibility and Scalability: Practical applicability and potential for further development.
  • User Experience: Usability, accessibility, and clarity of the solution.

problem_statement:
Event Overview

WebCloneMania is a web development competition designed to test participants' frontend development, debugging, and problem-solving skills. The event will feature two segments: Beginner and Advanced, allowing participants to compete based on their skill levels.

  • Beginner Segment – Website Recreation: Participants will recreate a reference website revealed by the organisers at the beginning of the competition, focusing on visual accuracy, responsiveness, and functionality.
  • Advanced Segment – Debug and Deploy: Participants will receive a pre-written codebase containing bugs, incomplete features, and backend issues. They must identify and fix the issues, implement the required functionality, and ensure the application works as intended.

Eligibility and Participation

  • Participation is individual; team formation is not permitted.
  • Students from any college are eligible to participate.
  • Participants from any academic year or specialization may participate.
  • Participants must register for the appropriate segment according to the registration instructions provided by the organisers.
  • Each participant may compete individually and must submit their own work.

Segment 1: Beginner – Website Recreation

Format

Participants will be shown a reference website on the spot and must recreate it within the allotted time.

Rules

  • The reference website will be revealed immediately before the challenge begins.
  • Participants will have approximately 3–4 hours to complete the challenge, subject to the final schedule announced by the organisers.
  • Participants may use HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Next.js, or other permitted frontend technologies.
  • AI tools, coding assistants, libraries, frameworks, and official documentation are permitted.
  • Participants must develop their own implementation during the competition. Submitting a pre-built clone or copying another participant's work is prohibited.
  • Unauthorised external assistance is not permitted.
  • The final website must be functional and accessible for evaluation.

Submission Requirements

Each participant must submit:

  • Source Code: A GitHub repository containing the complete project.
  • Live Website: A deployed website link or clear instructions to run the project locally.
  • Demonstration Video: A short video demonstrating the completed website.
  • Participant Details: Name, registration details, and other information requested by the organisers.

All submissions must be completed before the announced deadline.

Segment 2: Advanced – Debug and Deploy

Format

Participants will receive an existing codebase containing intentional bugs, broken functionality, incomplete implementations, or backend integration issues. Their task is to analyse the code, identify the problems, implement the required fixes, and make the application work correctly.

Rules

  • The starter codebase and problem statement will be provided by the organisers at the beginning of the challenge.
  • Participants will have approximately 3–4 hours to debug, implement, test, and demonstrate their solutions.
  • The codebase may include frontend, backend, database, API integration, authentication, or other web application components.
  • Participants must identify and fix the issues in the provided code rather than replace the entire project with an unrelated implementation.
  • Participants may use permitted programming languages, frameworks, debugging tools, AI coding assistants, and official documentation.
  • Participants must understand and be able to explain their changes during evaluation.
  • Unauthorised external assistance, copying another participant's solution, or sharing solutions during the competition is prohibited.
  • The final application must run successfully and satisfy the requirements specified in the problem statement.
  • Participants must submit their corrected codebase and demonstrate the working application before the deadline.

Submission Requirements

Each participant must submit:

  • Source Code: A GitHub repository containing the corrected project.
  • Working Application: A live deployment, where feasible, or a locally running application for evaluation.
  • Demonstration: A short video or live demonstration showing the fixes and working features.
  • Participant Details: Name, registration details, and other information requested by the organisers.

Evaluation Criteria

Beginner Segment

  • Visual similarity to the reference website.
  • Layout, typography, colours, and styling.
  • Responsiveness across screen sizes.
  • Functional interactions and navigation.
  • Code quality and overall completeness.

Advanced Segment

  • Correct identification and resolution of bugs.
  • Successful implementation of required features.
  • Frontend–backend integration and API functionality.
  • Application stability, error handling, and testing.
  • Code quality, efficiency, and completeness.
  • Ability to explain the implemented fixes.

The organisers will announce the final scoring weights and evaluation procedure at the event.

Fair Play and Disqualification

  • Copying another participant's work or submitting someone else's implementation is prohibited.
  • Unauthorised collaboration or external assistance is not allowed.
  • Participants must not interfere with another participant's system, code, or submission.
  • Misrepresenting work or exploiting the evaluation process may result in disqualification.
  • The organisers reserve the right to disqualify participants who violate the rules.

General Instructions

  • Participants must bring their own laptops and ensure their development environments are ready.
  • Participants should arrive at the venue before the scheduled start time.
  • Internet access will be provided subject to availability.
  • The organisers will communicate the exact timings, problem statements, submission links, and scoring weights before the competition begins.
  • All decisions made by the organising team regarding the conduct and evaluation of the event will be final.

title: Agents that act. Systems that answer. | Free Virtual Agentic-AI Hackathon
problem_statement:
About the Hackathon:

Anyone can build an AI demo that works once. Agents that act. Systems that answer. is about what happens when it goes wrong. It's a free, 3-day virtual hackathon for student builders, hosted by StudentChakra and co-hosted by Priyanshu Agarwal (founder of NextMove, organiser of Hackorizon).

What You'll Build:

An agentic AI system for a real person with a real task. Start with a person, not an industry: who are they, what do they hate doing, what does your agent do for them, and where does it break? Solo or in a team of up to 4. No experience required.

How Projects Are Judged:

We judge how your project behaves when things go wrong:

  • Failure modes: how does it break?
  • Human oversight: who stays in the loop?
  • Intervention: can someone stop it?
  • Reversibility: can a mistake be undone?

Plus usefulness to a real person and the quality of your working build.

Prizes:

$680 in prizes: 1st place about $500 in Apify credits; 2nd and 3rd place Cursor subscriptions.

Judges:

Experts from AI governance, cybersecurity, venture and OpenAI, including Dr. Esona Fomuso (formerly VP of Technology, JPMorgan Chase), Dr. Aleem Khalid Alvi (Professor of Cybersecurity & Software Engineering, Sheridan College), Kunal Kapoor (Venture Continuity, Katha) and Priyanshu Agarwal (ChatGPT Lab, OpenAI India).

Key Dates:

  • Registration closes: Nov 27
  • Hackathon: Nov 28–30 (virtual)
  • Final results: Dec 8

Who Can Join:

Students worldwide, solo or in teams of 1–4. Free.

More than just a competition, HackNova is a launchpad for India's future innovators, connecting talented individuals from across the country to learn, collaborate, innovate, and shape the future through technology.

Solve Real-World Problems
Work on meaningful challenges that address real issues affecting society, industry, and the environment.

Promote Social and Environmental Sustainability
Embrace the principle of "Real Problems, Real Solutions" by developing innovative approaches that support healthy, sustainable, and thriving communities.

Collaborate Nationwide
Connect with innovators from across India, build diverse teams, exchange ideas, and expand your professional network.

Event Description

Compete in a timed competitive programming challenge by solving a set of algorithmic problems of increasing difficulty. Submissions are evaluated automatically for correctness, and the leaderboard is ranked based on problems solved and total time, including penalties for incorrect submissions. Problems will cover arrays, strings, sorting, greedy algorithms, graphs, and dynamic programming.

Guidelines

  • Eligibility: Open to students from any college.
  • Participation Format: Individual participation only. Team participation is not permitted.
  • College ID: Participants must carry a valid college ID card for verification.
  • Programming Languages: C, C++, Java, and Python are supported on the judging platform.
  • Problem Statements: Participants will solve algorithmic problems of varying difficulty, covering arrays, strings, sorting, greedy algorithms, graphs, and dynamic programming.
  • Duration: The contest will run for a fixed duration announced by the organizers.
  • Evaluation: All submissions will be judged automatically on predefined test cases.
  • Leaderboard: Rankings will be determined by the number of problems solved, followed by total time, including penalties for incorrect submissions.
  • Requirements: Participants must bring their own laptop and charger.

Rules

  1. Supported Languages: Only C, C++, Java, and Python are permitted for submissions.
  2. Scoring: Participants will be ranked by the number of problems solved. Ties will be broken using total time, including penalties for incorrect submissions.
  3. Fair Play: Collaboration, the use of AI assistants, and any form of outside help during the contest are strictly prohibited.
  4. Plagiarism: Copying solutions or submitting plagiarized code will result in disqualification.
  5. Independent Participation: Each participant must solve the problems independently and submit their own solutions.
  6. Submission Deadline: All solutions must be submitted within the allotted contest duration. Late submissions will not be accepted.
  7. Final Decisions: Decisions made by the organizers regarding judging, scoring, disputes, and disqualification will be final.

title: Haven Ahmedabad
problem_statement:
About the Event

  • Welcome to Haven Ahmedabad, a beginner-friendly, 24-hour problem-solving game jam tailored specifically for high school students. Scheduled for November 14th to 15th, this event invites programmers, artists, and engineers to spend 24 immersive hours together building fun computer games.
  • Following in the footsteps of major gatherings like Daydream and Campfire Ahmedabad (which was hosted at Ahmedabad University on February 28, 2026, as part of Hack Club's worldwide network of 100 concurrent events and 7,000 attendees), Haven brings the vibrant energy of global hackathons right to your doorstep. Organized under Hack Club—a 501(c)(3) nonprofit empowering over 50,000 teenagers worldwide to code—this is your space to innovate, create, and collaborate.

Our Mission

  • Our mission is to inspire the next generation of makers across Gujarat and beyond by introducing you to game development in a fun, collaborative, and low-stakes environment. Working in teams, you will tackle exciting challenges and build incredible projects that enhance your creativity, collaboration, and innovation skills. For us, hacking is all about problem-solving, making cool projects, and forging lifelong friendships with fellow coders, makers, and artists. Whether you are writing your first line of code or designing your next masterpiece, Haven is designed to help you discover the joy of creating.

Why Ahmedabad?

  • Ahmedabad is the ultimate home for Haven. As India's first UNESCO World Heritage City and home to world-class institutions like IIT Gandhinagar, CEPT, and NID, the city has always been a buzzing hub of innovation, entrepreneurship, and creativity. Rooted in the local spirit of jugaad (innovative problem-solving) and collaboration—from our historic textile mills to today's thriving startup ecosystem—young makers across neighborhoods from Navrangpura and Satellite to Maninagar and Vastrapur are brimming with potential. Haven Ahmedabad brings together young creators from all over to learn, build, and grow together.

What to Expect

  • Beginner-Friendly Atmosphere: No prior game jam experience? No problem! Dive into coding and design in a supportive, low-stakes environment.
  • 24 Hours of Creation: Spend an intense, fun-filled day and night building games, learning from peers, and bringing your ideas to life.
  • Community & Mentorship: Connect with fellow high school coders, artists, and engineers, draw inspiration from your peers, and build lasting friendships.

Requirements

  • Demographics: The event is open to high school students (almost all under 18) who are excited to code.
  • Technology: Attendees need to bring their own devices and setup to code, with Wi-Fi and power outlets provided at the venue to support participants.
  • Safety & Permissions: Attendees must follow the official Code of Conduct. Leaving the premises is restricted except during designated, parent-approved outdoor activities with the appropriate parental waiver signed.

Join us, build something amazing, and help shape the future of tech in Ahmedabad!

title: Drone Soccer | TECHKRITI | IIT KANPUR
problem_statement:
Rules & Guidelines:

  • Team Structure:
    • Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 5 members.
    • Cross-college teams are allowed—participants from different institutions can team up.
  • Model Regulations:
    • Each team must use its own custom-built or custom-configured drone wrapped in a protective cage/exoskeleton; exchanging models or components between teams during match rounds is strictly prohibited.
    • Standard RTF (Ready-To-Fly) commercial consumer drones are not allowed, though pre-programmed flight controllers and stabilization boards are permitted.
    • Only one main drone model can be used throughout all competition rounds.
  • Flight and Conduct Rules:
    • No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams will receive a 2-minute warm-up/trial period before Round 2 matches.
    • Lifting or repositioning the drone manually during active gameplay is strictly prohibited.
    • A drone that crashes and is unable to take off within the allotted restart window immediately forfeits that specific attempt or round.
    • The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on all match rules, scoring disputes, and safety calls.

Event Structure:

Round 1: Drone Soccer Arena Showdown:

  • Obstacle & Defender Navigation: Teams must pilot their caged drones through an active arena featuring physical obstacles and designated opponent defense zones.
  • Goal Scoring Task:
    • Teams must navigate their drone past defensive barricades and maneuver it cleanly through the elevated circular Goal Ring to score points.
    • Each successful goal scored within the match time earns points based on precision and execution.
    • If a goal attempt fails, misses, or bounces off the goal frame, no points are awarded, but no negative penalty is incurred. Teams can immediately reset and attempt another run.
  • Match Execution: Matches are conducted in timed sprints where agility, mid-air defense, collision recovery, and scoring accuracy determine the final winners.

problem_statement:

    • Each team must consist of a minimum of 2 and a maximum of 6 members.

    • Each team must have its own custom-built drone; exchanging models between teams is strictly prohibited.
    • RTF (Ready-To-Fly) models are not allowed, but pre-programmed boards can be used.
    • Only one model can be used throughout all competition rounds.
  • Flight and Conduct Rules:
    • No trial attempts are allowed in Round 1, but teams can have a 2-minute trial before Round 2.
    • Lifting the drone manually to improve position during any round is not allowed.
    • Any failed landing attempt that does not result in a score immediately ends the round.
    • The competition organizers and judges hold the final decision on any disputes.

Event Structure:

Round 1:

  • Teams must fly their drone through 5 circular rings placed at varying heights (between 1 meter to 2.5 meters).
  • Each ring carries different points based on difficulty.

title: Pixels To Prognosis
problem_statement:
About the Event

Gliomas are among the most aggressive brain tumours, and outlining them accurately on MRI is central to diagnosis, surgical planning and treatment monitoring. Doing it by hand is slow, and different radiologists often draw the boundaries differently.

Pixels to Prognosis asks you to build an AI system that does this automatically. Using multimodal brain MRI scans, your model has to locate a glioma and separate it into its three subregions: active (enhancing) tumour, necrotic core, and surrounding edema.

The event combines neuroscience, MRI physics and computer vision. You’ll need more than a model with a good leaderboard score. You’ll also need to understand what the scans show, why models fail, and how to make one that holds up on real clinical data.

Who Can Participate

  • Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from any college and any stream
  • Especially suited to students in Biotechnology & Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, and AI & Data Science
  • Teams of 1 to 3 members. Cross-disciplinary teams are encouraged.

Competition Structure

Round 1: Online Quiz (Screening)

This is a case-based quiz on:

  • How MRI machines work and the basics of MRI imaging
  • The biology of brain gliomas and how they appear on MRI scans
  • Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Image Processing

The questions reward reasoning over memorisation. The quiz is meant to sharpen your problem-solving for the later rounds.

Round 2: Model Submission Round

Shortlisted teams train a segmentation model on a curated glioma dataset we provide, [derived from the BraTS 2021 challenge]. Each patient has four MRI modalities: T1-weighted, post-contrast T1-weighted (T1ce), T2-weighted and T2-FLAIR.

Your model must segment three regions: Whole Tumour, Tumour Core and Enhancing Tumour. Models are ranked on a hidden patient-level test set.

Rules:

  • Train only on the dataset provided. No external data.
  • All learnable parameters must start from random initialisation. Pretrained weights are not allowed. You may use published architectures such as U-Net variants.
  • The Colab notebook runtime must be 9 hours or less.

Submission requirements:

  • Complete source code (.py / .ipynb)
  • Final trained weights (.pt / .keras)
  • Training logs, including loss and validation curves, config and seed used (.csv)
  • A technical report (.pdf) covering your thought process, pipeline, architecture details and the compute you used

Evaluation: Segmentation quality is measured with the Dice score and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance for each tumour region. Scoring also covers anatomical consistency, false-positive control, and the quality of your technical report.

Finals: Offline Round at IIT Madras

Finalists come to campus and receive a new set of MRI scans with real-world problems. These can include motion artefacts, missing modalities, or pathologies your model has never seen.

Each team must:

  • Work out what is wrong with the data and why it happened
  • Adapt the model through preprocessing, retraining or other corrective strategies
  • Present the problems they found, the medical reasoning behind them, and how they handled them

Evaluation criteria:

  • Problem identification and medical reasoning
  • Model adaptation strategy and outcome
  • Clarity of presentation and understanding

Knowing when your model should not be trusted counts in your favour. Flagging an unreliable case for expert review is part of good clinical AI.

Prizes & Recognition

  • Cash prizes for the top 3 teams [prize pool: ₹35000]
  • Special Awards for Best Robust Model and Best Diagnostic Reasoning
  • Certificates of Merit for the winners(Hard Copy)
  • Certificates of Merit for all finalists(Soft Copy)
  • Certificates of Participation for all Round 2 participants

Important Dates

  • Round 1 (Online Quiz): 5th December, 2026
  • Round 2 submission window: 9th - 16th December, 2026
  • Finals at IIT Madras: 4th January, 2027

Selected teams will advance to Round 1.

Qualified teams must navigate a specially designed obstacle course while maintaining stable, low-altitude flight.
The course includes:

  • Semicircular and quarter hoops.
  • Diagonal split rectangular hoops.
  • Sharp 90° turns.
  • Double quarter hoops.
  • Crossover and split semicircular hoops.
  • Triangular and freely hanging circular hoops.
  • T-rod obstacles.

Teams must complete the obstacle sequence, cross the finish line, and land at the designated point.
Scoring is based on course completion, time bonuses, and penalties for rule violations.

Round 2: Checkpoints Challenge
The top-performing teams from Round 1 will qualify for this timed challenge.

  • Reach as many checkpoints as possible within the allotted time.
  • Follow the obstacle-course rules applicable to Round 1.
  • Earn 10 points for each successful checkpoint.
  • Avoid unnecessary contacts and unsafe manoeuvres.
  • The number of qualifying teams will be determined by the organisers based on participation.

Teams will carry an organiser-provided payload through the obstacle course and release it onto a marked target area. Scoring would consider course completion, delivery accuracy, time bonuses, and penalties.

Rules and Regulations:

  • Drone type: Only multirotor drones, such as quadcopters and hexacopters, are permitted.
  • Control system: Drones must be operated manually using a remote controller. Autonomous flight is not permitted.3. Dimensions: The drone must not exceed 1 metre and must not be smaller than 0.3 metre in any direction.
  • Flight altitude: Drones must not exceed a height of 1.5 metres and must follow the prescribed arena boundaries and safety-net restrictions.
  • Flight performance: Drones must demonstrate stable hovering, precise low-altitude flight, and controlled manoeuvrability.
  • Obstacle contact: Contact with hoops, rods, will attract penalties.

  • Clearly marked start and finish points will be provided.
  • Obstacle dimensions and placements will have a tolerance of ±5%.

Students, robotics enthusiasts, and teams interested in drone technology, aerial robotics, and engineering innovation are encouraged to participate, subject to the final eligibility criteria announced by the organisers. Participants must ensure that their drones comply with the technical specifications and safety requirements.

Scoring and Evaluation:

Qualification Process

Every participant must demonstrate basic familiarity with the AeglysAI project before selection.

The qualification process involves:

  • Registering individually through the official form.
  • Forking the official AeglysAI repository into a personal GitHub account.
  • Cloning the fork and demonstrating that the baseline builds or runs.
  • Documenting the basic architecture and request/decision flow.
  • Providing one meaningful technical observation, one realistic improvement idea, and a proposed validation approach.
  • Submitting the required GitHub links and sanitised build evidence for organiser review.

Completing qualification does not guarantee selection.

Competition Format and Rounds

Round 1 — Technical Screening

Participants submit a working project, source code, a README with setup instructions, testing or validation evidence, and a demonstration video of no more than two minutes. Reviewers evaluate the solution's functionality, intelligent features, relevance, reproducibility, and video clarity.

Round 2 — Finalist Demonstration

Shortlisted finalists present their working projects live through Google Meet. Each finalist receives five minutes for the demonstration, followed by five minutes of technical questions and answers.

Round 2 determines the final ranking. The two rounds are scored separately.

Judging Criteria

Round 1 — 100 points

  • Working functionality: 30 points
  • AI/ML or intelligent feature: 25 points
  • Relevance and creativity: 20 points
  • Reproducibility: 15 points
  • Video clarity: 10 points

Round 2 — 100 points

  • Live demonstration: 35 points
  • Technical understanding: 25 points
  • Solution quality and safety: 20 points
  • Technical Q&A: 15 points
  • Presentation: 5 points

Final Project Submission Requirements

Each team must submit:

  • Team ID and selected challenge
  • Public GitHub source repository and a fixed review commit or tag
  • Project README and reproducible setup instructions
  • Demonstration video of up to two minutes
  • Explanation of the AI/ML or intelligent technique used
  • Testing or validation evidence
  • Data and model attribution, licensing information, and known limitations

A slide deck or walkthrough alone is not sufficient. The submission must be a working minimum viable product (MVP), executable prototype, or functional proof of concept. Any programming language or framework may be used.

Competition Rules

  • Participation is free; no registration fee is required.
  • Every participant must complete individual qualification and selection before competing.
  • Teams must follow the approved roster and team ID requirements.
  • Projects must address the selected challenge and demonstrate functional, testable behaviour.
  • Participants must submit original work or properly attribute third-party code, data, models, and other resources.

  • Use only systems and data you are authorised to access. Security testing against unauthorised real systems is prohibited.
  • Do not include passwords, credentials, personal information, confidential material, or patent-related private data in public submissions.
  • Participants must treat others respectfully, avoid harassment or discrimination, and credit collaborators and prior work.
  • Judges must disclose conflicts of interest and recuse themselves where appropriate.
  • Team changes, roster changes, and other exceptions require organiser approval.
  • Final rankings are determined after Round 2 judging and organiser review. Qualification or registration alone does not guarantee selection, finalist status, a certificate, or an award.

Timeline and Important Information

The organisers should publish the confirmed registration deadline, qualification deadline, project-submission deadline, finalist announcement, and final event date before this listing is approved.

title: Build 2 Rise 2026
problem_statement:
Overview

Krixov presents: AI for Operational Intelligence Case Challenge

Build Real. Showcase Skills. Unlock Opportunities.

About the Challenge:

BUILD2RISE 2026 is an online, idea-based case challenge organized by Krixov. It invites college and university students to analyze real-world operational challenges and propose innovative, practical, data-informed, and responsible AI-enabled solutions.

Participants will select one problem statement, analyze its root causes, define the intended users, design a feasible solution, and present their idea through a structured presentation. The challenge focuses on problem-solving, analytical thinking, product innovation, data-driven decision-making, and responsible use of AI.

Whether your strengths are technology, business, analytics, design, operations, research, or communication, this is an opportunity to showcase your thinking and present an idea with real-world potential.

Event Overview:

  • Event name: BUILD2RISE 2026
  • Theme: AI for Operational Intelligence
  • Format: Online
  • Competition type: Idea / Case-study presentation
  • Duration: 72 hours (3 days)
  • Problem statements: 6
  • Participation: Individual or team
  • Team size: 1–4 members
  • Eligibility: Currently enrolled college/university students from any discipline and academic year
  • Submission format: PDF or PowerPoint presentation
  • Rounds: One submission and evaluation round
  • Registration deadline: 15-11-2026 (11:59 PM)
  • Challenge start: 16-11-2026 (12:01 AM)
  • Submission deadline: 18-11-2026 (11:59 PM)
  • Organizer contact: campus@krixov.com

Rewards and Recognition:

BUILD2RISE 2026 is designed to help students showcase their ideas, strengthen their portfolios, and explore potential career opportunities.

1st and 2nd Place — Top 2 Teams:

  • Internship opportunities
  • Consideration for professional recommendations
  • Winner recognition
  • Opportunity to showcase projects and solutions

3rd, 4th, and 5th Place — Next 3 Teams:

  • Consideration for professional recommendations
  • Recognition among the top-performing teams
  • Opportunity to showcase projects and solutions

Other Eligible Participating Teams:

- Digital Certificate of Participation for eligible teams that complete the required participation and submission process.

Important Reward Terms: Internship opportunities and professional recommendations are subject to eligibility, evaluation, availability, and the organizer’s applicable selection process. They are opportunities for consideration, not a guarantee of an internship, employment, or recommendation. No cash prize is being advertised in this listing.

Problem Statements:

Participants must select exactly one of the following six problem statements.

Problem Statement 1: The Broken Handoff Problem

Problem:

Work is often delayed when tasks move between departments or team members without complete information, clear ownership, or a defined next action.

Challenge:

Design a solution that identifies incomplete handoffs, detects missing information, prioritizes tasks at risk of delay, and recommends actions to improve coordination.

Expected solution:

A workflow-management concept, intelligent checklist, handoff-risk dashboard, or another practical solution.

Success measures:

Reduced incomplete handoffs, less rework, clearer ownership, and shorter resolution time.

Problem Statement 2: The Invisible Cost Detector

Problem:

Businesses may overlook avoidable operational costs caused by repeated work, unused software licenses, duplicate purchases, and recurring delays.

Challenge:

Propose a transparent system that identifies potential waste, ranks opportunities for investigation, and estimates possible savings using clear calculations.

Expected solution:

A cost-intelligence dashboard, expense-analysis system, duplicate-purchase alert, or related concept.

Success measures:

Better visibility into cost drivers, more reliable identification of potential waste, and transparent savings estimates.

Important requirement:

Participants must distinguish confirmed waste from uncertain opportunities. Estimated savings must not be presented as guaranteed savings.

Problem Statement 3: Trust Before Automation

Problem:

AI systems may generate misleading answers when they use outdated documents, conflicting policies, or unverified information.

Challenge:

Design an AI-assisted system that answers questions using approved documents, provides source citations, detects conflicting information, and escalates uncertain cases to a human reviewer.

Expected solution:

A source-grounded AI assistant, policy-verification workflow, or document-conflict detection system.

Success measures:

Higher factual accuracy, appropriate source coverage, reliable conflict detection, and responsible handling of uncertainty.

Important requirement:

The proposed system must not invent policy rules or present unsupported answers as verified facts.

Problem Statement 4: Material Shortage Decision Support

Problem:

Shortages of essential materials can disrupt business operations when inventory levels, demand forecasts, safety stock, and supplier lead times are not considered together.

Challenge:

Design a decision-support solution that identifies materials at risk of shortage, estimates when stock may run low, and recommends suitable actions based on available information.

Expected solution:

An inventory-risk dashboard, reorder recommendation tool, shortage-warning system, or supply-planning concept.

Success measures:

Earlier shortage warnings, better-prioritized purchasing decisions, and fewer avoidable stockouts.

Important requirement:

Participants should explain the assumptions behind forecasts and recommendations rather than treating predictions as certain.

Problem Statement 5: Quality Intelligence System

Problem:

Unusual production patterns may indicate an increased risk of defects, but quality teams may struggle to identify which production batches require further investigation.

Challenge:

Design a system that detects unusual patterns in production data, flags potentially high-risk batches, and recommends evidence-based investigation steps.

Expected solution:

A quality-monitoring dashboard, anomaly-detection concept, or batch-risk prioritization system.

Success measures:

Earlier identification of unusual patterns, faster investigations, and improved prioritization of quality checks.

Important requirement:

The solution must distinguish unusual patterns from confirmed defects and must not assign blame without supporting evidence.

Problem Statement 6: Customer Operations Intelligence

Problem:

Unusual patterns in product returns and warranty claims may indicate recurring customer issues, product defects, or operational weaknesses.

Challenge:

Design an analytics solution that identifies meaningful patterns, estimates potential business impact, and prioritizes corrective actions.

Expected solution:

A customer-operations dashboard, returns-analysis system, warranty-trend monitor, or customer-issue prioritization tool.

Success measures:

Improved visibility into recurring issues, better prioritization of investigations, and more informed corrective-action decisions.

Important requirement:

Participants should explain the evidence behind their findings and avoid treating correlations as proof of causation.

Eligibility and Participation:

  • The challenge is open to currently enrolled college or university students from any discipline and academic year.
  • Beginners, intermediate participants, and advanced participants are welcome.
  • Participants may register individually or in teams of 1–4 members.
  • Inter-college, inter-specialization, and interdisciplinary teams are allowed.
  • Team members may belong to different academic streams, branches, or specializations.
  • Each individual or team must select exactly one of the six problem statements.
  • Participation and submission will take place online through the designated event process.
  • Each individual or team must submit one final presentation for its selected problem statement.
  • Participants are responsible for ensuring that registration details, team details, and submissions are accurate and complete.
  • A participant may be part of only one team and may submit only one final presentation.

Submission Requirements:

Submit one PDF or PowerPoint presentation containing approximately 6 - slides.

Your presentation should cover:

  • Problem understanding — Define the problem, its root causes, affected users, and current workflow.
  • Proposed solution — Explain your idea and how it addresses the selected problem.
  • Data and assumptions — Present relevant evidence, sample data, or clearly stated assumptions.
  • Workflow or system design — Include a flowchart, solution architecture, sample dashboard, interface mock-up, or illustrative output where appropriate.
  • Feasibility — Explain how the solution could be implemented, including the proposed technical or analytical approach.
  • Impact — Identify expected benefits and define measurable success indicators.
  • Risks and limitations — Address uncertainty, data quality, privacy, bias, responsible AI, implementation risks, or other relevant safeguards.
  • Implementation roadmap — Outline the next steps required to develop, test, and evaluate the solution.
  • References and contributions — Acknowledge relevant sources and explain each team member’s contribution.

No working code, live deployment, or functioning prototype is required. Judges will evaluate the quality of the idea, reasoning, feasibility, evidence, originality, responsible design, and expected impact.

Participants may use organizer-provided resources, publicly available references, or clearly identified assumptions where appropriate. Any external data, assumptions, images, frameworks, and references must be properly cited.

No confidential, personal, or proprietary company data may be used in any submission.

Judging Criteria:

All submissions will be evaluated using a common 100-point rubric.

  • Problem understanding and relevance: 20 points
  • Solution clarity and user workflow: 20 points
  • Feasibility and technical/analytical approach: 20 points
  • Evidence, dataset use, and reasoning: 15 points
  • Measurable impact and evaluation plan: 10 points
  • Originality and differentiation: 10 points
  • Presentation quality and responsible design: 5 points
  • Total: 100 points

Judges will consider the practicality of the proposed solution, clarity of reasoning, quality of evidence, originality, responsible use of AI, and potential real-world impact. Coding complexity is not required and will not be a prerequisite for evaluation.

Rules and Guidelines:

  • Participants must select one problem statement from the six available challenges.
  • All submissions must be original and prepared specifically for this competition.
  • Plagiarism, copied presentations, and misrepresentation of another person’s work are not permitted.
  • External references, datasets, images, frameworks, and other third-party assets must be appropriately acknowledged.
  • Participants must disclose material use of AI tools and remain responsible for the accuracy, originality, and quality of their submissions.
  • Do not include personal, confidential, or proprietary company information in any submission.
  • Any estimates, forecasts, assumptions, and claims must be explained and supported wherever possible.
  • Submissions must follow the specified presentation format and be uploaded before the official deadline.
  • Incomplete or late submissions may be disqualified in accordance with the organizer’s announced rules.
  • Participants are responsible for entering correct registration and team information.
  • Internship opportunities and professional recommendations, where offered, are subject to the stated eligibility and selection conditions. They are not guaranteed outcomes.
  • Any updates or clarifications will be communicated through the official event channel.
  • The organizer’s published event rules and evaluation process will govern participation and judging.

Why Participate?

BUILD2RISE 2026 is an opportunity to:

  • Showcase your problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Explore practical applications of technology, AI, and business intelligence.
  • Strengthen your project portfolio through a structured solution proposal.
  • Collaborate with students from different colleges and specializations.
  • Earn recognition for strong ideas and presentations.
  • Be considered for the internship and professional recommendation opportunities described above, subject to applicable conditions.
  • Receive a digital certificate of participation if you meet the eligibility and submission requirements.

Whether your strength is technology, data analysis, business, design, operations, or research, you can contribute to developing a meaningful solution.

Your Ideas. Your Skills. Your Next Opportunity.

BUILD2RISE 2026 — Build Real. Showcase Skills. Unlock Opportunities.

problem_statement:
Link: https://bharatcode.ai/hackathon#register

Join the WhatsApp group for details: https://chat.whatsapp.com/EMNvrZuuZc75sAZ3GVEgDB

Turn Your Idea into a Working Product

The BharatCode Build League is a hackathon for students, developers, and anyone interested in building useful products with artificial intelligence.

The goal is simple. Find a problem worth solving and build something that addresses it. You can create an application, an artificial intelligence agent, a chatbot, a developer tool, an automation system, or any other product that you think would be useful.

You can participate individually or as part of a small team. We welcome projects across different fields and encourage participants to experiment with new ideas.

Prizes and Opportunities:

Cash Prize:

  • The winner will receive ₹10,000 in prize money.

Software Development Internship Opportunity

The winner will also get an opportunity to interview for a paid software development internship offering a stipend of ₹60,000 per month for three months.

The total stipend for the internship is ₹1,80,000. However, winning the hackathon does not guarantee the internship. The candidate must clear a separate interview and selection process to be considered for the position.

Additional Benefits:

Participants can also benefit from the following opportunities, subject to the applicable terms:

  • One thousand GC.
  • Three complimentary Ginhouse event tickets.
  • An opportunity to showcase their projects to the BharatCode team and community.
  • Consideration for developing selected projects into official BharatCode offerings.
  • Free access to BharatCode for eligible students, subject to usage limits.
  • A discount on Ginclair learning paths.

What Can You Build?

You are free to choose the problem you want to solve. Here are a few areas to get you started.

  • Education and learning: Build tools that help students understand difficult concepts, practise questions, or learn at their own pace.
  • Research and information: Create applications that help people find information, analyse data, or organise their research.
  • Productivity and automation: Develop tools that simplify repetitive tasks, manage documents, or make everyday work more efficient.
  • Software development: Build coding assistants, debugging tools, or applications that help developers work more effectively.
  • Artificial intelligence agents: Create agents that can use tools, process information, and complete useful tasks.
  • Chatbots and assistants: Develop conversational applications for websites, businesses, or online communities.

These are only suggestions. You can work on any other idea as long as your project demonstrates a useful application of artificial intelligence.

How to Participate:

Step 1: Register

  • Register for the event. You can participate individually or with a small team.

Step 2: Choose Your Idea

  • Identify a problem you want to solve and decide what you want to build. You can choose from the suggested categories or work on an idea of your own.

Step 3: Build Your Project

  • Use the BharatCode model application programming interface to develop your project. You can build a website, an application, a chatbot, a developer tool, or another type of product.
  • We encourage participants to focus on building something functional that solves a real problem rather than creating a basic demonstration with little practical value.

Step 4: Publish Your Code

  • Upload your source code to a public GitHub repository. The repository must contain a file named BharatCode.txt in its root directory.

Step 5: Submit Your Project

  • Submit the main GitHub repository link through the official event page. Include your project name and a short description of what it does.

Step 6: Get Your Project Evaluated

  • Projects will be assessed using community interest and the judges' evaluation. GitHub stars and votes submitted through the BharatCode website are among the factors considered.

Who Can Participate?

  • The event is open to college students, software developers, artificial intelligence enthusiasts, aspiring founders, and independent builders.
  • You do not need to be an expert to participate. What matters is your ability to identify a problem, develop a solution, and demonstrate what you have built.

Important Date:

  • The application deadline is 10 November 2026 at 11:59 PM Indian Standard Time.
  • Please check the official event page for the latest participation rules and submission requirements.

Get Started:

If you have an idea that could solve a real problem, this is an opportunity to put it into practice.

Build your project, share your work, and compete for ₹10,000 in prize money and an opportunity to interview for a paid software development internship.

We look forward to seeing what you build.
