title: Operation Ward Zero
problem_statement:
Build a Hospital That Fits Inside a Bedroom

About the Hackathon:

What if a patient's bedroom could function like a smart hospital ward?

Hospitals have monitoring systems, trained healthcare professionals, and alert mechanisms to detect changes in patient conditions. At home, however, patients often depend on family members and caregivers who may not have access to continuous monitoring or early-warning systems.

Operation Ward Zero is an online healthcare technology hackathon inviting innovators, developers, and problem-solvers to design intelligent home healthcare solutions.

Participants will develop a working prototype demonstrating how IoT simulation, full-stack applications, and AI/ML can work together to monitor patient conditions, identify potential risks, and support timely caregiver responses.

The central mission is:

Sense → Understand → Predict → Alert → Respond

Participants are encouraged to develop practical, affordable, scalable, and user-friendly solutions that address real-world home healthcare challenges.

No physical hardware is required. Participants may use simulated sensors, synthetic patient data, mock devices, and software-based environments.

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Open to students, recent graduates, aspiring developers, and technology enthusiasts interested in healthcare innovation.
  • Participants from engineering, computer science, information technology, data science, artificial intelligence, and related disciplines are encouraged to participate.
  • Team Size: Minimum 2 and maximum 3 members.
  • Inter-college teams: Allowed. Participants from different colleges or institutions may form a team.
  • Inter-specialization teams: Allowed. Participants from different academic branches, specializations, or technical backgrounds may collaborate.
  • Each participant may belong to only one team.
  • Each team must nominate one team leader responsible for registration, coordination, and final submission.
  • Participants should possess basic technical knowledge relevant to their chosen solution.

Competition Structure and Format:

Number of Problem Statements: 1 overarching problem statement covering IoT, Full Stack, and AI/ML.

Competition Format: Single-round project submission and evaluation.

Round 1: Prototype Development and Submission

Participants must develop and submit a working prototype addressing the official problem statement.

The submission must demonstrate how the proposed system collects or simulates patient data, processes information, identifies risks, generates alerts, and enables caregiver responses.

Submission Deadline: 24 October 2026

Participants must submit their solution through the official Wooble challenge page.

Round 2: Evaluation and Results:

All eligible submissions will be evaluated by the designated reviewers based on predefined technical and practical evaluation criteria.

There is no separate live presentation or physical evaluation round specified.

Results Announcement: 31 October 2026

Winners will be selected based on their overall evaluation scores and compliance with the competition guidelines.

Problem Statement:

Build an Intelligent Home Healthcare Monitoring and Response System

Design and develop a software-based healthcare monitoring solution that demonstrates how a patient's home can operate like a small, intelligent hospital ward.

The proposed solution should illustrate the following workflow:

Patient Data → Monitoring Platform → Risk Assessment → Alert Generation → Caregiver Response

Participants may address one or more of the following challenges:

  • Patient Monitoring: Simulate and monitor patient vitals such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, and temperature.
  • Caregiver Monitoring: Develop mechanisms to track caregiver attendance, activity, and response to alerts.
  • System Reliability: Demonstrate how the system handles connectivity interruptions, delayed data transmission, or temporary service failures.
  • Contextual Intelligence: Combine patient vitals, historical information, and caregiver notes to support risk assessment.
  • Predictive Analytics: Explore AI/ML techniques to identify possible patient deterioration 24–48 hours in advance.
  • Alert and Escalation: Develop a system that categorizes risks and notifies the appropriate caregiver or responsible person.

Participants are not required to build a production-ready medical device or clinically validated diagnostic system.

The objective is to demonstrate technical capabilities, problem-solving skills, integration, and practical thinking through a functional prototype.

 Technical Tracks:

Participants may contribute through one or more of the following technical areas:

IoT Development:

  • Simulated sensors and patient monitoring devices.
  • Collection and transmission of patient data.
  • Device communication and monitoring workflows.

Full Stack Development:

  • Patient monitoring dashboards.
  • Data visualization and application interfaces.
  • Caregiver alert and acknowledgment systems.
  • Backend services, databases, and APIs.

AI/ML Engineering:

  • Patient risk classification.
  • Identification of unusual patterns.
  • Analysis of patient context and caregiver notes.
  • Explainable risk predictions and alerts.

Teams are encouraged to demonstrate end-to-end integration, but participants are not expected to be experts in every technical domain.

Mandatory Submission Requirements:

Each team must submit the following deliverables:

A. Working Prototype:

A functional demonstration showing patient data collection or simulation, platform processing, risk detection, alert generation, and caregiver acknowledgment.

B. Source Code Repository:

A GitHub or GitLab repository containing:

  • Source code.
  • README documentation.
  • Installation and setup instructions.
  • Required dependencies and configurations.
  • Sample or synthetic datasets, where applicable.

C. Technical Documentation:

A document explaining:

  • Problem understanding and proposed solution.
  • System architecture and technology stack.
  • Major features and functionality.
  • Data processing and risk assessment approach.
  • Assumptions, limitations, and future improvements.

D. Demonstration Video:

A video of approximately 3 minutes, demonstrating the complete workflow:

Sensor Simulation → Platform → AI Risk Detection → Alert → Caregiver Response.

Important: Physical hardware is not mandatory. Software simulators, mock sensors, and synthetic datasets are permitted.

Evaluation Criteria:

Submissions will be evaluated using the following weighted criteria:

Evaluation Parameter Weightage
End-to-End Integration 25%
Technical Skills 20%
Reliability & Resilience 20%
Practical Implementation 20%
Explainability & Clinical Safety 15%
Total 100%

End-to-End Integration (25%): How effectively the proposed components communicate and function as a unified system.

Technical Skills (20%): Quality of implementation, architecture, programming practices, and appropriate use of technology.

Reliability & Resilience (20%): Ability to handle failures, unexpected conditions, and interruptions.

Practical Implementation (20%): Usability, feasibility, completeness, and relevance to real-world home healthcare.

Explainability & Clinical Safety (15%): Clarity of risk explanations, responsible handling of healthcare information, and avoidance of unsafe or unsupported medical claims.

Prizes and Recognition:

Total Cash Prize Pool: ₹10,000

  • 1st Position: ₹5,000
  • 2nd Position: ₹3,000
  • 3rd Position: ₹2,000

Additional Opportunities:

  • 3 internship opportunities with potential Pre-Placement Offers (PPOs), subject to selection and organizational requirements.
  • Verifiable participation certificates for eligible participants who successfully submit their work.
  • Opportunity to demonstrate technical skills to industry reviewers and the organizing company.

A PPO is not guaranteed and depends on internship performance, organizational requirements, and applicable selection criteria.

Rules and Regulations:

  • All participants must register and submit their projects through the designated official platform within the announced deadline.
  • Each team must consist of 2–3 members. A participant cannot be part of multiple teams.
  • Inter-college and interdisciplinary collaboration is permitted.
  • Each team may submit only one final solution.
  • Submissions must represent the team's own meaningful technical contribution. Existing open-source libraries, frameworks, pretrained models, and APIs may be used with appropriate acknowledgment and license compliance.
  • Plagiarism, unauthorized copying, fabricated results, or misrepresentation of functionality may result in disqualification.
  • AI-assisted development tools are permitted, provided the team understands and can explain its implementation.
  • Teams must provide accessible source code, functional demonstration material, and the required documentation.
  • Participants must not use real patient information without appropriate authorization. Synthetic or anonymized data is strongly recommended.
  • The developed solution must be treated as an experimental prototype and must not make unsupported claims about medical diagnosis, treatment, or clinical accuracy.
  • Participants are responsible for ensuring that submitted materials do not infringe third-party intellectual property rights.
  • Incomplete, inaccessible, or late submissions may be rejected.
  • Evaluation will be based on the published criteria, and the judging panel's decision will be final regarding competition rankings.
  • The organizing team may verify submissions, request clarification, or investigate suspected rule violations.
  • Participants retain ownership of their original work, subject to the licenses and rights of any third-party components they use.
  • Any changes to the competition schedule or guidelines will be communicated through official organizer channels.

Official Submission Platform:

All project submissions and challenge-related information are available on Wooble.

Challenge Link:
https://wooble.org/companies/nursio-innovation-pvt-ltd-2/challenges/operation-ward-zero

Build technology that helps caregivers respond earlier, patients feel safer, and home healthcare become smarter.

problem_statement:
Hacktopia Pune – 24-Hour Hackathon

Hacktopia Pune is a 24-hour hackathon organised by Gotham-AI, the AI and emerging-tech community at JSPM’s Rajarshi Shahu College of Engineering (RSCOE), Tathawade, Pune. It is held by the Department of Computer Science and Business Systems.

Hacktopia Pune is open to students from all colleges and disciplines. Teams will build innovative solutions, receive guidance from mentors, and pitch their work to a panel of judges.

Dates: 18–20 December 2026
Venue: JSPM’s RSCOE, Tathawade, Pune
Prize Pool: ₹1,00,000+ (cash prizes, certificates and opportunities)

Eligibility

  • Open to all UG and PG students from any college.

  • Open to all disciplines, including tech, business, design and more.

  • Team size: 2 to 5 members.

  • Inter-college teams: Allowed.

  • Inter-specialization teams: Allowed.

  • Every team must have at least one member interested in content creation. Beginners are welcome, and no prior experience is required.

Rounds

Teams will showcase their best project or innovative idea by submitting a PPT, GitHub repository, and a short video pitch explaining their solution, its key features, and implementation. The video pitch must be uploaded to YouTube, with the link included in the submission.

Having a deployed application is recommended.

The PPT template, video guidelines, submission deadline and other details will be announced soon.

Round 2 – 24-Hour Offline Hackathon (at RSCOE)

The top teams from Round 1 will be invited to the offline hackathon at RSCOE. Teams will build solutions over 24 hours based on the officially released problem statements, with mentorship and technical support, followed by presentations to the judges.

Evaluation Criteria

  • Innovation

  • Problem relevance

  • Technical implementation

  • Feasibility

  • Scalability

  • User impact

  • Presentation

  • Overall solution quality

Rules

  • Each participant can be part of only one team.

  • During Round 2, teams must work on the officially released problem statements.

  • Open-source libraries, frameworks and APIs are allowed, provided they are credited.

  • At least one team member must be present at the venue throughout the 24-hour round.

  • Participants must carry a valid college ID card to the offline round.

  • Plagiarism, copying another team’s work, or any misconduct will lead to immediate disqualification.

  • The judges’ decision will be final and binding.

  • The organisers may change the schedule, rules or format, and any updates will be posted on this page.

  • Detailed guidelines will be shared with registered teams soon.

FAQs

1. Is there an entry fee for Round 1?

No, Round 1 is free. If your team clears Round 1, the entry fee for Round 2 will be ₹250 per participant.

2. Will selected teams be notified before Round 2?

Yes, selected teams will be notified 2–3 days before Round 2.

3. Can students from different colleges form a team?

Yes, inter-college teams are allowed.

4. What is the team size?

Each team must have 2–5 members.

5. Will food and overnight rest arrangements be provided?

Yes, meals, snacks, drinking water and overnight rest arrangements will be provided during the offline event.

6. What needs to be submitted for Round 1?

Teams must submit a PPT and a GitHub repository. A deployed application is recommended.

7. When will the problem statements be released?

Round 1 is an Open Innovation round, so teams can submit their own project or idea. Official problem statements will be released for the offline Round 2.

8. Is having a content creator in the team compulsory?

Yes, every team must have at least one content creator. Special content-creation challenges and additional prizes will also be there.

9. Will technical mentors be available during the hackathon?

Yes, there will be two rounds of mentorship during the 24-hour event.

10. Where will submission links and further updates be shared?

All submission links, PPT templates, deadlines and important announcements will be shared in our official WhatsApp group. Make sure to join the group to stay updated.

11. Do I need prior content creation experience?

No! Beginners are welcome. You don't need any professional skills or prior experience.

12. Do I need a large social media following?

Not at all! You don't need to be an influencer or have thousands of followers. Anyone interested in trying content creation is welcome.

title: AI BuildFest 2026
problem_statement:
Overview

48-Hour Online AI Hackathon

Organized by Frontend Arena | In collaboration with Adaption

  • Event Dates: December 10–12, 2026
  • Format: Online
  • Duration: 48 hours
  • Team Size: 2–4 members

About AI BuildFest 2026

AI BuildFest 2026 is a 48-hour online hackathon focused on building AI-powered solutions for real-world challenges. It brings together students, developers, and AI enthusiasts to explore how custom-trained AI models can be developed and applied to practical problems.

Participants will work in teams to understand a challenge announced during the hackathon, prepare or generate a suitable dataset, train their own model using Adaption’s platform, and build a working solution that demonstrates its capabilities.

The event emphasizes practical model development, problem-solving, experimentation, and the creation of useful AI applications.

Hackathon Theme

Own Your AI: Train a Model That Solves a Real Problem

Participants will be challenged to build an AI solution in which a trained model plays a meaningful role in addressing a real-world problem.

The official problem statements and challenge requirements will be announced to registered participants during the hackathon. Teams will then have the event period to understand the challenge, develop their approach, train a model, and implement their solution.

Challenge Format

AI BuildFest will follow a challenge-based format. No specific tracks or problem statements are being published in advance.

  • Official problem statements will be revealed during the hackathon.
  • Teams will select or be assigned a challenge according to the instructions announced by the organizers.
  • The challenge will require participants to develop an AI-based solution using the Adaption platform.
  • Detailed requirements, deliverables, and submission instructions will be communicated when the challenge is announced.

Teams should be prepared to work with data, train a model, and demonstrate a functional solution within the 48-hour period.

Required Use of Adaption

Adaption is the technology partner for AI BuildFest. Teams must use Adaption’s platform as part of their model-development workflow.

Dataset Preparation or Generation

Teams will use Adaptive Data to transform raw files into a training dataset, or Invent-a-Dataset to generate a dataset suited to their challenge.

Model Training

Teams will use AutoScientist to train their own model for the selected task.

Solution Development

Teams will build a functional application or prototype that uses their trained model to address the announced challenge.

Demonstration

Teams must demonstrate their solution and explain how the dataset and trained model contribute to solving the problem.

Participants retain their trained model weights and may publish them on platforms such as Hugging Face or Kaggle, subject to applicable platform terms and data or licensing restrictions.

Core requirement: Projects must demonstrate meaningful use of Adaption for dataset preparation or generation and model training. Simply integrating an existing third-party AI API without training a model through the required Adaption workflow will not satisfy this requirement.

Technical Workshop

A technical workshop led by an Adaption representative is planned before the hackathon. It will help participants become familiar with the platform and its model-development workflow.

Planned workshop topics:

  • Introduction to Adaption’s platform
  • Preparing or generating datasets
  • Training models using AutoScientist
  • Technical guidance and participant Q&A

Workshop date and time: To be announced
Format: Online

The confirmed schedule and joining details will be shared with registered participants.

Eligibility and Team Formation

  • Each team must consist of 2–4 members.
  • Participants must provide accurate registration and team information.
  • Each team should nominate a point of contact for event communication.
  • Teams are responsible for coordinating their work and submitting their project on time.
  • Participants must follow the official challenge instructions announced during the hackathon.

Project Submission

Teams must submit their completed projects by the deadline communicated by the organizers.

The submission is expected to include:

  • Team name and member details.
  • Project title and the announced challenge being addressed.
  • Description of the problem and proposed solution.
  • Dataset details and how it was prepared or generated.
  • Explanation of model training using Adaption’s platform.
  • Source-code repository and instructions for reviewing or running the project.
  • A working demo or recorded walkthrough.
  • Explanation of results, limitations, and potential real-world usefulness.

The official submission link, deliverables, and deadline will be provided to participants during the event.

Prizes and Adaption-Sponsored Benefits

The following Adaption-sponsored benefits are planned, subject to the final confirmed partnership terms.

Overall Winner, First Runner-up, and Second Runner-up

Recognized team members may receive additional Adaption platform credits worth $1,000 per member, subject to the confirmed eligibility and allocation terms.

Adaption Swag

Adaption swag kits will be available for recognized winners.

Best Use of Adaption Award

A $100 cash prize for the winning team will recognize effective and meaningful use of Adaption’s platform, subject to the award criteria.

Adaption Leaderboard Prize

A $200 cash prize will be awarded to an eligible participant who reaches #1 on any Adaption leaderboard domain during the 48-hour hackathon, even if they are later overtaken. This award is subject to Adaption’s leaderboard terms.

Adaption-sponsored prizes and benefits are subject to the final partnership agreement.

Event Communication

Workshop details, official problem statements, submission instructions, judging information, and other event updates will be shared through the official communication channels specified by Frontend Arena.

Participants are responsible for checking announcements and ensuring their team receives the relevant information.

Register for AI BuildFest 2026

Join the hackathon, take on a real-world challenge, train your own AI model, and develop a working solution in 48 hours.

AI BuildFest 2026 — Own Your AI. Build for a Real Problem.

problem_statement:
About the Hackathon:

What happens when creativity meets chaos?

Welcome to ChaosCore Hackathon 2026 - an open-innovation hackathon where unconventional ideas, bold experiments, and creative problem-solving come together.

There is no fixed problem statement, no predefined domain, and no restriction on technology. Choose a problem you care about, improve an existing system, create a product you've always wanted to build, or explore an entirely new idea.

This Halloween, step into the chaos, challenge the ordinary, and turn your wildest ideas into working solutions.

Embrace the Chaos. Build the Unexpected.

Join the WhatsApp group for updates and communication:

https://chat.whatsapp.com/GEJJPzKFCUDBLa4IyZl2Md?s=cl&p=a&mlu=4&ilr=4&iam=2

Tracks:

  • AI & Intelligent Systems
  • Software & Developer Tools
  • Healthcare & Wellbeing
  • Education & Learning
  • Finance & Commerce
  • Social Impact & Accessibility
  • Mobility & Urban Systems
  • Cybersecurity & Privacy
  • Productivity & Automation
  • Open Innovation

Tracks are provided for guidance only. Participants are free to build beyond these categories.

Why Participate?

  • Build Without Limits: Choose any problem, idea, or opportunity worth exploring.
  • Think Differently: Challenge conventional approaches and experiment with fresh ideas.
  • Turn Ideas Into Reality: Build a working product or functional prototype.
  • Embrace Experimentation: Explore technologies, test possibilities, and try unconventional approaches.
  • Collaborate & Create: Connect with developers, designers, AI/ML enthusiasts, and innovators.
  • Showcase Your Skills: Build a project you can demonstrate and add to your portfolio.
  • Learn From Experts: Gain feedback and insights from mentors and industry professionals.
  • Get Recognized: Showcase your creativity, technical skills, and problem-solving abilities.

Eligibility:

ChaosCore welcomes anyone interested in building with technology, including:

  • Students
  • Software Developers
  • Engineers
  • AI/ML Enthusiasts
  • Researchers
  • Entrepreneurs & Startup Builders
  • Anyone interested in building with technology

Team Size: 1–4 members

Solo participation is allowed, and cross-college, cross-disciplinary teams are welcome.

Event Format:

Round 1 - Idea Submission:

Every great creation starts with an idea. Identify a problem, opportunity, or unmet need and propose a solution worth building.

Teams must submit a short PPT presentation covering the following:

  • Slide 1: Project Title, Chosen Track, Team Name & Members
  • Slide 2: The Problem / Opportunity
  • Slide 3: Target Users & Why the Problem Matters
  • Slide 4: Your Proposed Solution
  • Slide 5: Existing Solutions / Current Approach
  • Slide 6: How It Works / User Flow
  • Slide 7: Technology Stack & Project Architecture
  • Slide 8: Basic Implementation Approach

The most promising ideas will be shortlisted for the Final Round.

Final Round - Pitch & Prototype Demo:

The top 15 shortlisted teams will advance to the Final Round.

Each team must submit a 5-7 minute pitch video presenting its project and demonstrating the working solution or functional prototype.

The video should cover:

  • Problem and target users
  • Proposed solution
  • Key features and functionality
  • Technology stack and implementation
  • Working product / prototype demonstration
  • Impact and future scope

The judging panel will evaluate how effectively each team transforms an idea into a practical, innovative, and meaningful solution.

What matters most? What you built, how well it works, the problem it solves, and the value it creates.

The top 3 teams will be selected as winners based on the final judging scores.

Rules & Guidelines:

  • Team size must be 1 - 4 members.
  • Cross-college and cross-disciplinary teams are allowed.
  • Participants may choose their own problem statement and domain.
  • There are no restrictions on programming languages, frameworks, or technologies.
  • AI tools and coding assistants are allowed.
  • Projects should demonstrate meaningful development during the hackathon.
  • Previously built projects must not be presented as entirely new work; existing components must be disclosed.
  • Teams must acknowledge external APIs, datasets, libraries, and open-source components used.
  • Plagiarism, copied submissions, and other unfair practices will result in disqualification.
  • Teams must clearly explain their problem, solution, implementation, and impact.
  • All submissions must meet the specified deadlines and requirements.
  • The judges' decisions will be final and binding.

Judging Criteria:

  • Problem Understanding – 15%
  • Problem-Solution Fit – 20%
  • Innovation & Originality – 15%
  • Feasibility & Implementation Approach – 30%
  • Impact & Value Potential – 10%
  • Idea Explanation & Clarity – 10%

Rewards & Recognition:

Top-performing teams will receive:

  • Winner / Runner - Up Certificates for the top 3 teams
  • Certificates of Merit for the top 15 teams
  • Participation Certificates for eligible participants
  • Networking Opportunities with fellow builders and professionals
  • Open-Source Recognition for noteworthy contributions

About Invoqe:

Invoqe is a student-built technology initiative focused on helping the next generation of builders learn by creating real products.

We believe that the best way to develop engineering and problem-solving skills is to build, experiment, collaborate, and ship.

Through hackathons, internships, mentorship, and hands-on projects, Invoqe creates opportunities for students, developers, and aspiring engineers to move beyond tutorials and build solutions to real-world problems.

title: Next Horizon 2026

problem_statement:
Overview

Presenting The Next Horizon 2026, an exciting online innovation marathon organized by the International Enterprise and Innovation Society, Florida and The Institution of Engineers and Scientists on 28–29 November, 2026.

This hackathon is a dynamic platform where students, professionals, and tech enthusiasts come together to brainstorm, build, and showcase cutting-edge solutions to real-world challenges. Whether you’re a seasoned coder, a design prodigy, or a curious beginner, the event offers a collaborative space to learn new skills, experiment with emerging technologies, and network with like-minded innovators.

This is your chance to turn your bold ideas into impactful prototypes. Guided by mentors and industry experts, you will tackle significant problems, push the boundaries of technology, and help pave the way for the next generation of problem-solvers. Join us to innovate, build, and make a difference!

Hackathon Themes: 

Participants are challenged to build innovative solutions in one of the following domains. You are free to identify a specific problem within your chosen theme.

  • Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI
  • Cybersecurity and Network Security
  • Smart Cities and Sustainable Development
  • Healthcare and Digital Well-being.
  • FinTech and Blockchain Applications
  • Internet of Things and Smart Automation
  • Education Technology and Digital Learning
  • Agriculture and Rural Technology
  • Open Innovation and Emerging Technologies

Eligibility:

  • This competition is open to all university students (undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral), working professionals, and technology enthusiasts.
  • There are no age or educational background restrictions. We welcome participants from Engineering, Design, Business, Sciences, and all other fields.

Team Formation:

  • Participants must form teams of 2 - 4 members.
  • Inter-college/Inter-organization team members are allowed and highly encouraged.
  • Inter-specialization team members are highly encouraged. A diverse team with developers, designers, and business strategists often creates the most well-rounded solutions.
  • Lone wolves are not allowed; participation is strictly team-based.

Competition Format & Rounds

Round 1: Idea Submission

  • Submit a  PDF/ PPT detailing:
    • Problem statement and chosen theme
    • Proposed solution and unique features
    • Technology stack
    • Real-world impact and feasibility
  • Evaluation based on innovation, clarity, feasibility, and relevance.
  • Shortlisted teams advance to Round 2.

Round 2: Prototype Development & Final Presentation

  • Build a working prototype or MVP.
  • Finalists present live (virtually) to an expert jury from academia and industry.

Timeline & Duration

  • Hackathon Dates: November 28-29, 2026 (2 days)
  • Registration Deadline: November 15, 2026

Rules & Regulations:

  • Code of Conduct: All participants must maintain a professional and respectful environment. Harassment or any form of misconduct will result in immediate disqualification.
  • Originality: All work must be the original creation of the team. Ideas and code should be developed during the hackathon. Using pre-existing projects is strictly prohibited.
  • Open Source: The use of open-source libraries, frameworks, and public APIs is permitted and encouraged. You must declare all such components in your final submission.
  • Intellectual Property (IP): Your team will retain full ownership of what you build. By participating, you grant the organizers the right to showcase your project for promotional and non-commercial purposes.
  • Submission Deadlines: All deadlines are final. Late submissions will not be considered for evaluation.
  • Judging: The decision of the judging panel is final and binding. The judging criteria will include:
    • Innovation & Creativity: How original and novel is the solution?
    • Impact & Relevance: How effectively does it address a real-world problem?
    • Technical Implementation: The quality, functionality, and elegance of the code.
    • User Experience (UX/UI): How intuitive and well-designed is the final product?
    • Presentation: Clarity and persuasiveness of your final pitch.
  • The organizers reserve the right to modify any rules or timelines. All changes will be communicated clearly to the participants.

Rewards & Prizes:

  • Total Prize Pool $1500 for Winners & Runner-Ups
  • All finalists will receive Certificates of Recognition

Have questions?

Feel free to reach out to us at secretary@theioes.org

About the Event: (https://datanovathon.com)

DataNova 2026 is a global virtual Data-thon designed to bring together innovators, students, researchers, developers, data scientists and technology professionals to address meaningful challenges through data-driven innovation.

  • Participants can leverage AI tools for prompting, development, testing, and deployment. The focus is on solving the given problem effectively, demonstrating smart prompt engineering, building a usable product, and delivering a successful deployment. The top 8 teams will qualify to present their products through live demonstrations to a panel of judges.

Guidelines

  • Eligibility: Open to students from any college.
  • Team Formation: Teams must consist of 2–3 participants.
  • Problem Statement: The problem statement will be released by the organizers at the beginning of the event. Teams must build their solution based on the given statement.
  • Event Duration: The competition will run from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM.
  • AI Tools: Approved AI tools may be used for prompting, development, testing, debugging, and deployment.
  • Required Equipment: Participants must bring their own laptop and charger, along with their development tools, GitHub access, AI-tool accounts, and any required API credentials.
  • Submission Requirements: Each team must submit:
    • A publicly accessible live product URL.
    • A GitHub repository containing the event project.
    • A README documenting the problem statement, solution, technology stack, implementation, deployment, and limitations.
    • Key prompt history demonstrating iteration and debugging.
    • A short screen-recorded demonstration of the product.
  • Finalist Selection: The top 8 teams will be selected based on the preliminary evaluation and will proceed to the live demonstration round.
  • Final Presentation: Each finalist team will deliver a three-minute live demo followed by two minutes of questions from the judges.

Event Schedule

  1. 9:00 AM – 9:15 AM: Reporting, seating, platform access, and connectivity check.
  2. 9:15 AM – 9:30 AM: Rulebook briefing, judging criteria, and problem statement release.
  3. 9:30 AM – 11:30 AM: Build phase — architecture, prompting, development, and testing.
  4. 11:30 AM – 11:50 AM: Final submission and preliminary evaluation.
  5. 11:50 AM – 12:45 PM: Live demonstrations by the top 8 teams, followed by judges' questions.
  6. 12:45 PM – 1:00 PM: Results announcement and closing.

Rules

  1. Original Work Only: All projects must be developed during the event in response to the released problem statement. Previously completed projects and project-specific code prepared before the event are prohibited.
  2. Approved AI Tools: Participants may use AI tools for prompting, coding, debugging, testing, and deployment, subject to the approved tools and restrictions specified by the organizers.
  3. Mandatory Submission: All required deliverables, including the live product URL, GitHub repository, README, prompt history, and screen-recorded demo, must be submitted before the deadline.
  4. Deployment: The submitted product must be publicly accessible and functional at the time of evaluation.
  5. Judging Criteria: Teams will be evaluated according to the following criteria:
    • Problem-solving and innovation — 25%
    • Prompt strategy and execution — 25%
    • UI/UX and functionality — 20%
    • Deployment and completeness — 15%
    • Live pitch and demo — 10%
    • Documentation — 5%
  6. Finalist Presentations: The top 8 teams must present a three-minute live demo, followed by two minutes of questions from the judges.
  7. Fair Play: Plagiarism, misrepresentation of work, and attempts to gain an unfair advantage are prohibited and may result in disqualification.
  8. Team Participation: All team members must be registered participants and contribute to the development and presentation of their solution.

problem_statement:
Overview

The Last Daemon — Capture The Flag (CTF) by Beunwrapd

Join the Official WhatsApp Community:
https://chat.whatsapp.com/EpDiRs3oQ1t6riNwVgGJqF

About the Competition

The digital world is full of secrets, vulnerabilities, and hidden information. Are you ready to uncover them?

The Last Daemon is a cybersecurity Capture The Flag (CTF) competition organized by Beunwrapd, designed to challenge aspiring ethical hackers, cybersecurity enthusiasts, and students through hands-on security problems.

Participants will test their technical knowledge, analytical thinking, investigative abilities, and problem-solving skills across multiple cybersecurity domains. From decoding cryptographic messages to investigating digital evidence and uncovering web vulnerabilities, every challenge will push participants to think critically and approach problems creatively.

Whether you are an experienced CTF player or a beginner exploring cybersecurity, The Last Daemon invites you to test your skills and compete against other participants.

No teams. No shortcuts. Just you, your skills, and the challenge.

Competition Domains

Participants can expect challenges across the following cybersecurity domains:

  • Web Security: Identify vulnerabilities and solve web-based security challenges.
  • Cryptography: Decode encrypted messages and uncover hidden flags.
  • Digital Forensics: Investigate files, metadata, and digital evidence.
  • OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence): Analyze publicly available information to uncover clues.
  • Reverse Engineering: Analyze programs and uncover their underlying logic.
  • Miscellaneous: Solve unconventional technical puzzles requiring creativity and logical reasoning.

Challenges may vary in difficulty, allowing participants to demonstrate their skills and learn through practical problem-solving.

Eligibility and Participation Guidelines

  • The competition is open to students and cybersecurity enthusiasts interested in ethical hacking and information security.
  • Participants from all colleges, universities, academic disciplines, and specializations are welcome.
  • Participation Mode: Solo Only. Every participant must compete individually.
  • Team formation and team registrations are not permitted.
  • Inter-college and inter-specialization teams are not applicable because this is an individual competition.
  • Every participant must register individually through the official Unstop listing.
  • Participants must use their own registered accounts to access challenges and submit flags.
  • Beginners are welcome. A basic understanding of computers and cybersecurity concepts may be helpful.

Competition Format

  • Competition Type: Capture The Flag (CTF)
  • Participation Mode: Individual / Solo
  • Format: Challenge-based cybersecurity competition
  • Challenge Domains: Web Security, Cryptography, Digital Forensics, OSINT, Reverse Engineering, and Miscellaneous
  • Number of Challenges: To be announced through the official competition platform.
  • Competition Duration: The confirmed date, start time, end time, and total duration will be communicated through the official event listing or organizer announcements.

How It Works

  • Register: Complete your individual registration through Unstop.
  • Access the Platform: Follow the instructions provided by the organizers.
  • Solve Challenges: Investigate and solve problems across the available cybersecurity domains.
  • Capture the Flags: Find hidden flags and submit them through the designated platform.
  • Earn Points: Gain points for correctly solving challenges according to their assigned values.
  • Climb the Leaderboard: Compete individually against other participants.
  • Final Results: Rankings will be determined according to the official scoring and tie-breaking rules.

All challenges must be solved independently. Collaboration on solutions and sharing flags with other competitors during the competition are prohibited.

Rules and Regulations

  • Individual Participation: Every participant must compete independently. Team participation and joint submissions are prohibited.
  • Fair Play: Sharing flags, complete solutions, or restricted hints with other competitors during the event is not allowed.
  • Authorized Scope: Participants may test only the challenges and systems explicitly included within the competition scope.
  • No Infrastructure Attacks: Attacking the CTF platform, organizer infrastructure, or other participants' systems is strictly prohibited.
  • No Service Disruption: Denial-of-service attacks, excessive requests, or any activity intended to disrupt the competition are forbidden.
  • No Unauthorized Access: Accessing other participants' accounts, submissions, private data, or restricted resources is prohibited.
  • No Score Manipulation: Exploiting platform vulnerabilities to manipulate scores or obtain unauthorized points may result in disqualification.
  • Responsible Tool Usage: Tools and scripts may be used for legitimate challenge-solving purposes, provided they remain within the authorized scope and do not disrupt services.
  • No Plagiarism: Submitting another participant's work as your own is prohibited.
  • Report Technical Issues: Suspected vulnerabilities in the competition infrastructure must be reported privately to the organizers.
  • Account Responsibility: Participants must use their own registered accounts and are responsible for securing their credentials.
  • Professional Conduct: All participants must behave respectfully toward the organizers and fellow competitors.
  • Disqualification: Cheating, unauthorized attacks, rule violations, or attempts to gain an unfair advantage may result in disqualification.
  • Organizer Authority: The organizing team reserves the right to investigate violations, verify submissions, resolve disputes, and make final decisions regarding the results.
  • Schedule Updates: Any changes to the competition schedule, format, or instructions will be communicated through official channels.

Scoring and Leaderboard

  • Points will be awarded for correctly solving challenges and submitting valid flags.
  • Challenge scores may vary according to difficulty.
  • Rankings will be based on individual performance.
  • In case of a tie, the official tie-breaking criteria communicated by the organizers will apply.
  • Final results will be subject to score verification and compliance with the competition rules.

Get Ready for the Hunt

  • Every flag tells a story. Every challenge hides a clue. Every solution brings you one step closer to the truth.
  • The Last Daemon is about thinking differently, investigating carefully, and proving what you can accomplish on your own.
  • One participant. One mission. One ultimate hunt.

Are you ready to face The Last Daemon?

title: Bazaar: Beat the Markets
problem_statement:
All that you need to know about EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market

EIC Bazaar: Beat the Market

Everyone has an opinion on the market. Very few can act on it when prices move every second and the news is half-true. EIC Bazaar is where you find out which one you are.

Organized by the Entrepreneurship & Incubation Cell (EIC) as part of E-Summit, Bazaar is a live stock market trading competition for students. Fictional companies, simulated markets, virtual capital. The pressure is real.

What Makes Bazaar Different?

  • Forget static prediction games and paper quizzes. Bazaar runs on a trading platform built specifically for this event, with live prices, breaking news and timed sessions where every decision counts.
  • You don't just trade one market, you trade two. First you play as a retail investor, reading charts and reacting to news. Then you step up to the institutional level, where your own orders move prices, bots trade alongside you, and the market pushes back.
  • News reaches you from many sources: newspapers, analysts, insiders and finfluencers. Not all of them deserve your trust, and knowing which to believe is half the game. The Grand Finale is held at E-Summit, so you compete in the same venue as founders, investors and innovators.

Who Should Apply?

  • Bazaar is for anyone who follows the markets, enjoys fast decisions, data or strategy, and wants to experience trading without risking real money. You don't need prior trading experience.
  • Beginners can learn from the rulebook and strategy hints shared before the Finale, and experienced traders will find plenty to exploit. Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students across India. Cross-college teams are welcome.

Competition Structure

Bazaar runs across two rounds.

  • Round 1 is an Online Quiz on Unstop, covering stock market basics, financial instruments, chart and news reading, and risk-based reasoning.
  • Round 2 is the Grand Finale, held in person at PEC, Chandigarh on 14-15 November as part of E-Summit. Finalists trade on Bazaar's live platform across two stages:
  • Stage 1: Retail. Start with virtual capital. Trade across a range of instruments using technical tools. Trading happens in timed sessions that get tougher as new instruments and news unlock.
  • Stage 2: Institutional. Start fresh with new virtual capital. Now your trades move prices, and bots compete with you for liquidity.

Every trade carries a transaction fee, so overtrading will cost you. Teams are ranked on trading performance. General scoring guidelines and a rulebook will be shared with registered teams before the Finale.

Team Details

  • Team Size: 2 to 4 members
  • Cross-college and cross-city teams: Fully allowed and encouraged
  • Solo registrations: Not accepted
  • One person registers as Team Leader and adds the remaining members on Unstop

title: The Outpost
problem_statement:
THE OUTPOST

One Problem. One Builder. Six Hours.

THE OUTPOST is a 6-hour, fully online, individual frontend development hackathon organized by Frontend Arena, designed to challenge participants to turn creative ideas into functional, visually impressive, and user-friendly web experiences.

Inspired by the spirit of exploration, strategy, and teamwork-free individual competition, THE OUTPOST gives every participant the opportunity to showcase their frontend development skills, creativity, and problem-solving abilities through a time-bound coding mission.

Participants will receive a problem statement at the beginning of the hackathon and must independently design, develop, test, and submit their solution within the allotted six hours.

This is an individual competition. Every participant builds their own project, submits their solution, and competes against other participants based on the quality of their implementation.

Hackathon Format

Duration: 6 Hours
Mode: Fully Online
Participation: Individual
Domain: Frontend Web Development
Challenge Format: Problem Statement-Based
Participation Fee: Completely Free
Evaluation: Defined Hackathon Evaluation Criteria
Competition: Individual Project Submission

Participants will receive the challenge at the beginning of the event and will have six hours to understand the requirements, plan their approach, build the application, test its functionality, and refine the final experience before submission.

The Frontend Mission

THE OUTPOST focuses on building modern, interactive, and visually polished web applications.

Participants must transform the given problem statement into a working frontend solution that demonstrates creativity, usability, functionality, and strong design decisions.

The goal is not simply to create a webpage. Participants should build an experience that solves the given problem while demonstrating their ability to make effective technical and design decisions under time constraints.

Modern Technology Requirement

THE OUTPOST is designed around modern frontend development practices.

Participants are required to use a modern frontend framework, library, or technology stack to build their projects.

Examples of acceptable technologies include:

  • React

  • Next.js

  • Vue

  • Nuxt

  • Svelte

  • SvelteKit

  • Angular

  • Astro

  • Remix

  • TypeScript

  • Tailwind CSS and modern styling frameworks

  • Modern UI and component libraries

  • Animation and interaction libraries such as Framer Motion

  • Other suitable modern frontend technologies

Participants may choose the technology stack that best suits their solution, provided it meets the hackathon requirements.

Standalone Technologies Are Not Permitted as the Primary Stack

The following are not permitted as the primary project stack:

  • Raw HTML-only projects

  • Raw CSS-only projects

  • Vanilla JavaScript-only projects

  • Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript websites without a modern framework or technology stack

HTML, CSS, and JavaScript may naturally be used within modern frameworks, but the project must be built using a suitable modern frontend stack.

Vibe Coding and AI-Assisted Development

Participants may use modern development tools to accelerate their workflow and improve productivity.

Permitted tools and resources include:

  • AI coding assistants

  • Vibe Coding platforms

  • Code editors and development environments

  • UI design and prototyping tools

  • Component libraries and design systems

  • Animation and interaction libraries

  • Public documentation and learning resources

  • Debugging and testing tools

  • Other relevant frontend development tools

Participants are responsible for understanding, testing, and validating the code they submit. The use of AI tools does not replace the need for a functional, well-designed, and technically sound solution.

Evaluation Criteria

Submissions will be evaluated using the following criteria:

1. UI/UX Design and Visual Quality
Visual consistency, layout, typography, spacing, usability, and overall presentation.

2. Functionality
Working interactions, navigation, core features, and implementation of the required functionality.

3. Creativity and Innovation
Original ideas, thoughtful design choices, and creative approaches to solving the problem.

4. Problem Statement Alignment
How effectively the project addresses the given challenge and fulfills its requirements.

5. Code Quality and Technical Implementation
Code structure, maintainability, appropriate use of technologies, and overall implementation quality.

6. Responsiveness and Accessibility
Usability across different screen sizes, responsive layouts, and attention to accessibility.

The final evaluation will follow the official criteria and scoring framework announced by the organizers.

How THE OUTPOST Works

01 — The Brief
Receive the official problem statement at the beginning of the hackathon.

02 — Plan
Understand the requirements and decide how to approach the challenge.

03 — Build
Develop your solution using an eligible modern frontend technology stack.

04 — Test and Improve
Validate functionality, refine the UI, fix issues, and improve the overall user experience.

05 — Submit
Submit your completed project through the official submission process before the deadline.

06 — Evaluation
The submitted projects are assessed according to the official hackathon evaluation criteria.

07 — Results
Final results are determined according to the organizers' announced evaluation and ranking process.

Rules and Guidelines

  • THE OUTPOST is an individual participation hackathon. Team submissions are not permitted.

  • The total development period is six hours.

  • The event is conducted fully online.

  • Participation is completely free.

  • Participants must build a solution relevant to the provided problem statement.

  • A modern frontend framework, library, or technology stack is mandatory.

  • Raw HTML-only, CSS-only, and Vanilla JavaScript-only projects are not permitted as the primary stack.

  • AI-assisted development and Vibe Coding tools are permitted.

  • Projects should be developed within the official hackathon duration.

  • Participants are responsible for testing their project and checking the submission requirements before submitting.

  • Submissions received after the official deadline may not be considered.

  • Participants must follow all instructions communicated by the organizers.

  • The final results will be determined according to the official evaluation process.

Who Can Participate?

THE OUTPOST welcomes individuals interested in:

  • Frontend Development

  • Web Development

  • UI/UX Design

  • Creative Coding

  • Modern JavaScript Frameworks

  • Vibe Coding

  • AI-Assisted Development

  • Rapid Prototyping

  • Building Digital Products

Whether you are a student, aspiring developer, experienced coder, or technology enthusiast, this is an opportunity to challenge yourself and demonstrate your ability to build under pressure.

The Challenge

At the beginning of the event, participants will receive a specific problem statement.

Your mission is to transform that brief into a creative, functional, responsive, and visually polished frontend experience within six hours.

Your project should demonstrate:

  • A clear understanding of the problem

  • Functional and meaningful interactions

The Final Mission

Six hours. One problem statement. One individual builder.

THE OUTPOST is your opportunity to think creatively, build strategically, and turn your ideas into a working digital experience.

Design. Develop. Deploy your creativity.

Each challenge represents a practical security scenario, encouraging participants to think like ethical hackers while maintaining legal and responsible boundaries. The aim is not just to break systems but to understand, analyze, and defend them that promote both offensive and defensive cybersecurity skills.

problem_statement:
Overview:

Techkriti’27, IIT Kanpur, presents Capture the Flag (CTF) — a cybersecurity competition where participants solve practical security challenges in a simulated real-world environment. Identify vulnerabilities, apply technical problem-solving skills, and capture hidden flags to score points.

The competition will challenge participants across areas such as penetration testing, reverse engineering, cryptography, and vulnerability exploitation, requiring them to choose the right tools and techniques to solve increasingly challenging problems.

Guidelines:

  • Team Composition: Participants can compete individually or in teams of up to 2 members. The contest is team-rated, and participants forming a team must register accordingly.

  • Fair Play & Disqualification: Any form of malpractice or plagiarism will result in immediate disqualification. Participants must follow all competition guidelines. In case of any dispute, the decision of the Techkriti Team, IIT Kanpur, will be final.

Rules & Event Structure:

  • Competition Format: The competition will consist of a single round featuring numerous cybersecurity and cryptographic challenges, approximately 8–10.
  • Each challenge will contain a hidden flag, represented as a string of characters, which participants must discover to earn points. The contest will be conducted online and will have a duration of 6 hours.
  • Each problem will be accompanied by a problem statement and relevant code for participants to analyze and work with. Winners will be determined based on their total score.
  • In case of a tie, the participant/team with the faster submission time will be given preference. 

Difficulty Progression:

The challenges will increase in difficulty as the competition progresses, testing participants' ability to identify vulnerabilities, analyze systems, and apply appropriate cybersecurity techniques. Participants may need to demonstrate skills in penetration testing, reverse engineering, cryptography, and related areas of cybersecurity.

  • Individual participation: Yes. Participants can compete individually or in a team of a maximum 2 members.

problem_statement:

Build or Migrate an AI App. Publish It on Anna. Grow It With Real Users.

The Anna AI App Builder Challenge invites developers to turn an existing AI Agent, Python or Node.js script, MCP server, workflow, open-source project, SaaS product, or a completely new idea into a fully functional user-facing App on Anna AI OS.

Participants will build or migrate their project, submit it for Anna App Review, publish the approved App, and grow real user adoption.

Get Started Now:

Understand everything: Official Program Rules and FAQ.

  • Create Your Anna Account: https://anna.partners
  • Join the Builder Discord: https://discord.gg/7ftTdsdMMz
  • Read the Docs: https://anna.partners/developers
  • Use the AI-Readable Developer Docs: https://anna.partners/llms.txt. Paste this URL into Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, or another AI coding assistant to help it understand the Anna development framework.
  • Explore GitHub Examples: https://github.com/whtcjdtc2007/anna-executa-examples
  • Step-by-Step Beginner's Guide: From Zero to Your First Anna App

Challenge Goal:

Build or migrate a functional AI App, pass Anna App Review, publish it for real users, and grow verified user adoption.

Challenge Highlights:

  • Up to $5,000 per App per eligible month
  • Grants begin at 200 Qualified App MAU
  • Up to $80,000 in total Builder Grants each month
  • No Top 3 leaderboard and no winner-takes-all judging
  • Existing Agents, scripts, MCP servers, open-source projects, and SaaS products are welcome

Every eligible App that reaches a published MAU tier may receive the corresponding monthly grant, subject to the Official Program Rules.

Qualify by November 30, 2026, and continue participating in future monthly grant cycles afterward.

Who Should Join?:

This challenge is designed for:

  • Indie hackers and solo builders
  • AI Agent developers
  • MCP server builders
  • Open-source maintainers
  • Automation and workflow creators
  • Existing AI or SaaS teams
  • Hackathon teams that want to continue beyond the demo

You do not need to start from scratch. You may adapt an existing project into an Anna App.

What Can You Build?:

Your starting point may include:

  • Python or Node.js scripts
  • AI Agents
  • MCP servers
  • Multi-agent systems
  • Open-source projects
  • Existing AI or SaaS products
  • A completely new App idea

The final submission must be a complete Anna App that:

  • Is approved and published on the Anna App Store
  • Is fully runnable by users inside Anna
  • Has a clear user-facing interface
  • Includes working backend logic or execution
  • Provides genuine and independently usable functionality

A repository, Agent, MCP server, demo video, or pitch deck alone is not an eligible final submission.

Challenge Objective & Submission:

Your challenge is to build or migrate a functional AI App on Anna AI OS and publish it for real users.

To Complete the Challenge, Participants Must:

  • Create or migrate an eligible project into an Anna App
  • Build a complete user-facing interface with working functionality
  • Submit the App for Anna App Review
  • Pass review and publish the App on Anna
  • Grow genuine user adoption after publication

Submissions are evaluated based on successful App Review, publication, functional usability, and real, verified user adoption. There is no traditional Top 3 judging model.

How The Challenge Works:

Create an Account → Activate Developer Access → Build or Migrate → Submit for Review → Publish → Grow

Create your Anna account, activate your developer profile, and start building or adapting your existing project using Anna’s developer tools. Submit your completed App for review, publish it to the Anna App Store after approval, and grow your Qualified App MAU.

Monthly Grant Tiers:

Grow your App and qualify for the highest eligible tier you reach each month based on Qualified App MAU:

  • 200+ MAU — $50/month
  • 500+ MAU — $100/month
  • 1,000+ MAU — $200/month
  • 4,000+ MAU — $1,000/month
  • 10,000+ MAU — $2,500/month
  • 20,000+ MAU — $5,000/month

Important Grant Rules:

  • Each App receives the grant for the highest eligible MAU tier reached that month.
  • Tier rewards are not cumulative.
  • Each calendar month is measured and settled separately.
  • Approved grants are normally paid within 30 days after the measurement month ends.
  • The $80,000 amount is the total monthly Builder Grant pool, not a single-App prize.

For complete eligibility, verification, payment, and fair-play requirements, please review the Official Program Rules and FAQ.

What Is Qualified App MAU?:

MAU means Monthly Active Users.

One Qualified App MAU is one unique, signed-in Anna user who successfully completes at least one Qualified App Run during the applicable calendar month.

A Qualified App Run must:

  • Be initiated by a valid, signed-in Anna user
  • Successfully execute the App’s declared primary function
  • Return a meaningful, non-trivial result

Qualified usage may come from Free Anna Credits, Paid Anna Credits, or BYOK (Bring Your Own Key).

Simply opening, viewing, or installing an App does not count. Failed runs, test accounts, bots, device farms, coordinated self-runs, and artificial or meaningless usage are also excluded.

Anna’s server-side execution records are used for MAU measurement and verification.

Participants who discover the challenge through Unstop can continue building, publishing, and growing their App on Anna after Unstop registration closes. title: Pokerbots
organizer: International Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Bangalore
problem_statement:
About the Event:

Test your algorithmic trading and game theory skills in Pokerbots, a high-stakes algorithmic bot competition!

Teams must code an autonomous Python bot to compete in a custom poker variant designed with modified Texas Hold’em mechanics to prevent the use of public repositories.

Technical & Runtime Constraints:

  • Environment: Python 3.11.
  • Allowed Libraries: Standard Python libraries, NumPy, and SciPy only (no pip installations allowed at runtime).
  • Compute Limits: 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, read-only filesystem, and zero network access.
  • Time Bank: Cumulative time bank per match (~60 seconds for 400 hands) with a hard wall-clock kill. Crashes or exhausted time banks result in match forfeiture.
  • Communication Protocol: Bots operate automatically via a predefined stdin/stdout protocol.

Tournament Structure & Progression:

All matches utilize duplicate deals (playing every deal twice with swapped seats) to mitigate luck and seat advantage.

  • Stage 1 (Swiss Qualifier): Valid bots play 6 rounds of ~200 duplicate deals (400 hands). Match points: 1 for Win, 0.5 for Draw, 0 for Loss.
  • Stage 2 (Top 32 Finals): The top 32 qualifying teams advance to a full round-robin stage (~500 duplicate deals each). Scores reset prior to this stage.
  • Tie-Breakers: Calculated using a capped chips per hand formula.

Rules & Regulations:

  • Team Size: Teams must consist of exactly 2 members. An individual can only be on one team.
  • Submissions: Teams can re-upload/overwrite submissions until November 15th at 23:59 IST. Only the last valid upload counts.
  • Fair Play & Code Review: Code copying, collusion, and network calls are strictly prohibited. Winners' source code will undergo a thorough manual review prior to prize payouts.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Duplicate Deal Performance: Match points accrued during the Swiss Qualifier and final standings in the round-robin stage.

title: The Black-Box Protocol: Stage 03 - System Convergence
problem_statement:
The Black-Box Protocol: Stage 03 — “System Convergence”

The 36-Hour Hackathon Mirage Is Dead.

Conventional hackathons often end where the real engineering begins.

Developers build rushed prototypes, prepare a final presentation, demonstrate a concept, and walk away. The code may work for a few minutes—but the system rarely survives beyond the closing ceremony.

This is the Mirage.

The Black-Box Protocol was engineered to break that cycle.

Stage 03 // “System Convergence” is a 36-hour, high-intensity offline engineering crucible designed to push builders beyond prototypes and towards systems that demonstrate architectural resilience, technical depth, real-world utility, and long-term scalability.

No forced tracks.
No predefined problem statements.
No restricted technology stack.

You choose the problem. You design the architecture. You build the system.

Welcome to Stage 03 // “System Convergence.”

Are you ready to build systems that survive?

The 2-Round Architecture & Execution Model

To maintain a high-quality technical ecosystem, the hackathon follows a structured two-round pipeline.

To reach the final 36-hour build arena, teams must clear the initial registration and screening process before entering the physical engineering crucible.

Round 01 // Registration & Initial System Screening

Online Registration & Idea Screening

  • Registration Opens: August 28, 2026
  • Registration Deadline: September 25, 2026 | 11:59 PM IST
  • Shortlist Announcement: September 28, 2026
  • RSVP Confirmation: September 29, 2026

Round 01 Execution Model

  • Portal Onboarding: Register your team and submit the required participant and team details.
  • Each team must consist of 2–4 members.
  • Every participating team must include at least one female builder. Teams without female representation will be disqualified during the initial screening process.
  • Preliminary Idea Pitch: Stage 03 follows a strict 100% Open Innovation model.
  • There are no artificial domain restrictions or mandatory tracks.
  • Teams are free to identify any meaningful real-world problem and develop a solution using their preferred technologies, frameworks, programming languages, protocols, and development methodologies.
  • The Initial System Filter: Submitted teams and ideas will undergo an initial screening process before the final shortlist is announced.
  • The objective is to identify teams capable of participating in a high-intensity engineering environment and developing meaningful, technically viable solutions.
  • Shortlist Announcement: September 28, 2026.
  • Approximately 75–90 teams will be shortlisted for the offline hackathon.
  • RSVP & Final Confirmation: October 1, 2026.
  • Shortlisted teams must complete their final RSVP confirmation, travel verification, and participant credentialing.
  • Only confirmed teams proceed to the 36-hour System Convergence.

Round 02 // The 36-Hour System Convergence

Offline Engineering Crucible

  • Date: October 6–7, 2026
  • Location: TBA
  • Duration: 36 Hours — Non-Stop
  • Scale: Approximately 300–350 builders across 75–90 teams

This is where the real protocol begins.

No presentation-first approach.

No prototype-only evaluation.

You build. You test. You deploy. You prove.

Round 02 Execution Model — Step by Step

Hour 00 // Ingestion & Deployment

Participant Check-In

Physical verification, ID kit distribution, table allotment, and network setup.

Opening Briefing

Protocol orientation, evaluation rubric briefing, and mentor introductions.

Hacking Commences

Hour 00:00

Repository creation, initial commit verification, and the 36-hour build officially begins.

Hour 08 // Checkpoint 01 — Architecture Audit

Mentors conduct the first structured diagnostic review.

The audit focuses on:

  • System architecture
  • Database selection
  • API design
  • System schemas
  • Scope feasibility
  • Architectural weaknesses

The objective is to identify unviable scope and structural problems before they become critical failures.

Hour 18 // Checkpoint 02 — Stress-Test Clinic

The second diagnostic intervention pushes the system under pressure.

Focus areas include:

  • Backend load handling
  • Concurrency
  • API limitations
  • Security
  • Reliability
  • Backend debugging

Your system doesn't just need to work. It needs to withstand stress.

Hour 28 // Checkpoint 03 — Viability Polish

The final mentor intervention focuses on transforming a working build into a convincing product.

Teams receive guidance on:

  • UX smoothness
  • User onboarding
  • Deployment health
  • Product viability
  • Live demonstration flow
  • Pitch refinement

Hour 34 // Code Freeze

October 7

The repository enters absolute freeze.

No commits will be accepted after the deadline.

All teams must have their final working systems ready for evaluation.

Hour 34+ // Tier-1 Table-Side Scrutiny

Four parallel judging pools evaluate the participating teams.

Each team receives:

  • 3-Minute Live Demo
  • 2-Minute Q&A

No dry pitching.

No presentation-only evaluation.

Show the system. Run the system. Defend the system.

The Top 10 teams advance to the Grand Stage.

Hour 36 // The Grand Stage

The Top 10 finalists pitch their systems live before the grand jury and audience.

  • 4-Minute Pitch
  • 2-Minute Jury Q&A

This is the final test of your:

  • Technical execution
  • Problem understanding
  • Product thinking
  • Scalability
  • Business viability
  • Communication

Awards & Incubation Reveal

8 October 2026

The final winners are announced.

Cash rewards, internships, goodies, merchandise, and post-hackathon opportunities are revealed.

The 100% Open Innovation Horizon

There are zero restricted tracks.

You are not limited to a predefined theme.

Build wherever the problem takes you.

Builder Horizons

  • Autonomous AI agents & generative systems
  • Distributed networks
  • Cryptographic & Web3 protocols
  • Enterprise developer tooling
  • Cloud infrastructure
  • DevOps
  • FinTech
  • Healthcare
  • Logistics
  • Cyber Defense
  • IoT
  • High-complexity consumer applications
  • Any other meaningful real-world challenge

The domain is yours. The engineering is yours. The system is yours.

The Universal Technical Benchmark

Every project will be tested against core engineering benchmarks.

Architecture Resilience

Clean modular boundaries and maintainability.

Security & Error Handling

Ability to withstand failures and edge cases.

Execution Completeness

A fully functioning live system with zero mock data.

Real-World Utility

Measurable impact and clear adoption logic.

Registration Compliance & Protocol Rules

Fresh Codebase

Open-source packages and APIs are permitted.

Pre-built private codebases will lead to immediate disqualification.

Repository Integrity

All code must be authored and systematically committed during the active 36-hour build window.

100% Builder IP

All code, designs, and intellectual property remain 100% owned by the participating teams.

Team Integrity

Team-member swaps after on-ground check-in are strictly prohibited.

Zero Tolerance

A strict anti-harassment policy will be enforced to maintain a safe and inclusive environment.

This Is System Convergence

A problem is only the beginning.

An idea is not a product.

A prototype is not a system.

And a demo is not proof.

Build the architecture.
Survive the stress.
Deploy the system.
Prove the utility.

The Black-Box Protocol: Stage 03 — System Convergence is built for developers, designers, founders, and builders who want to move beyond temporary prototypes and engineer solutions capable of surviving the real world.

36 HOURS.
75–90 TEAMS.
300–350 BUILDERS.
ONE SYSTEM TO PROVE.

Stop Building Throwaway Apps.

Start Building Systems That Survive.

Welcome to the Black-Box Protocol.

Stay Connected

title: Slay CTF
organizer: Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College (JGEC), West Bengal
problem_statement:
About the Event:

Slay CTF is a thrilling, jeopardy-style Capture The Flag competition designed to test your offensive security skills, analytical thinking, and problem-solving abilities. Whether you are a beginner looking to break into the world of cybersecurity or a seasoned hacker hunting for complex challenges, Slay CTF offers a dynamic environment to exploit vulnerabilities, crack ciphers, and trace digital footprints.

Put your skills to the test, climb the global leaderboard, and prove your mettle in the ultimate battle of bits and bytes!

Eligibility & Registration Guidelines:

  • Target Audience: Open to all students (UG/PG/Diploma), early-career professionals, and self-taught security enthusiasts.
  • Inter-College Teams: Allowed and highly encouraged.
  • Inter-Specialization Teams: Allowed (Open to all branches and backgrounds).
  • Team Size: Participate individually or in teams of [1 - 3 members].
  • Prerequisites: Eagerness to learn.

Challenge Categories (Topics)

The CTF will feature a diverse set of challenges scaled from beginner to advanced difficulties across the following domains:

  • Web Exploitation: Uncover vulnerabilities in web applications (e.g., SQLi, XSS, IDOR, SSRF).
  • OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence): Track down hidden information and piece together digital trails across the public internet.
  • Cryptography: Break encryption schemes, decode ciphers, and analyze cryptographic protocols.
  • Digital Forensics: Analyze memory dumps, network packet captures (PCAPs), and hidden file metadata.
  • Reverse Engineering: Deconstruct compiled binaries and understand their underlying logic.
  • Miscellaneous / Sanity: Brain-teasers, scripting challenges, and out-of-the-box puzzles.

Event Format & Process

  • Format: Hybrid (Online + JGEC Campus), Jeopardy-Style CTF.
  • Platform: Challenges will be hosted on our dedicated infrastructure (CTFd).
  • Duration: The competition will run continuously for 3 hours.
  • Scoring System: Dynamic scoring will be implemented (the point value of a challenge decreases as more teams solve it).
  • Process: Once registered on Unstop, team leaders will receive the platform link and credentials via email 24 hours prior to the event kickoff.

Rules & Code of Conduct

  • No Flag Sharing: Sharing flags or solutions with other teams is strictly prohibited and will result in immediate disqualification of all involved parties.
  • No Brute-Forcing: Automated brute-forcing of the flag submission platform or challenge infrastructure is forbidden unless explicitly mentioned in the challenge description.
  • No Attacking the Infrastructure: Do not launch Denial of Service (DoS/DDoS) attacks or attempt to compromise the hosting servers.
  • Collaboration: You are free to use Google, AI tools, and public documentation, but collaboration is strictly limited to your own team members.
  • Final Decisions: The organizing team's decisions regarding scoring, disputes, and disqualifications are final and binding.

Prizes & Perks

  • Cash Prize, Certification Vouchers and goodies. [NOTE: Cash Prizes and Goodies exclusively for offline participation]
  • Official Certificate of Participation for those who solve at least one challenge.

title: AETHOS - Day Zero
problem_statement:

  • Unlike conventional hackathons that ask participants to build products around a technology, DAY ZERO challenges teams to engineer the foundations of an entirely new civilization.
  • Participants are encouraged to think beyond applications and incremental improvements. Every project should solve a meaningful challenge that contributes to rebuilding society—whether through communication, energy, healthcare, infrastructure, education, resilience, exploration, or entirely new approaches that redefine the future.

  • It is about engineering tomorrow.

The Mission:

  • Design and develop an innovative solution that would help humanity rebuild after the collapse of modern civilization.
  • Your project may be software, hardware, embedded systems, IoT, AI, robotics, communication systems, cybersecurity, biotechnology, space technology, sustainable engineering, or any interdisciplinary solution aligned with the mission.
  • Projects should focus on solving real-world problems with practical engineering, long-term scalability, and meaningful societal impact.

Civilization Pillars:

  • Every project belongs to one of the official Civilization Pillars that represent the essential functions required to rebuild society.
  • The detailed descriptions of all pillars are provided separately.
  • Choose the pillar that best represents the purpose of your solution, not simply the technologies you use.

Who Can Participate?

  • Students from any recognized institution are welcome.
  • Participants from all engineering, science, technology, design, management, and interdisciplinary backgrounds are encouraged.
  • Teams must follow the team size specified on the registration page.
  • Innovation thrives when diverse disciplines work together.

What Can You Build?

We welcome projects across a wide range of domains, including but not limited to:

  • Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning
  • Embedded Systems & Electronics
  • Internet of Things (IoT)
  • Robotics & Automation
  • Wireless Communication Systems
  • Healthcare & Medical Technologies
  • Renewable Energy
  • Smart Infrastructure
  • Disaster Management
  • Cybersecurity
  • Space & Aerospace Technologies
  • Sustainability
  • Human-Centered Design
  • Frontier & Moonshot Innovations

If your solution contributes meaningfully to rebuilding civilization, it belongs here.

Submission Requirements:

Teams should be prepared to submit:

  • Project presentation
  • Technical documentation
  • Source code repository
  • Prototype or proof of concept
  • Demonstration video (if applicable)

Additional submission guidelines and templates will be shared with registered participants.

Evaluation:

Projects will be assessed on their overall contribution toward rebuilding civilization, including:

  • Innovation
  • Engineering excellence
  • Technical feasibility
  • Scalability
  • Societal impact
  • Resilience
  • Quality of presentation

The complete judging rubric is available in the attached documentation.

General Rules:

  • All submitted work must be original.
  • Open-source libraries, frameworks, APIs, and development tools may be used with proper attribution.
  • AI-assisted development is permitted unless otherwise specified.
  • Plagiarism or intellectual property violations will result in immediate disqualification.
  • Participants are expected to maintain professionalism and uphold the event's code of conduct.
  • Decisions made by the organizing committee and judging panel will be final.
  • A comprehensive rulebook is available in the attached resources.

Why Participate?

  • DAY ZERO is more than a competition.
  • It is an opportunity to think like the engineers who would shape the first generation of a new civilization.
  • Challenge assumptions.
  • Collaborate across disciplines.
  • Build technologies that matter.
  • Engineer systems that could redefine humanity's future.
  • Tomorrow Begins Here.
  • History remembers the civilizations that were built.
  • The next one starts with your idea.
