title: CAD Competition
problem_statement:
Competition Description:

  • Do you have the creativity, precision, and technical skills to transform an engineering idea into a 3D model under time pressure? Welcome to Speed Modelling, an exciting CAD challenge where engineering design meets speed and accuracy!
  • Participants will be given a mechanical component, reference image, or engineering drawing and must recreate its 3D model using CAD software within the allotted time. The challenge is to interpret the given reference, visualize the geometry, and construct an accurate digital model using appropriate modelling tools and techniques.
  • From basic geometric features to intricate mechanical components, every modelling operation counts. Participants will be evaluated on dimensional accuracy, geometric precision, modelling approach, and completion time.
  • Can you turn a design into a precise 3D model before the clock runs out?
  • Visualize. Model. Conquer!

Competition Format:

  • Participation: Individual
  • Duration: As specified by the organizers.
  • Software: CAD software specified by the organizers (e.g., CATIA, SolidWorks, or Fusion 360).
  • Challenge: Create a 3D model of the given mechanical component using the provided reference.
  • Evaluation: Dimensional accuracy, geometric precision, completeness, and time management.
  • Winning Criteria: Highest overall score based on modelling accuracy and completion.

Rules And Regulations:

  • Each participant must independently create the assigned 3D model using the designated CAD software.
  • A reference image, engineering drawing, or component geometry will be provided at the beginning of the competition.
  • Participants must complete the assigned model within the allotted time.
  • Only the CAD software and tools approved by the organizers may be used.
  • Participants must work independently. Collaboration, communication with other participants, or external assistance is prohibited.
  • Use of pre-existing CAD models, downloaded files, or ready-made templates for the assigned component is strictly prohibited.
  • Participants must save their work in the designated file format and submit it before the deadline.
  • The model must represent the given component accurately, including its major geometric features and dimensions.
  • Participants must not use mobile phones, the internet, or external references unless explicitly permitted.
  • Any technical issues must be immediately reported to the event coordinators.
  • The organizers’ decisions regarding evaluation, rule violations, and final results will be binding.

Judging Criteria:

Evaluation Parameter Weightage
Dimensional Accuracy 30%
Geometric Accuracy and Completeness 25%
Modelling Approach and Feature Utilization 20%
Time Management 15%
File Organization and Final Submission 10%
Total 100%

Winner Selection:

  • Participants will be ranked based on their cumulative scores across all evaluation parameters. The participant achieving the highest score in the final round will be declared the winner.
  • In case of a tie, the participant who completes the model with greater accuracy in lesser time may be given preference.

Prizes And Certificates:

  • Exciting prizes and certificates will be awarded to the winners, with certificates of participation for eligible participants.

What To Expect:

  • Get ready to test your engineering visualization, spatial reasoning, CAD proficiency, and design efficiency. This competition challenges you to transform two-dimensional references into accurate three-dimensional models while racing against time.
  • Every sketch, feature, dimension, and modelling operation matters!
  • Can you design with precision when every second counts?

title: Math Sprint
problem_statement:
No opponents, no luck: just you and the questions.

Math Sprint is a live online Maths challenge on Mind Race (mindrace.in). Everyone starts together and solves questions one by one, on their own. The questions adapt to you: get them right and they get harder; get stuck and they get easier. Everyone is tested at their own level, and the leaderboard shows who is really the strongest.

When: Saturday, 14 November · 8:00–9:00 PM IST
Subject: Mathematics
Where: Online at mindrace.in, on your phone or laptop
Entry: Free, individual

How to take part

  1. Register here on Unstop.
  2. Important: the event is played on Mind Race, so registering on Unstop alone is not enough. Before 14 Nov, create your free Mind Race account, verify your email and join the event here: mindrace.in/e/FXZNEG?ref=unstop (event code FXZNEG).
  3. At 8:00 PM, open the event and press Start.

How it works

  • Answer questions one at a time until 9:00 PM. Each question has its own timer, from 30 seconds for easy ones to 90 seconds for the hardest.
  • Attempt at least 75 questions to be ranked. Skips and time-outs count as attempts. That's under 48 seconds per question, so keep moving.
  • You're ranked by your Mind Score: the skill your answers prove. Hard questions solved count for more, and a careless mistake on an easy one costs a lot. Answering more makes your score more certain, not bigger, so accuracy beats rushing.
  • You can skip at most 1 question in 3. A skip counts as half a wrong answer, and the next question won't be easier.
  • The leaderboard freezes for the last 5 minutes. You can't start after 8:50 PM.

Prizes

  • ₹200 · ₹150 · ₹100 Amazon vouchers
  • A certificate of participation for everyone who attempts 75 questions

Fair play Solve it yourself: no calculator, AI, search engine or help from anyone. One player, one account, one device. We check the timing and accuracy of every answer. Before winners are announced, top players may be asked to solve a few questions live on Google Meet with camera, mic and screen sharing on. Anyone caught cheating loses their result and prize and is banned from Mind Race for 3 days.

title: ANAVRAN - The Sustainability Event Of Xaviesta 5.0
organizer: Xavier Business School (XBS), St. Xavier's University, Kolkata
venue_address: St. Xavier's University, Kolkata Plot No. III - B/1, Action Area III B Newtown, Kolkata - 700160
problem_statement:
ANAVARAN, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is an immersive sustainability investigation and strategy competition that challenges participants to uncover the gap between corporate sustainability claims and ground realities. Teams of four step into the roles of Sustainability Investigators and Corporate Strategists, investigating Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd., a fictional organisation whose green image may not reflect its actual environmental and social impact. Across three challenging rounds, participants will identify greenwashing, investigate hidden contradictions, assess business risks and develop commercially viable sustainability strategies under real-world-inspired crises. From questioning environmental claims to defending strategic decisions before a jury, ANAVARAN tests critical thinking, ESG awareness, analytical ability and the power to build a genuinely sustainable future.

ROUND 1 – GREEN OR GREENWASH?

Spot the Illusion

  • Teams will receive a collection of fictional ESG claims, advertisements, sustainability statements, corporate announcements and certification claims made by Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. regarding its proposed Hooghly Data Park in West Bengal.
  • Participants must critically examine each of the 10 claims and classify them into one of three categories:

  • Genuine Sustainability

  • Greenwashing

  • Misleading Communication

Each classification must be supported by a short justification explaining what is being promised, whether the claim is verifiable, what important information is missing and whether the communication creates an exaggerated positive impression.

Round Details:

  • Mode: Online on Unstop.

  • Format: ESG Claim Classification + Justification Brief.

  • Case: Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd. – Hooghly Data Park.

  • Number of Claims: 10.

  • Submission: Each claim must include its classification and a justification of 3–6 lines.

  • Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Classification Accuracy – 50%

  • Quality of Justification – 40%

  • Clarity of Expression – 10%

ROUND 2 – THE GREENWASH FILES

Uncover the Truth

  • The qualifying teams will receive a comprehensive investigation dossier containing public statements, internal technical documents, employment projections, renewable energy plans, community partnership updates and environmental assessments relating to Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd.
  • Teams must investigate the contradictions between the company's public sustainability commitments and its internal operational realities.
  • Participants must identify instances of greenwashing, uncover misleading disclosures, assess environmental and social implications, and evaluate the financial, regulatory and reputational risks arising from these gaps.
  • Teams will present their investigation findings and risk assessment before the jury.

Round Details:

  • Mode: Offline.

  • Timing: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM (as specified in the event brochure).

  • Format: Case Investigation + Jury Findings Presentation.

  • Case: Detailed investigation of Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd.'s Hooghly Data Park.

  • Qualification: Top 6 Teams advance to Round 3 (Grand Finale).

Key Areas of Investigation:

  • Water consumption, groundwater stress and water-positive claims.

  • Renewable energy commitments and net-zero targets.

  • Employment claims and actual local job creation.

  • Farmer partnerships and treated wastewater utilisation.

  • Green certifications and environmental compliance.

  • Financial, regulatory, reputational and social risks.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Completeness of Findings – 30%

  • Quality of Risk Assessment – 30%

  • Systems Thinking – 20%

  • Presentation & Clarity – 20%

ROUND 3 – THE REBUILT GREEN LEGACY

Shape the Future – Grand Finale

  • The six finalist teams will face individual sustainability crises based on the specific findings they uncovered during Round 2. Each team must step into the role of a Special Recovery Cell appointed by the Board of Vasundhara Data Infrastructure Ltd.
  • Participants must develop a credible and commercially viable sustainability recovery strategy addressing the crisis assigned to their team. The strategy must demonstrate how the organisation can stabilise its current situation, repair stakeholder relationships, rebuild its sustainability framework and establish measurable commitments for the future.
  • Teams must present their strategy before the jury and defend their recommendations through a live presentation and cross-examination.

Round Details:

  • Mode: Offline – Live Defence, Grand Finale.

  • Format: Crisis-Driven Strategy Design + Live Presentation & Defence.

  • Finalists: Top 6 Teams from Round 2.

  • Preparation: Closed-book, using Round 2 notes saved on the team laptop, the Round 3 pack and the Benchmark Card.

Mandatory Strategic Framework – Four Horizons:

  • STABILISE: Address the immediate crisis and minimise operational, financial and reputational damage.

  • REPAIR: Correct past shortcomings, rebuild stakeholder trust and address existing sustainability gaps.

  • REBUILD: Design a commercially viable and long-term sustainability strategy.

  • PROVE: Establish measurable targets, accountability mechanisms and independent verification to demonstrate actual progress.

Submission Requirements:

  • Strategy deck: Maximum 8 main slides plus 2 appendix slides.

  • Commitments Ledger: One-page document containing commitment, baseline, target, date, owner, cost, funding source and verification method.

  • Financial View: Cost by strategic horizon, funding route, impact on lender covenant and value at risk avoided.

Presentation Format:

  • Pitch: 8 minutes (strict time limit).

  • Jury Q&A: 8 minutes.

  • A new Board-level development will be introduced at the beginning of the Q&A, requiring teams to respond immediately.

  • Any team member may answer questions.

Evaluation Criteria:

  • Quality of Strategy – 30%

  • Commercial Feasibility – 25%

  • Crisis Response & Adaptability – 20%

  • Innovation & Systems View – 15%

  • Live Defence & Communication – 10%

OVERALL RULES & REGULATIONS

  • Team Size: Each team must consist of exactly 4 members across all three rounds. No substitutions will be permitted once registration is completed.

  • Eligibility: The competition is open to all college students. Valid institutional ID cards are mandatory for offline rounds.

  • Competition Structure: Round 1 (Online) → Top 12 teams advance to Round 2 (Offline) → Top 6 teams advance to Round 3 (Offline Grand Finale).

  • Offline Timing: The offline rounds are scheduled within the 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM window on the finale day, as specified in the ANAVARAN Event Brochure. The venue will be communicated to shortlisted teams.

  • Continuity: Findings from Round 2 will directly shape the specific crisis assigned to each finalist in Round 3. Teams cannot reset their position or disregard their earlier findings.

  • Round 1 Integrity: Participants must base their classifications on the provided materials. AI tools may be used only for language polishing and not for generating the actual classifications.

  • Devices: One laptop per team is permitted for preparation and presentation during offline rounds. Mobile phones are strictly prohibited during offline rounds.

  • Submissions: All submissions must follow the prescribed format and be submitted through the official channel within the stipulated deadline. Late entries and resubmissions will not be accepted.

  • Conduct: No communication or collaboration between competing teams is permitted during any round. Violation will lead to disqualification.

  • Round 3 Preparation: Participants must use their Round 2 notes, the provided crisis brief and the Benchmark Card. Assumptions must be clearly identified, and unsupported figures must not be presented as facts.

  • Commitments Ledger: Every commitment made during the Round 3 presentation must be included in the prescribed Commitments Ledger with its baseline, target, timeline, owner, cost, funding source and verification method.

  • Judging: The decisions of the judges and organising committee are final and binding at every stage.

  • Organisers' Rights: The organising committee reserves the right to modify the rules, timelines or competition format if required, with prior notice to participants.

title: KaalDrishti - The BA Event Of Xaviesta 5.0
organizer: Xavier Business School (XBS), St. Xavier's University, Kolkata

problem_statement:
KaalDrishti, presented as part of XAVIESTA 5.0 – KAALCHAKRA, is a business analytics competition that challenges participants to step into the role of Data Investigators and uncover the truth behind a company's crisis. Teams of four will work with fragmented financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business information to identify hidden patterns, detect anomalies and establish the real cause of a problem. Across three challenging rounds, participants will investigate an unsolved business crisis, tackle analytical challenges and defend their conclusions through hypothesis testing and a live boardroom presentation. The event tests analytical thinking, data interpretation, statistical reasoning, problem-solving and the ability to convert data into meaningful business decisions.

ROUND 1 – THE CRIME SCENE: FIND THE STORY

Project Mirage – Uncover the Hidden Truth

  • Participants will receive a business scenario, problem statement and relevant datasets. The case file will contain fragmented information such as financial records, internal communications, customer data and other business evidence.
  • Teams must independently understand the situation, identify relevant patterns and anomalies, determine the root cause of the crisis and develop a hypothesis explaining what went wrong and why.
  • Based on their analysis, teams must propose feasible business solutions while complying with the given constraints.

Round Details:

  • Mode: Online on Unstop

  • Format: Open-Ended Data Investigation + Written Hypothesis Brief

  • Submission: PDF deck of maximum 10 pages, excluding the Introduction and Closing slides.

  • Qualification: Top 12 Teams advance to Round 2.

  • Evaluation Criteria:

    • Understanding of the problem and root cause analysis.

    • Analytical rigour specific to the dataset.

    • Methodology adopted.

    • Feasibility and quality of the proposed business solution.

ROUND 2 – THE LOCKED DATA: UNLOCK THE EVIDENCE

Xcelerate – Excel E-Sports

  • The qualifying teams will enter an analytical challenge where they will be provided with a dataset and a problem statement. Participants must analyse the given information and develop an optimised solution or analytical model according to the requirements.
  • Teams will be required to demonstrate their analytical capabilities using Microsoft Excel. They can use Excel charts, VBA, Macros and other Excel plugins to develop and present their solutions. However, the final solution must be presented entirely in Excel.
  • The methodology adopted and the plugins used must be explicitly mentioned.

Round Details:

  • Mode: Offline

  • Format: Dataset-Based Analytical Modelling and Excel Challenge.

  • Tools: Microsoft Excel, Excel Charts, VBA, Macros and other Excel plugins.

  • Submission/Presentation: The solution must be presented in Excel only.

  • Qualification: Top 5 Teams advance to Round 3.

  • Evaluation Focus:

    • Analytical reasoning.

    • Data interpretation and modelling.

    • Problem-solving ability.

    • Efficiency and accuracy of the solution.

    • Methodology and effective use of Excel tools.

ROUND 3 – THE FALSE TRAIL & THE BOARDROOM TRIAL: DELIVER THE VERDICT

Find the Real Cause. Defend It Under Fire.

  • The finalists will be presented with multiple plausible explanations for the company's crisis, each supported by a different set of evidence. Only one explanation will represent the actual cause.
  • Teams must test each hypothesis against the evidence collected in the earlier rounds, identify explanations based on bias, false correlation or manipulated data, and trace the crisis back to its Point of No Return — the exact past decision that set the crisis in motion.
  • Participants will then present their final verdict and business recommendations before a jury acting as the company's Board, which will cross-examine their assumptions and conclusions.

    • Methodology adopted.

    • Feasibility and quality of business solutions.

    • Causal reasoning and data validation.

    • Hypothesis testing and business judgement.

    • Boardroom communication and ability to defend conclusions.

problem_statement:
Overview

YUGANTAR, presented by FINNOVATION as part of XAVIESTA 5.0, is an immersive marketing strategy competition that challenges participants to rewrite the destiny of a fictional Indian footwear brand. Through three interconnected rounds, teams will investigate the brand's history, uncover the strategic decision behind its downfall, rewrite a defining moment in its journey, and navigate the consequences of their choices. From analysing fragmented evidence and developing revised marketing strategies to tackling real-time marketing crises, participants must demonstrate their consumer understanding, analytical thinking, creativity and strategic decision-making. Here, every decision shapes the future, and every consequence tells a story.

Round 1 – The Archive

Decode the Brand

Teams will receive a fragmented case archive containing old advertisements, consumer reviews, sales data, competitor movements, internal memos and market research relating to Kadam Footwear, a fictional Indian footwear brand.

Participants must reconstruct the brand's timeline, identify the single strategic decision that changed its destiny and support their conclusions with evidence from the provided documents.

Round Details:

  • Team Size: 4 Members
  • Mode: Online on Unstop
  • Format: Fragmented Evidence Reconstruction + Written Hypothesis Brief
  • Submission: One PDF containing:
    • Reconstructed timeline of 8–12 events in chronological order.
    • Hypothesis brief of maximum 500 words.
    • Supporting evidence with document references.
  • Qualification: Top 12 Teams
  • Evaluation: Timeline accuracy, identification of the turning-point decision, evidence-based analysis and critical thinking.

Round 2 – The Butterfly Effect

Rewrite the Past

The qualifying teams will get an opportunity to change one defining decision from Kadam Footwear's history. They must analyse how this single intervention could have altered the brand's journey, considering its impact on brand equity, market share, profit margins, competitive positioning and consumer perception.

Based on their revised historical scenario, teams must develop a coherent marketing strategy and justify the consequences of their chosen intervention.

Round Details:

  • Team Size: 4 Members
  • Mode: Offline
  • Format: Single-Decision Rewrite + Revised Strategy Brief
  • Challenge: Rewriting one historical decision and analysing its consequences.
  • Submission: Revised strategy brief.
  • Qualification: Top 6 Teams
  • Evaluation: Strategic coherence, consequence analysis, marketing strategy, positioning and decision-making.

Round 3 – The Present Break & Break the Chakra

Survive 2027, Then Choose the Future

The final round brings the consequences of each team's revised decision into the present. Each finalist will face a team-specific marketing crisis shaped by the changes introduced in Round 2.

Teams must allocate a limited marketing budget across digital marketing, influencers, product, retail, partnerships and consumer research to respond to the crisis. They will then face a CEO-level dilemma, choosing whether to Accept, Alter or Reset the brand's future direction.

The challenge concludes with a live boardroom presentation and jury cross-examination, where teams must defend their strategy and decisions.

  • Team Size: 4 Members
  • Mode: Offline – Live Defence
  • Format: Crisis Budget Allocation + CEO Dilemma + Jury Presentation & Cross-Examination

Weight Classes, Roster & Eligibility:

Every machine must pass formal technical inspection before competing. Weight limits are strictly enforced, with a maximum tolerance of 1%.

Weight Classes:

  • Featherweight: up to 8.0 kg (17.6 lbs)
  • Middleweight: up to 15.0 kg (33.0 lbs)
  • Heavyweight: up to 30.0 kg (66.0 lbs)

Roster & Structural Rules:

Team Roster: 2 to 6 registered members per team. Teams may include members from more than one college, provided everyone’s student credentials are verified.

Dimensions: there is no limit on overall dimensions. The fully assembled robot must fit through the 4 ft × 4 ft arena access hatch without disassembly.

Walker Bonus: robots using true non-wheeled linear walking mechanisms get an extra 10% weight allowance above their class limit.

Cluster Bots: a team may deploy multiple sub-units under one entry. The combined mass and dimensions of all active sub-units must stay within the class limits.

Technical, Power & Weapon Regulations:

Control Systems & Radio:

Radio Protocol: 2.4 GHz digital spread-spectrum systems with frequency-hopping channels.

Prohibited Control: tethered remote connections and fully autonomous robots are strictly prohibited.

Fail-Safe Requirement: all drive systems and weapon throttles must return to neutral/zero power immediately if the transmitter signal is lost or interrupted.

Electrical Power & Battery Shielding:

Voltage Cap: electric drive systems only. The potential between any two electrical points must not exceed 36 V DC.

Engines: internal combustion engines (ICE) are banned.

Battery Containment: every LiPo, LiFe or gel battery cell must be fully enclosed in a rigid enclosure of at least 2 mm steel or aluminium plate, to contain thermal runaway.

Mobility & Weapons:

Allowed Mobility:

  • Wheels
  • Treads
  • Walking mechanisms
  • Controlled hopping assemblies (maximum height clearance of 6 ft)

Prohibited Mobility:

  • Vacuum pads
  • Magnetic locks onto the arena floor
  • Sticky treads
  • Chemical adhesives
  • Flight components

Permitted Weapons:

  • Vertical and horizontal kinetic spinners and drums
  • Pneumatic flippers
  • Overhead hammers
  • Lifters
  • Hydraulic clamps
  • Low-pressure regulated flamethrowers

Banned Weapons:

  • Liquid sprayers
  • High-voltage tasers
  • Untethered projectiles
  • Entangling nets or ropes
  • Radio signal jammers
  • Explosive charges

Weapon Spin-Down: every high-kinetic-energy spinning weapon must come to a complete stop within 60 seconds of signal cut-off or activation of the emergency stop switch.

Tournament Structure & Match Phases:

Phase 1: Tech Check & Safety Inspection:

Safety Verification: a robot is cleared to fight only after a mandatory check of:

  • Fail-safe operation
  • Battery containment
  • Wire gauge and insulation
  • Structural integrity

Official Weigh-In: robots are weighed on certified event scales. A robot over the tolerance must be modified immediately and re-tested.

Pit Setup: each team gets a dedicated pit station with regulated charging and safety equipment for repairs between matches.

Phase 2: League Trials (Round-Robin Pool Stage):

Match Duration: 3 minutes per bout.

Pool Grouping: teams are split into groups for round-robin fixtures, with at least 2 to 3 matches per team.

Scoring:

  • TKO victory: 3 points
  • Judges’ decision victory: 2 points
  • Draw / tie: 1 point
  • Loss or disqualification: 0 points

Advancement: the top two teams by points in each pool advance to the Knockout Bracket.

Phase 3: Knockouts:

  • Single-elimination bracket format
  • 5 minutes per bout
  • The hazard pit opens during the final 60 seconds

Phase 4: Grand Finale:

  • The two finalists face off in a best-of-3 series.
  • Each bout is 5 minutes long.
  • If the series is tied 1–1, a final 3-minute Sudden Death Overtime round is played.

Victory Conditions, Judging & Conduct:

Match Outcomes & Arena Engagement:

Technical Knockout (TKO): declared if a robot cannot show controlled linear movement for 10 consecutive seconds when the referee asks.

Pinning Cap: clamping or pinning an opponent against the arena walls is limited to 15 seconds per occurrence. When the referee directs, the attacker must immediately back off by at least 3 ft.

Judges’ Criteria (11 points total):

  • Damage (5 points): structural and functional impact
  • Aggression (3 points): frequency and severity of direct attacks
  • Control (3 points): arena management and tactical positioning

Safety Regulations & Code of Conduct:

Pit Safety:

  • All power locks and weapon locks/pins must stay inserted at all times outside the battle arena.
  • Powering up active weapons inside the pit is strictly forbidden.

Sportsmanship: any of the following results in immediate team disqualification:

  • Unprofessional conduct
  • Verbal abuse toward officials
  • Deliberate arena destruction
  • Unsafe pit handling

Referee Authority: referees have final, unappealable authority over all match calls, TKO countdowns and safety disengagements.
prizes_summary: Cash prizes, certificates, official mentorship, and PPI hiring opportunities.

Overview

Welcome to Xcelerate 4.0, a high-energy, 3-day innovation marathon inclusive of a startup fair and a 24-hour ideathon, where innovation knows no limits. No restrictions, no boundaries, just pure creativity, collaboration, and the relentless drive to build something extraordinary. Whether you're shaping the next big startup, solving real-world challenges, or pushing the limits of your imagination, this is your playground.

This year, Xcelerate embraces "Open Innovation", giving participants the freedom to work on an idea of their choice in any sector. No predefined problem statements, just one challenge: bring your boldest vision to life.

Unlike hackathons, ideathons are open to everyone, even those with limited technical backgrounds. Here, you'll be evaluated on your entrepreneurial mindset, business acumen, and creativity, not just coding skills.

Competition Format

Round 1: Qualifying Round (Online Submission) :

Your journey starts with an online submission where you’ll present your idea through :

  • A basic presentation outlining your concept, target market, feasibility, and potential impact.
  • A short video (maximum 1 minute) delivering an elevator pitch about your product (optional).
  • Evaluation Criteria: Innovation, feasibility, scalability, and clarity of thought.
  • Only 50 teams will advance to the final round.

Round 2: The Grand Finale (Offline Round) :

The top 50 teams will take on the 24-hour challenge at Shiv Nadar University (Delhi NCR) on November 21st & 22nd, where they’ll refine their ideas and engage in challenges designed to test creativity, adaptability, and business acumen. 

Who Can Participate?

  • Open to individuals and teams (maximum 4 members per team).
  • Only college students are eligible. (Including undergraduates, students from 5-year integrated courses, and MBA programs.)
  • No fully developed idea? No problem. All you need is a strong vision and the drive to bring it to life.

Rules & Guidelines

  • Theme: Xcelerate 4.0 follows the theme of Open Innovation; participants have the freedom to select a problem statement from any sector.
  • Originality Matters: Submissions must be original and should not replicate existing products or businesses.
  • Fair Play: No plagiarism or AI-generated pitches are allowed. 
  • Consistency: The problem statement presented in the online round must be the same one pursued in the offline round (if qualified).
  • Presentation Standards: Final presentations must be clear, concise, and delivered within the allocated time.
  • Offline Round Details: Further information will be shared with qualified teams upon selection.

problem_statement:

Theme:

  • The Next Billion: Unlocking India's Untapped Markets and Consumers

Article Topics:

  • The Her Economy: Why Women in Bharat Are India's Most Underestimated Consumers
  • The Gig Wallet: How Informal Income Is Rewriting Credit and Consumption
  • The Language of Growth: Why India's Next Billion Will Speak Vernacular
  • ⁠The Trust Economy: Why Winning Bharat Requires More Than Competitive Pricing
  • Beyond Digital Access: Leveraging India's Digital Public Infrastructure to Create New Economic Opportunities
  • Reimagining the Last Mile: Building Scalable Business Models for India's Underserved Markets
  • Innovation at the Right Price: Rethinking Product Design for India's Value-Conscious Consumers
  • From Data to Demand: Using Consumer Analytics to Discover India's Hidden Markets
  • ⁠Mapping India's Next Growth Corridors: Identifying Emerging Consumer Markets Beyond Metros
  • Insuring the Uninsured: Why Micro-Insurance Keeps Failing on Distribution and Trust, and What an Embedded Model Could Fix

Rules and Guidelines:

  • The competition is for individuals/teams (1-2 members).
  • Choose any one of the above-given topics.

  • The article should be an original work of creation, and references should be mentioned wherever necessary. However, there is no limit to creativity.
  • Relevant graphs or data can be added to the article only if the participant makes them.
  • Text font size: 12, font style: Times New Roman, and page limit: 2 pages (standard A4 size on typical word processing software, e.g., MS Word), excluding infographics, charts, tables, and references. You are free to use any design tool such as Canva.

Rewards:

  • E-certificates for winners and runners-up, along with cash prizes.

All the best!

ROUND 3 – YUGPARIVARTAN

Shape the Future

title: Global Case Masters 2026
problem_statement:
Overview

Global Case Masters 2026, the inaugural edition of the international management case competition hosted by the International Relations Centre, IMT Ghaziabad, brings together students from universities and institutions across India and abroad.

Centered around the theme "Navigating Global Business Challenges," the competition provides participants with an opportunity to analyze a business situation, evaluate different alternatives, and develop practical solutions. It challenges teams to apply their classroom learning to business decisions while testing their analytical, strategic, and problem-solving abilities.

With participants competing on a common platform, Global Case Masters aims to encourage fresh perspectives, sound business judgment, and well-reasoned recommendations.

Case Brief: Aureon Mobility – Growth Across Borders

The competition will revolve around Aureon Mobility Group, a multinational automobile manufacturer operating across Asia, Europe and the Americas, with manufacturing facilities in India, Mexico and Poland.

As the company plans its next phase of international growth, it faces important decisions concerning market opportunities, manufacturing capacity, investment priorities and supply-chain risks.

Participants will take on the role of business advisors and develop a growth strategy for Aureon Mobility. They will need to evaluate the company's expansion options, decide where investments should be directed, and consider how it can manage international business risks while remaining profitable by 2030.

The challenge is to develop a clear, practical, and well-supported strategy that addresses the company's long-term business objectives.

General Guidelines and Eligibility

  • The competition is open to all undergraduate, postgraduate and PhD students pursuing a full-time degree at institutions in India or abroad.
  • Participants must be currently enrolled as full-time students at their respective institutions.
  • Students can register individually or in teams of 1–3 members.
  • Cross-college teams are not allowed. All members of a team must belong to the same institution.
  • An individual cannot be a member of more than one team.
  • Any deviation from the eligibility criteria or team formation guidelines may result in the disqualification of the entire team.

Competition Structure

The competition will be conducted in two online submission rounds.

Round 1: Preliminary Submission

  • Teams must submit a 2-slide PowerPoint presentation outlining their understanding of the case, the key challenges faced by Aureon Mobility and their proposed course of action.
  • The submission should clearly identify the major business issues and present the team's initial direction for addressing them.
  • Shortlisted teams will qualify for the next round.

Round 2: Detailed Presentation Submission

  • Shortlisted teams must submit a 4–5-slide PowerPoint presentation presenting their detailed business strategy.
  • The presentation should explain the key challenges, recommended growth strategy, reasoning behind the proposed decisions, and steps for implementation.
  • Teams are expected to consider relevant market opportunities, investment choices, international operations, and potential business risks.
  • Research and relevant information should be used to support the recommendations.

Submission Guidelines

  • The case document and submission instructions will be available on the Unstop competition page.
  • All submissions must be made in PowerPoint format through the respective round's submission link on Unstop.
  • The maximum permitted file size is 50 MB per submission.
  • The team leader must upload the final submission using the Submit option on the platform.
  • Submissions can be changed before the respective deadline by navigating to Submission → Change Submission.
  • No extensions will be provided beyond the announced submission deadlines.

Rewards and Recognition

Outstanding teams will be recognized for their analysis, strategic thinking, and proposed business solutions.

  • Winner: ₹12,000 cash prize
  • Runner-up: ₹8,000 cash prize

The prizes will be awarded by the International Relations Centre, IMT Ghaziabad.

Skills to Be Assessed

The competition will provide participants with an opportunity to demonstrate the following skills:

  • Analytical Thinking: Understanding the business situation, identifying key issues and examining relevant information.
  • Strategic Thinking: Developing a clear growth strategy while considering market opportunities and business conditions.
  • Problem-Solving: Identifying business challenges and suggesting practical solutions.
  • Business Understanding: Applying knowledge of how companies operate, compete and grow across different markets.
  • Decision-Making: Evaluating available alternatives and explaining the reasoning behind business decisions.
  • Research and Data Interpretation: Using relevant information and data to support recommendations.
  • Planning and Implementation: Outlining practical steps to execute the proposed strategy while considering resources and risks.
  • Communication and Presentation: Organizing ideas and presenting recommendations in a clear, structured and convincing manner.

Think Globally. Decide Strategically.

title: CASE CLOSED: THE POLICY CRIME SCENE
problem_statement:
Case Closed: The Policy Crime Scene puts you in the role of a Special Economic Forensics Officer investigating a fictional government programme that has gone wrong. Examine documents, crack codes, analyse financial records, connect conflicting statements and determine what actually happened. No specialist knowledge of economics or public policy is required. The challenge rewards observation, reasoning, teamwork and evidence-based conclusions.

A fictional government programme received an allocation of ₹100 crore to improve school infrastructure. Records show that ₹72 crore was spent, while several schools claim that promised equipment never arrived. Officials maintain that the programme was implemented successfully. Something does not add up. Your mission is to determine: Where did the implementation process break down? Which records contradict one another? What can the evidence establish - and what remains unverified? What is the most defensible explanation for the failure?

All figures, documents and allegations are fictional. A discrepancy alone does not prove fraud or establish individual wrongdoing.

Because blimps operate in a slow, buoyancy-dominated regime that is highly sensitive to control input, the competition tests both piloting precision and real-time combat strategy.

  • Team Size: Up to 3 members per team.
  • Participation Model: Open registration with an online technical check.

Competition Stages

1. Online Qualification Check

  • Every registered team must submit a single continuous, unedited video demonstrating basic flight competency.

  • This round is evaluated on a pass/fail basis to grant an on-site Day 1 slot.

2. Round 1: Precision Navigation

  • All blimps must pass a Day 1 technical check to ensure they meet limits, it must fit in a box of dimensions 1m * 0.5 m * 0.5m, helium gas only, a custom-built gondola, and a maximum total weight of 800 g.
  • Teams pilot their blimp through a 3D course of up to 10 suspended hoops within a 3-minute time limit.

3. Round 2: Aerial Combat (Grand Finale)

  • The top 6 teams compete in a bracket-based, single-duel tournament inside a netted arena.
  • The objective is to use a  5 cm standard pin to puncture the opponent's Mylar/BoPET envelope while protecting their own.
  • A duel is won when the opponent's envelope is visibly punctured and loses lift.

  • Build Rules: Envelopes must be commercially purchased, while the gondola and electronics must be built from scratch by the team.
  • Propulsion & Control: The blimp must use electric motors with propellers and be controlled via a 2.4 GHz RC; autonomous flight is not permitted.
  • Safety: Helium is the only permitted lifting gas; the use of hydrogen will result in strict and immediate disqualification.
  • Combat Conduct: Ramming with the gondola or contacting an opponent's electronics during combat is prohibited and leads to immediate disqualification.

title: Call for Papers: The Arthniti 2026-27
problem_statement:
About:

The Arthniti (ISSN: 2277-1344) is the official peer-reviewed research journal of the Department of Economics at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai. The journal features research papers and articles written by undergraduate students of economics and related disciplines. 

Every year, the journal publishes research on a specific theme, enriching the scope and suggesting a refreshing strand of thought to pick upon by the students every year across the disciplines of Economics, Finance, Political Science, Psychology, Technology, inter alia, and this year The Arthniti invites abstracts on the theme ‘Emergence’.

Theme:

Emergence is the process by which interactions among simple underlying components can give rise to complex behaviours and structures. Often, the ultimate outcome observed is neither intuitive nor reducible to those individual components. This theme looks at interdisciplinary ideas as emerging concepts that rarely respect the boundaries of a single field. 

Emergence therefore, is not merely change, but it further examines what change produces. An understanding of these processes is therefore imperative to not only navigating uncertainty but also building systems that are resilient to adapting for what comes next. This year, The Arthniti tries to capture the essence of its theme, ‘Emergence’ through diverse research papers.

Instructions:

This post is a call for paper submissions, that is, a complete research paper of up to 6000 words (excluding References and the Appendix) has to be submitted for the entry to be considered.

The paper submissions have to adhere to the following guidelines:

  1. All in-text citations, references, tables figures, and depictions to be in the American Psychological Association (APA) 7 format and accurately numbered. The font must be Times New Roman with font size as 12. 
  2. The paper must follow the following structure:

    • Abstract: A summary of the entire study, including the methods, findings and future outlook under 300 words.

    • Introduction: A brief overview of the background of your research study, a brief outline of the various fundamental elements that constitute the phenomenon you seek to explain.

    • Literature Review: A comprehensive review of literature surrounding the chosen subject, using any method of review.

    • Objectives: The various steps/methods/processes used as part of the study in answering the research question, in brief.

    • Hypothesis: The primary and secondary research questions that the author of the study seeks to answer, including the hypothesised relationship between the variables of the study.

    • Methodology: An exhaustive overview of the methods, datasets, models, processes that have been utilised in your research paper. 

    • Policy Recommendations (if applicable): Actionable and empirical policy implications of your study.

    • Limitations: A transparent declaration of the pitfalls that you encounter in the process, or any information that hampers the validity or scope of the claims being made by the study.

    • Conclusion: A brief summary of the study.

  3. Since the journal is ISSN-indexed, all submissions made must be exclusive to The Arthniti, and any duplicate papers will be regarded as plagiarism.
  4. The journal maintains stringent academic standards, and any plagiarism or AI-generated textual usage will lead to disqualification of the submission.

Note: Please submit your entries through this form link.

problem_statement:

Competition Description

Think you can communicate an engineering concept without saying a single word? Welcome to Guess & Sketch, a fun and engaging team challenge that combines mechanical knowledge, non-verbal communication, quick thinking, and drawing skills!

One team member will be shown the name or image of a mechanical component and must communicate it to their teammates using gestures and actions only. Speaking, writing, spelling, or revealing the component's name is strictly prohibited.

The remaining team members must identify the component and draw its diagram within the allotted time. From familiar machine elements to challenging mechanical components, every round tests how effectively a team can communicate, interpret, and visualize engineering concepts.

Can your team turn silent gestures into the perfect engineering sketch?

Competition Format

  • Participation: Team-based
  • Suggested Team Size: 3–4 members
  • Duration: 2–3 minutes per round
  • Materials Provided: Component prompts, paper, and drawing materials
  • Challenge: Identify the mechanical component and sketch its diagram
  • Winning Criteria: Highest score based on correct identification and drawing accuracy

Rules and Regulations

  • One team member will be designated as the performer and shown a mechanical component prompt.
  • The performer may communicate the component only through gestures, actions, and body movements.
  • Speaking, whispering, mouthing words, writing, drawing, or using objects to spell or reveal the component's name is prohibited.
  • Teammates must guess the component based on the performer's gestures.
  • Once the team identifies the component, they must draw its diagram on the provided paper within the time limit.

  • Teams must not use mobile phones, the internet, or external assistance.

Judging Criteria

  • Identification Accuracy: Correctly guessing the mechanical component.
  • Sketch Accuracy: Producing a recognizable diagram showing the component's essential shape and features.
  • Time Management: Completing both tasks within the allotted time.
  • Rule Compliance: Communicating exclusively through permitted gestures.

Winner Selection

The team with the highest cumulative score across the designated rounds will be declared the winner. In case of a tie, a sudden-death round with a challenging mechanical component may be conducted.

Prizes and Certificates

Exciting prizes and certificates will be awarded to the winning teams, with certificates of participation for eligible participants.

Get ready for a competition where engineering meets creativity! Test your mechanical knowledge, decode gestures, think on your feet, and transform ideas into sketches. Whether it's a gear, crankshaft, bearing, or complex machine element, your team's coordination will make all the difference.

No words. No hints. Just gestures, guesses, and great sketches!

Breaking into markets is competitive. Whether you're interested in Sales & Trading, Equity Research, Asset Management, Hedge Funds, Quant, FinTech, or investing roles, knowing the markets is only part of the equation.

You also need to be able to demonstrate how you think.

  • Every participant covers the same 5 Nifty Midcap 100 stocks.

  • No essays. No subjective judging. No popularity contest.
  • Your calls. Your conviction. Your results.

Week 8  Format:

  • Same 5 stocks for everyone.
  • 5 prediction opportunities each trading day.
  • 25 market calls across 5 days.
  • Rankings based on accuracy and conviction.
  • No long-form submissions required.

Higher confidence on a correct prediction can earn you a higher score. Right direction gets you started. Conviction sets you apart.

Why Participate:

Anyone can write “passionate about financial markets” on a résumé. It is far more compelling to discuss real market calls you made before the outcome was known, where you were right, where you were wrong, and how strongly you believed each view.

Through the challenge, you can:

  • Build a measurable record of your market judgment.
  • Earn an IndiaStox digital certificate for LinkedIn, résumés, and internship applications.
  • Create substantive material to discuss in interviews and networking conversations.
  • Practice forming views, expressing conviction, and evaluating decisions against real outcomes.
  • Begin building a longer-term IndiaStox market track record.
  • Compete against students and aspiring finance professionals across India.

How it works:

  • The challenge runs from Nov 2 - 6, 2026.
  • The same 5 Nifty Midcap 100 stocks remain fixed throughout the week.
  • Each trading day, predict Up or Down for the stocks you want to call.
  • Set your confidence level from 1% to 100% with each prediction.
  • Submit before 1:00 PM IST for that trading day's close.
  • Predictions are resolved after the market closes.
  • Your score reflects the accuracy and conviction behind your calls.
  • The leaderboard updates as results come in.

Everyone faces the same securities and the same market outcomes, so your performance comes down to the quality of your judgment.

Simple Timing Rule:

  • If you vote before 1:00 PM IST, your prediction applies to that day's close and is measured against the previous trading day's close.
  • If you enter through the initial participation flow after 1:00 PM IST, your prediction moves to the next available trading day.
  • In short: Before 1:00 PM = today's prediction. After 1:00 PM = next available trading day's prediction.

title: Drishti '26 — Article Writing Competition
organizer: Pannalal Girdharlal Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (PGDAV) College, University of Delhi (DU), Delhi
problem_statement:
About the Competition

Ecolibrium, the Economics Society of PGDAV (M) College, presents Drishti '26, its inaugural Article Writing Competition, inviting undergraduate and postgraduate students to examine the forces shaping the global economy critically. Centred around the theme “The Economics of Power in the 21st Century”, the competition encourages participants to explore how nations, corporations, institutions and individuals exercise economic influence through trade, technology, finance, resources and labour.

The competition aims to foster original thinking, rigorous economic analysis, and informed perspectives on contemporary global developments. Winning entries will be considered for publication in Arthavistaar, Ecolibrium’s annual economics newsletter.

1. Eligibility & Participation

  • Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students across colleges and universities.
  • Individual and team submissions of up to two members are permitted.
  • Each participant/team may submit only one article. Inter-college collaborations are allowed.

2. Theme & Choice of Topic

Participants may choose a topic within the following themes or combine multiple themes in their article.

  • Trade & the New Globalisation: Tariffs, protectionism, trade wars, global supply chains, reshoring, friend-shoring and shifting patterns of global economic power.
  • The State of War: Economic consequences of armed conflict, military expenditure, inflation, trade disruptions, wartime economies and post-war reconstruction.
  • Economic Warfare: Sanctions, embargoes, export controls and the use of trade, finance, energy and currencies as instruments of geopolitical influence.
  • Technology, AI & Corporate Power: Artificial intelligence, technological competition, Big Tech, market concentration, productivity, employment and the distribution of technological gains.
  • Resources, Energy & the Green Transition: Energy security, critical minerals, resource dependence, the petrodollar system, greenflation and the economics of sustainable development.
  • Labour, Inequality & Economic Security: Wages, labour markets, bargaining power, income and wealth inequality, social protection and the distribution of economic gains.

Topics listed above are indicative rather than exhaustive. Articles should demonstrate a clear economic perspective and engage critically with the chosen subject.

3. Article Specifications & Submission Guidelines

  • Word limit: 1,200–1,500 words 
  • Language: English
  • Formatting: Times New Roman, 12-point font. Submissions must be in Microsoft Word (.doc/.docx) format.
  • Author details: Include the article title, author(s)’ name(s), college/university, and contact information.
  • File naming: ParticipantName_CollegeName or TeamName_CollegeName
  • Structure: Articles should have a clear title, coherent arguments, appropriate section headings wherever necessary, and a well-developed conclusion.
  • Tables and figures: All tables, graphs, figures, and images must be properly sourced, with due credit given to the original creators. Sources must be clearly cited. Images used in the article must also be submitted as separate, high-resolution files along with the article via email to ensure print quality. Captions and references for visual materials will not be counted towards the word limit.
  • Language and styling: Italicise and explain non-English terms. Bold formatting may be used for emphasis, and superscripts or asterisks must be explained in footnotes.
  • Referencing: APA style referencing is mandatory. All external sources, quotations, statistics, datasets, and borrowed ideas must be properly acknowledged.

4. Originality & Academic Integrity

  • All submissions must be original, independently written, and previously unpublished.
  • Plagiarism, fabricated data, misrepresentation of authorship, and AI-generated content are strictly prohibited.

The organising committee reserves the right to verify originality and disqualify entries that violate these requirements.

5. Evaluation Criteria

Submissions will be evaluated on the following parameters:

  • Originality & Innovation 
  • Depth of Economic Analysis 
  • Research & Evidence
  • Structure & Coherence 
  • Conclusion & Recommendations

6. Submission Rules

  • Articles (& Images) must be submitted through the official email before the announced deadline:
    ecolibrium@pgdav.du.ac.in
  • Late submissions and entries that do not comply with the prescribed guidelines may be rejected.
  • Participants must ensure that all submitted information is accurate.

7. Prizes & Publication

Winning entries will receive exciting prizes and will be considered for publication in Arthavistaar, Ecolibrium’s annual economics newsletter. Authors will receive due credit and retain ownership of their original work while granting Ecolibrium permission to publish selected articles with appropriate attribution. The editorial team reserves the right to make edits for clarity, coherence, and factual accuracy while retaining the author's intended meaning.

8. General Rules

  • The organising committee reserves the right to resolve unforeseen issues and disqualify entries that violate the guidelines.
  • The judges' and organising committee's decision shall be final.

9. Important Dates

  • Registration Deadline: 10 November, 2026
  • Article Submission Deadline: 20 November, 2026

For queries or clarifications, participants may contact the Ecolibrium organising team through the official communication channels.

  • Fill in the Blanks: +3 for correct answers.

The final round consists of 3–4 mandatory engineering challenges and one elective challenge selected by each team. Datasheets and documentation for active components will be shared beforehand.

Evaluation will consider functionality, component efficiency, solution optimisation, implementation creativity, and edge-case handling.

Rules and Guidelines

title: Reverse Engineering Challenge

problem_statement:

Competitors will face a series of hands-on tasks that test their ability to understand, fix, and improve incomplete or faulty circuits. Covering a wide range of electrical engineering topics, this event encourages creative thinking and strengthens problem-solving skills. Participants will work through detailed scenarios to find hidden problems and create effective solutions, all while competing for the top position in this engaging and challenging competition.

Description: Conducted by Elecfest as part of Shaastra, IIT Madras' annual tech festival, the Reverse Engineering Challenge tests participants' ability to debug and complete incomplete electronic circuits to achieve desired functions.

  • The participants will be tested on key concepts from digital, analog, embedded and signal processing domains. Participants can earn a certificate from one of India's biggest annual tech festivals, certified by ISO 9001:2015.

title: Signal Quest
problem_statement:

From uncovering hidden frequencies and exploring Fourier transforms to mastering sampling techniques and designing digital filters, get ready to tackle challenges that go beyond the basics. Analyse signals, work through system behaviour, and put your problem solving skills to the test with applications in audio and video processing.

title: Godstockss Website Upgrade Challenge
problem_statement:
GODSTOCKSS Website Upgrade Challenge

GODSTOCKSS invites students, developers, designers, traders, and creative thinkers to participate in the Website Upgrade Challenge and share innovative ideas to improve the GODSTOCKSS website.

Rewards and Recognition

  • 1st Prize: ₹5,000 cash prize for the top-performing participant.
  • Participation Certificate: All eligible participants who participate in the challenge will receive a participation certificate.

Challenge Tasks

Participants must submit at least 5 suggestions to improve the GODSTOCKSS website. Suggestions can cover any relevant area, including:

  • Website design, UI/UX, and responsiveness.
  • New features and functionality.
  • User experience and navigation.
  • Website performance and usability.
  • Innovative ideas to improve the platform.

Optional Trading Strategy Submission

Participants who have developed a trading strategy may also submit it along with backtesting proof. Supporting evidence can include backtesting reports, screenshots, trade history, and performance statistics.

Trading strategies are optional. Participants can submit website improvement ideas without having any trading knowledge.

How to Participate

  • Prepare at least 5 suggestions for improving the GODSTOCKSS website.
  • Explain each suggestion clearly and describe its potential benefits.
  • Optionally include a trading strategy with supporting backtesting evidence.
  • Email your complete submission to godstockss@gmail.com.
  • Use the email subject: Website Upgrade Challenge – Your Name.

Rules and Guidelines

  • Suggestions must be original, practical, and relevant.
  • Participants may submit their answers in any clear written format.
  • AI tools may be used for assistance, but participants should understand their submissions.
  • Any trading strategy submitted must include genuine backtesting evidence to support its claims.
  • Participants should not submit copied work or unauthorized third-party data.

Evaluation Process

The GODSTOCKSS team will evaluate submissions based on originality, creativity, practicality, clarity, and potential impact on the website. Trading strategies, if submitted, will be assessed separately based on the quality of backtesting evidence and methodology.

The participant with the strongest overall submission will be selected as the winner and awarded ₹5,000.

title: LivingLab 2026
problem_statement:
LivingLab 2026 | E-Summit IIT Bombay

Where Products Get Proven

About LivingLab

  • LivingLab 2026 is a specialised showcase within the Startup Expo at E-Summit IIT Bombay, organised by the Entrepreneurship Cell, IIT Bombay.
  • Dedicated to innovative, research-driven and product-based startups, LivingLab provides a platform for startups with a working prototype or market-ready product to showcase their innovations to a large and diverse audience.
  • With access to 50,000+ attendees, including industry professionals, potential customers, investors and ecosystem leaders, LivingLab offers startups an opportunity to demonstrate their products, gain real-world feedback, explore investment opportunities and validate their products in a dynamic market.
  • LivingLab bridges the gap between groundbreaking innovation and real-world adoption.

Who Can Apply?

  • LivingLab is exclusively designed for product-based startups.
  • Eligible applicants should:
    • Be a product-based startup developing an innovative solution.
    • Have a working prototype or a market-ready product.
    • Have a product that can be demonstrated or showcased at the event.
    • Be interested in industry validation, customer discovery, investor exposure and product-market insights.

    • Customer Discovery: Interact with potential customers and understand their needs.
    • Investor Exposure: Explore investment opportunities and connect with investors.
    • Product-Market Insights: Gather feedback and insights to improve product positioning and market readiness.

    • Interaction with domain investors and professors of IIT Bombay.
    • Opportunity for visits by E-Summit speakers.

  • Register: Submit your application through the LivingLab registration portal.

title: Stocks Sena AlphaQuest 2026
problem_statement:
Overview:

Are you interested in stock markets, trading strategies, and financial research? Here's your opportunity to put your knowledge to the test!

Stocks Sena AlphaQuest 2026 is a pan-India competition designed for students passionate about financial markets, trading, and investment research. Organized by Stocks Sena, the competition challenges participants to test their knowledge, explore financial research tools, and experiment with trading strategies.

About Stocks Sena:

Stocks Sena is a stock market research platform built to make financial research more accessible and comprehensive. It brings together company financials, market-related news, portfolio tracking, and research tools to help users explore listed companies and financial markets.

Discover Backtest Lab:

One of the key features of Stocks Sena is Backtest Lab, which allows users to define trading strategy parameters and generate backtest reports showing how those strategies would have performed over a selected historical period.

Participants can experiment with different parameters, evaluate historical strategy performance, and gain practical exposure to systematic trading strategy analysis.

Competition Structure:

The competition consists of three rounds:

Round 1: Financial Markets Quiz

Test your understanding of financial markets, fundamental analysis, valuation, technical analysis, and investing concepts.

Round 2: The Stocks Sena Advantage Challenge

Explore Stocks Sena's features and demonstrate your understanding of how the platform can support financial research and market analysis.

Round 3: Backtest Lab Challenge

Use Stocks Sena's Backtest Lab to test a trading strategy over a specified historical period and submit your results for evaluation.

Cash Prizes:

Compete for a total national cash prize pool of ₹15,000.

  • All-India Rank 1: ₹10,000
  • All-India Rank 2: ₹3,000
  • All-India Rank 3: ₹2,000

National podium finishers may be considered for potential internship opportunities with Stocks Sena, based on their performance, skills, and the company's requirements.

This is an opportunity to showcase your understanding of financial markets, analytical abilities, and interest in financial research and technology.

Who Can Participate?

Students from colleges and universities across India who are interested in stock markets, financial research, investing, or trading strategies are encouraged to participate.

Whether you're beginning your journey in financial markets or already have experience analyzing companies and trading strategies, AlphaQuest offers an opportunity to learn, experiment, and compete.

Participants who meet the competition's participation requirements will receive a digital participation certificate.

Join the Challenge:

Explore the markets. Test your strategies. Compete with the best student talent across India.

title: Campus Ambassador Programme'26 | E-Cell IBS Hyderabad
problem_statement:
About the Program

For seven months, you’ll help bring E-Cell, IBS Hyderabad’s entrepreneurship events and learning opportunities to your campus. You’ll have a mentor to guide you and practical learning modules to work through as you go. The program is free, takes only a few hours a week, and can fit around your classes. You don’t need to have been an ambassador before.

What You’ll Do

  • Let students on your campus know about E-Cell events, competitions, and learning opportunities.
  • Help classmates find activities they’re interested in and encourage them to get involved.
  • Get to know the clubs, departments, and student groups that make up your campus community.
  • Help spread the word about entrepreneurship sessions, meet-ups, and events at your institution.
  • Stay connected with your mentor, keep track of what you’ve done, and share what students on your campus are saying.

How the Program Benefits You

  • Pick up useful skills. The learning modules cover personal branding and LinkedIn, social media and community growth, AI tools, marketing, sales, public speaking, and pitching. You’ll have chances to put those ideas into practice.
  • Build experience you can talk about. You’ll have real outreach, event promotion, and community-building work to draw on when you update your CV or talk about yourself in applications and interviews.
  • Meet people beyond your campus. Connect with student leaders at other colleges and get opportunities to meet founders, venture capitalists, and industry professionals.
  • Get support as you go. Your mentor can help you find your feet, and you’ll get to take part in E-Cell initiatives. There may also be opportunities to be featured on E-Cell’s social media.
  • Have something to show for your effort. You’ll receive a Campus Ambassador kit with an official badge, customised pen, and E-Cell booklet. If you complete the program and meet the credit requirement, you’ll receive a certificate. A Letter of Recommendation is also listed among the program’s recognition benefits.

Cash Awards for Top Performers

The top three performers receive cash awards—so consistent effort can bring both experience and a prize.

1ST PLACE
 ₹7,000

2ND PLACE
 ₹5,000

3RD PLACE
 ₹3,000

The team considers event registrations, campus activity, assigned tasks, social media outreach, and consistency. Selected ambassadors will receive the full credit system during onboarding.

Who Should Apply?

If you’re currently enrolled at a college or university in India, you can apply. This program may suit you if you’re curious about startups, enjoy meeting people, or want to feel more at ease with communication, leadership, or marketing. No ambassador experience is needed—showing up, being reliable, and following through are a great start.

How to Make the Most of the Program

  • Follow through on the outreach you take on, even when it’s a small task.
  • Try out what you learn in the modules—in your campus activities, conversations, and future work.
  • Keep your mentor in the loop and stay on top of your assigned tasks.
  • Build real connections and share information you’ve confirmed with E-Cell.
  • Think about what would make the program genuinely useful for students at your college.

Application Process

  • Fill in the application through the official Unstop listing.
  • The E-Cell team will review applications and shortlist candidates.
  • If you’re shortlisted, you’ll be invited to a brief interview.
  • Selected ambassadors will receive onboarding details, mentor support, and their Campus Ambassador kit.

Check the email address you registered with for application and onboarding updates.

A Few Ways to Meet the E-Cell Community

As an ambassador, you’ll help classmates find out about E-Cell’s events and learning opportunities. Here are a few of the experiences you can introduce them to:

Entrexpo - Startup Showcase
 Entrexpo is E-Cell’s startup showcase. Student founders set up stalls to show their products and sell directly to real customers. The latest edition featured 29 student startups and welcomed 2,000+ visitors, with outreach to 38+ colleges, including IIT Madras, BITS Hyderabad, and GITAM.

 E-Summit is a three-day summit about entrepreneurship, bringing students together to learn, compete, and meet people from the startup ecosystem. The latest edition saw 230+ registrations from 18 states, five competitions, venture capitalist judges, and a prize pool of ₹1 lakh+. At Pitch Fest, student founders get to present to VCs and hear their feedback.

title: ProdMad 6.0: Product Management Case Competition
problem_statement:
Presented by: bITeSys – The Business & Technology Club of IIM Shillong

“The journey of discovery begins not with finding new lands, but with seeing with new eyes.” — Marcel Proust

Overview

bITeSys – The Business & Technology Club of IIM Shillong proudly presents ProdMad 6.0 – ROOTS, the sixth edition of its flagship Product Management Case Competition.

This year, the journey leads to a village deep in the mountains of Northeast India, where the network is slow, the devices are few and the budget is small. The people hold generations of knowledge in their farms, crafts and stories. Participants must design a product, service, device or experience that meaningfully improves education for the village’s children. It has to be built within the village’s reality, work with limited connectivity, rely on open-source AI, and draw on the knowledge that already lives in the community.

Event Journey

Round 1 – Reading the Land (Quiz)
The journey begins! Take on a rapid-fire online quiz built to test your grasp of product thinking, user empathy, design frameworks and real-world problem solving. From product strategy to creative logic, every question brings you closer to the heart of the village.

Round 2 – Grow the Roots (Case Submission)
You’ve read the land, now it’s time to plant.

Shortlisted teams receive the ROOTS case: design a product, service or experience that improves education for the children of a mountain village with slow internet, few devices and a small budget. Your solution must work offline, run on open-source AI and draw on the village’s own knowledge.

Present your idea in a 9-10 slide deck, with designs and wireframes to bring it to life.

The best-rooted ideas will move on to the finale!

Round 3 – Council of Pioneers (Finale)
Your roots have taken hold, now show how they grow.

Finalist teams will present their solutions before a panel of industry experts and alumni who form the Council of Pioneers. Each team will showcase its idea, defend its design choices and answer the jury’s questions. The jury will weigh creativity, community understanding, feasibility and sustainability after the pilot ends.

Format: Live online presentation (8-10 minutes + Q&A)

The best idea earns the honor of shaping the village’s future.

About ProdMad 6.0

ProdMad 6.0 is more than a competition. It asks participants to build for the people technology usually forgets. It challenges them to design under real constraints, respect local knowledge and show that the best products start from the ground up.

Registration Details

  • Open to all B-School, Undergraduate and Postgraduate students.
  • Teams can consist of 1-3 members from the same institute.
  • A participant can be part of only one team.
  • Multiple entries from the same team will lead to disqualification.
  • Submissions after deadlines will not be accepted.
  • In case of any dispute, the decision of bITeSys, IIM Shillong will be final and binding.

In collaboration with The Product Folks, participants can build tech products through the Vibe Sprint. If you require credits to develop your product using the platform, please reach out to the organizers.

problem_statement:
BRAND WARS | Alpha Consulting Club

About the Competition:

Think strategically. Adapt quickly. Negotiate smartly.

Brand Wars is an online inter-college business strategy competition organised by Alpha Consulting Club, Lady Shri Ram College for Women. Designed to test participants' strategic thinking, analytical abilities, decision-making and negotiation skills, the competition places teams in the role of leading brands navigating a dynamic and competitive business environment.

From developing expansion strategies to responding to unexpected market disruptions and negotiating alliances, participants will need to make informed decisions, use data effectively and stay aligned with their brand's objectives.

Eligibility:

  • Open to students from LSR

  • Participation is in teams of 2-3 members.

  • Inter-specialisation teams are allowed.

  • Each participant may be part of only one team.

  • All rounds will be conducted online.

Competition Format:

The competition will consist of two rounds.

Round 1: The Strategy Quiz

  • Mode: Online quiz
  • Duration: 25 minutes
  • Format: 25 multiple-choice questions

This elimination round will assess participants' analytical and business aptitude through questions covering:

  • Statistics and probability
  • Data interpretation
  • Logical reasoning
  • Business and brand awareness
  • Numerical aptitude

Each question carries one mark. There is no negative marking. The highest-performing teams will advance to the final round. In case of a tie affecting shortlisting, a tie-breaker may be used.

Round 2: The Brand Wars Simulation

Mode: Live online event

Shortlisted teams will represent assigned brands and compete through three stages:

Stage 1: Strategic Pitch

Each team will receive a brand profile, business objective, relevant market data and constraints. Teams must develop and present a concise, data-informed strategy to help their brand achieve its objective.

  • Pitch duration: 3 minutes

  • Judges' questions: 1 minute

  • Teams may be asked to submit a short strategy document or presentation in advance.

Stage 2: Market Shocks

Teams will face unexpected developments in the business environment, such as a competitor's price war, supply-chain disruption or a shift in consumer preferences. Using the information provided, teams must adapt their strategies and justify their decisions under time pressure.

Stage 3: Alliances and Negotiation

Teams will negotiate with other participating brands to form partnerships, exchange resources or arrive at mutually beneficial business agreements. All proposed agreements must be submitted through the designated form within the stipulated time.

Evaluation Criteria

Final-round teams will be evaluated out of 100 marks on the following parameters:

  • Strategic thinking and feasibility of the pitch – 30 marks
  • Use of data and numerical reasoning – 20 marks
  • Response to market shocks and adaptability – 25 marks
  • Negotiation skills and value creation – 15 marks
  • Alignment with the assigned brand objective – 10 marks

The Round 1 quiz will serve only as an elimination round and will not contribute to the final-round scores.

Rules and Guidelines:

  • Teams must consist of 2–3 registered student members.
  • Participants must provide accurate registration details and ensure that all team members meet the eligibility criteria.
  • Only registered team members may contribute to their team's submissions and decisions.
  • Teams must adhere to the deadlines, time limits and instructions communicated by the organisers.
  • All strategies, pitches and responses must be the team's original work. Plagiarism, impersonation or misrepresentation may result in disqualification.
  • Teams must not share quiz questions, answers or confidential competition material with other participants during the competition.
  • During the final round, teams must make decisions based on the information provided and submit all required responses and agreements through the designated platforms.
  • Any attempt to manipulate scores, interfere with another team's participation or gain an unfair advantage may lead to disqualification.
  • The organisers reserve the right to make reasonable changes to the schedule or conduct of the competition, with due communication to registered participants.
  • The decision of the organisers and judges will be final.

Important Dates:

  • Registrations close: 3 November 2026, 6:00 PM

  • Round 1 – Online Quiz: 4 November 2026

  • Round 2 – Live Brand Wars Simulation: 6 November 2026

Further instructions, quiz access details and final-round materials will be communicated to registered participants through the contact details provided during registration.

Get ready to think like a strategist, respond like a decision-maker and negotiate like a leader. The market is yours to conquer.

The programme aims to identify, encourage and support promising ideas and innovations that address challenges faced by tribal communities across India.
  • The programme invites tribal youth, students, entrepreneurs and young changemakers/innovators to present innovative solutions that can contribute to inclusive development, community empowerment and sustainable impact.

    • Technology: Developing innovative technological solutions to practical challenges.

    • Culture: Preserving and promoting tribal heritage, traditions and indigenous knowledge.

    • Interested applicants must submit their applications through the designated online application platform by 5 November 2026, 11:59 PM IST.

From identifying promising companies to analysing sectors and balancing portfolio risks, every decision matters. Go beyond conventional stock picking and demonstrate your ability to turn market insights into a compelling investment strategy.

Can you think beyond the numbers and invest your way to the top?
