  • Students from colleges and universities across India are welcome.

  • Teams must consist of 2–4 members.

  • Inter-college, cross-specialisation and cross-year teams are permitted.

For detailed competition guidelines, portfolio requirements, submission instructions and the approved company universe, please refer to the attached documents.



Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. Who can participate in Investomania?

Investomania is open to all undergraduate (UG) and postgraduate (PG) students from recognised colleges and universities across India, irrespective of their academic discipline.

2. What is the team size?

Each team must consist of 2–4 members. Inter-college, cross-specialisation, and cross-year teams are permitted.

3. What is the investment corpus for the competition?

Each team will manage a hypothetical investment corpus of ₹5 crore (±10%). Teams must utilise the full corpus while constructing their portfolios.

4. Which companies can we choose for our portfolio?

Teams must select companies exclusively from the approved universe of 110 NSE-listed companies provided by the organisers. The complete company list is available in the attached document.

5. Is there a limit on the number of companies we can include?

No. There is no restriction on the number of companies you can select from the approved list. You may adopt either a diversified or a concentrated investment strategy, provided your decisions are logically justified.

6. What is required for the Preliminary Round?

Teams must submit a 3-slide presentation outlining their investment strategy. The presentation should cover portfolio allocation, company and sector analysis, investment rationale, and risk-management approach.

The cover slide, thank-you slide, and appendix are excluded from the three-slide limit.

7. What is the submission deadline and format?

Submissions must be uploaded through the Unstop platform in PDF format (maximum 10 MB) by 13 November 2026, 12:01 AM IST.

8. How will the Preliminary Round submissions be evaluated?

Submissions will be evaluated based on:

  • Fund allocation strategy

  • Company analysis

  • Sectoral outlook

  • Data-backed investment decisions

  • Risk-management approach

  • Presentation clarity

9. How many teams will qualify for the Final Round?

The top 15 teams from the Preliminary Round will qualify for the offline Final Round.

10. What happens in the Final Round?

Shortlisted teams will present and defend their investment portfolios before a panel of judges at Jadavpur University, Kolkata. The final winners will be determined based on the judges' evaluation.

11. When and where will the Final Round take place?

The Final Round will be held on 21 November 2026 at Jadavpur University, Kolkata.

12. Where can we find the detailed rules and approved company list?

The detailed competition guidelines, submission requirements, and approved 110-company research universe are available in the documents attached to the Unstop listing. Participants are advised to review them carefully before preparing their submissions.

title: Truss-T The Process
problem_statement:
Design Smart. Build Strong. Bear the Load.

Competition Description:

Think you have what it takes to design a bridge that can withstand the ultimate load test? Welcome to TRUSS-T, a team-based structural engineering challenge where creativity, calculations, and construction come together!

Teams must design and construct a bridge using ice cream sticks within the specified dimensions of 25 cm × 10 cm. The bridge must follow a truss structure, with the design, geometry, and arrangement of members decided by the team members themselves.

Once construction is complete, the bridge will be mounted on the designated supports, and weights will be gradually suspended from its centre to test its load-bearing capacity.

The real challenge lies in achieving maximum strength with a limited set of materials. Can your truss design withstand the greatest load without structural failure?

Design intelligently. Build precisely. Prove your engineering.

Competition Format:

  • Participation: Team-based
  • Duration: As announced by the organizers
  • Construction Material: Ice cream sticks and organizer-approved joining materials
  • Bridge Dimensions: 25 cm × 10 cm, as specified by the organizers
  • Structural Type: Truss bridge
  • Testing Method: Incremental loading at the centre of the bridge
  • Winning Criteria: Maximum load sustained before structural failure

Rules and Regulations:

  • Each team must design and construct a bridge using ice cream sticks within the prescribed dimensions.
  • The bridge must incorporate a recognizable truss structure, with the arrangement and geometry of the truss members decided by the team.
  • Only materials approved by the organizers may be used for construction.
  • Teams must complete their bridges within the allotted time.
  • The completed bridge must satisfy the specified dimensional and support requirements before testing.
  • During testing, the bridge will be placed on standardized supports, and weights will be suspended from its centre using the designated loading arrangement.
  • Loads will be increased gradually according to the organizers' testing procedure.
  • Participants must not touch, adjust, or reinforce the bridge once load testing begins.
  • The maximum load sustained before structural failure will determine the team's performance.
  • All participants must follow the organizers' safety instructions during construction and testing.
  • The organizers' decisions regarding dimensional compliance, structural failure, and final results will be binding.

Judging Criteria:

  • Load-Bearing Capacity: Maximum load sustained before structural failure.
  • Design and Structural Integrity: Effectiveness of the truss arrangement and load distribution.
  • Dimensional Compliance: Adherence to the specified bridge dimensions.
  • Rule Compliance: Use of permitted materials and adherence to construction and testing procedures.

Winner Selection:

  • The team whose bridge sustains the highest load before structural failure will be declared the winner, provided it satisfies all competition requirements.
  • In case of a tie, the organizers may use the bridge's self-weight and load-to-weight ratio as secondary criteria, provided these are announced before the competition.

What to Expect:

TRUSS-T challenges participants to apply the principles of truss mechanics, force distribution, tension, compression, and structural stability in a hands-on engineering environment. Every joint, member, and connection can influence the final result.

Can your bridge carry the weight of your engineering?

title: National Aeromodeling Challenge
problem_statement:
About:

The National Aeromodelling Challenge is presented by Techfest, IIT Bombay, for students passionate about aerospace and engineering. Teams design, build, and fly their own fixed-wing electric RC aircraft that carries golf-ball payloads. They first prove their aircraft can carry and land a payload safely, then complete a timed two-trip delivery mission. Ready-made models are not allowed. Bring your aircraft to life at Techfest, IIT Bombay, Asia’s largest science and technology festival.

Structure:

  • The competition has an abstract screening stage, followed by a Qualifier Round and a Main Round at Techfest, IIT Bombay.
  • Eligibility: Open to school, UG, and PG students. Teams can include students from different colleges or schools. Participants must carry a bona fide certificate signed by their HoD/Dean/Principal and a valid ID card.
  • Team Size: 2 to 4 members. A participant can be part of only one team.
  • Problem Statement: Design, build, and fly a fixed-wing aircraft that carries golf-ball payloads (45 g, 43 mm diameter, supplied by organizers) and completes the tasks in each round.

Abstract Submission (Online):

  • Submit an abstract of under 15 pages (A4, 1.5 line spacing) in the official Aeromodelling 2026 Abstract Form format.
  • The abstract should cover the aircraft’s basic design (dimensions, wing area, velocity, etc.) and how it suits the problem.
  • Attach a zip file of 5-10 photographs taken while building the aircraft.
  • Abstracts not following the format will not be evaluated.

Round 1 - Qualifier Round:

  • Carry one or more golf balls inside the aircraft, fly for at least 30 seconds within a 3-minute window, and land with the payload inside the designated area.
  • Score = (payload weight x 100) / aircraft weight without payload.
  • Each team gets two attempts, and the best counts.
  • The top 30 teams advance to the Main Round.

Round 2 - Main Round:

  • Complete a round trip of payload delivery within 3 minutes: load, take off, fly at least 30 seconds, land, unload, reload, take off again, fly at least 30 seconds, land, and unload.
  • Loading must be hands-free, using transmitter-operated compartment doors.
  • Score = E1 + E2 - C1 - C2 - C3. Each delivered golf ball earns 10 points per trip, and each second spent on the ground during loading and unloading costs 1 point.
  • Each team gets two attempts, and the best counts.
  • Overall Score = 0.25 x Normalized Qualifier Score + 0.75 x Normalized Main Round Score. Ties are broken by a separate round framed by the judges.

Design Constraints:

  • The aircraft must be designed and built by the team (no RTF/ARF/BNF models).
  • Maximum weight is 1 kg without payload.
  • Thrust-to-weight ratio must not exceed 1 without payload.
  • Wingspan is up to 1.2 m, with no tolerance.
  • Propeller diameter is up to 13 inches, and metal propellers are not allowed.
  • Electric motors only.
  • Gyroscopes, programmed mission steps, FPV, and any flying support are prohibited.

Timeline:

  • Registration Deadline: 25th November 2026
  • Abstract Submission Deadline: 25th November 2026
  • Abstract Result Announcement: 1st December 2026
  • Qualifier Round: 15th-16th December 2026
  • Main Round: 17th December 2026

Rules:

  • Register online to receive a Team ID. No late entries are accepted.
  • The same aircraft described in the abstract must be used in both rounds. Damaged aircraft can be repaired but not replaced.
  • No modifications to the aircraft are allowed after the thrust-to-weight ratio is measured.
  • A 2.4 GHz radio is required. Any other frequency must be informed to the organizers in advance.
  • Landing must be within the inner boundary, otherwise a 20% penalty applies. Touching or crossing the outer boundary disqualifies the attempt.
  • Teams must be ready at their turn, or they lose it.
  • Teams must not share aircraft components with other teams.
  • Safety violations or misconduct will lead to penalties or disqualification.
  • The judges’ and organizers’ decisions are final and binding.
  • Updates will be posted on the Techfest website and sent to registered teams. For official announcements, contact satwik@techfest.org (queries via email will not be entertained).

Rewards and Prizes:

  • Top 3 Winners: INR 1,00,000
  • Certificates: All participants who qualify for Round 2 will receive a certificate.

title: Tower of Torque
problem_statement:
Welcome to the Tower of Torque - Organised by Mechanical Engineering Department of Veer Surendra Sai University of Technology, Burla.

Think Fast. Build Tall. Beat the Clock.

Competition Description

Ready to put your creativity, precision, and structural balancing skills to the ultimate test? Welcome to Tower of Torque, an exciting individual challenge where speed meets stability!

Participants must construct the tallest possible freestanding tower using just 20 cups in 60 seconds. No tape, glue, or external support is allowed. Your tower must remain standing independently for at least five seconds to qualify.

But there’s a twist! In the final stage, participants must build using their non-dominant hand, challenging their coordination, adaptability, and ability to perform under pressure.

Do you have the strategy and steady hands to rise above the competition? Step up, beat the clock, and claim the title of Tower of Torque champion!

Competition Format

  • Participation: Individual
  • Duration: 1–2 minutes per participant
  • Building Time: 60 seconds
  • Materials Provided: 20 cups per participant
  • Winning Criteria: Greatest height achieved by a valid, freestanding tower

Rules and Regulations

  • Each participant will receive exactly 20 cups.
  • Participants must build their tower within the allotted 60 seconds.
  • No tape, glue, strings, or any other external support or fastening material is permitted.
  • The tower must stand independently for at least five seconds after the timer ends.
  • The non-dominant-hand challenge will be introduced in the final stage, as instructed by the event coordinators.
  • Participants may not use their body, clothing, furniture, or other objects to support the tower.
  • Only towers completed within the time limit and satisfying all stability requirements will be considered valid.
  • The organizers' decision regarding measurement, validity, and final results will be binding.

Judging Criteria

  • Primary criterion: Maximum height of the valid tower.
  • Stability: The tower must remain standing unsupported for five seconds.
  • Fair play: All participants must follow the same material, time, and construction restrictions.

Winner Selection

The participant who constructs the tallest valid freestanding tower wins. In case of a tie, the organizers may conduct a sudden-death tiebreaker using the same materials and time limit.

What to Expect

Get ready for a fast-paced challenge involving spatial reasoning, structural balance, quick decision-making, and hand-eye coordination. Every second counts, every cup matters, and one wrong move can bring your entire tower crashing down!

title: Xplore & Nova Exilaro Article Writing Competition
problem_statement:
Overview

When the Algorithm Makes the Call: Who Owns the Decision?

In a world where algorithms increasingly influence business decisions, from hiring and pricing to lending and supply chain management, an important question emerges: When an algorithm makes the call, who takes responsibility for the outcome?

NovaExilaro and Xplore, XLRI, invite students across India to participate in an individual article writing competition exploring the intersection of technology, management, leadership, and accountability.

As organisations rely increasingly on data-driven recommendations, the role of human judgement is evolving. Managers may still make the final call, but how much ownership do they truly exercise when decisions are shaped by systems they cannot fully question?

We invite you to go beyond conventional discussions on artificial intelligence and automation. Develop a distinctive perspective, challenge existing assumptions, and present a well-researched argument on where accountability should lie in an algorithm-driven business environment.

Why Participate?

  • Get Published: The winning article will be featured in Xplore Magazine in both digital and print formats.
  • Reach Industry Leaders: Xplore reaches 50+ CXOs per edition and has a cumulative LinkedIn audience of approximately 4 million impressions.
  • Showcase Your Thinking: Present your ideas and insights to an audience of industry leaders, academicians, and management professionals.
  • Get Recognised: Best contributions will receive a cash prize of INR [Amount] and an e-certificate.

Who Can Participate?

  • The competition is open to all students currently enrolled in a recognised undergraduate or postgraduate programme in India.
  • Participation is individual, and each participant may submit one article.

Submission Guidelines

  • Word Limit: 500–800 words (excluding title, summary line, author details, and references).
  • Format: Microsoft Word (.docx) only.
  • Font: Times New Roman, 12 pt, with 1.5 line spacing.
  • Page Setup: A4 size with 1-inch margins.
  • References: Minimum 3 credible sources, using APA 7 or Harvard referencing style.
  • Originality: Articles must be original, unpublished, and primarily written by the participant.

Your article should feature a compelling opening, a clearly developed argument supported by evidence, a counter-perspective, and a conclusion that presents a definite point of view.

Important: AI tools may be used for research and language checking but must not be used to write the article. An AI-use disclosure is mandatory. Entries with a similarity score above 20% (excluding references and quoted text) may be disqualified.

Judging Criteria

  • Originality and Insight – 30%
  • Argument and Evidence – 25%
  • Relevance to the Theme – 20%
  • Structure and Clarity – 15%
  • Style and Readability – 10%

How to Participate

  • Register for the competition through this Unstop page.
  • Develop your article in accordance with the theme brief and submission guidelines.
  • Save your submission as FullName_CollegeName.docx.
  • Upload your article on Unstop before the submission deadline.

Don't just describe how algorithms are changing the world. Question who is accountable when they make the decisions.

Bring your perspective, make your argument, and let your ideas reach beyond the classroom!

title: MED Detective - National Medical Case Study Competition
problem_statement:
Overview

Put your clinical reasoning and diagnostic skills to the test at MED DETECTIVE! Analyse medical case scenarios, identify clinical problems, and develop evidence-based diagnoses and management plans.

Eligibility: Medical and allied medical students from first year to final year, graduates, and postgraduate students/candidates.

Competition Process & Format:

  • Round 2: The top 8 teams qualify to analyse a new case, prepare a PPT, present their findings, and participate in a viva.

Rules:

  • Teams must have exactly 2 eligible members.
  • Submit the Round 1 PPT between 10:45 AM and 11:00 AM.
  • Medical claims must be supported by credible, verifiable sources.
  • AI tools may support research and brainstorming, but conclusions must reflect independent clinical reasoning.
  • Case confidentiality, academic integrity, punctuality, and professional conduct are mandatory.
  • Judges' decisions are final, subject to the stated tie-breaker rules.

Event Details:

  • Date: 27 November 2026
  • Venue: NIMS University

Investigate, analyse, and demonstrate your clinical excellence at NIMS QUEST 2026!

title: Board Room
problem_statement:
Event Guidelines

Boardroom Battle is a business strategy competition at PEC’s E-Summit 2026, where participants step into the roles of company executives to solve a business challenge.

Teams act as a company’s leadership, balancing strategy, finance, technology and marketing to develop a practical solution and defend it before a judging panel.

Event Details

  • Event dates: 14–15 November 2026; the exact schedule will be communicated to registered teams.
  • Mode: Offline.
  • Venue: PEC Campus, Chandigarh.
  • Team size: 3–4 members.
  • Intercollege teams are allowed: Members may belong to different colleges.

Competition Format

  • Briefing and Role Allocation: Teams assign executive roles among their members:
    • CEO: Overall strategy and business decisions.
    • CFO: Budgeting, costs and financial viability.
    • CTO: Technology, product development and operational feasibility.
    • CMO: Marketing, customer acquisition and brand positioning.
    • In teams of three, the CEO also handles the CMO’s responsibilities.
  • Case Reveal and Preparation: Teams receive a common business problem, along with relevant information, constraints and a budget. They must analyse the challenge and prepare a solution covering strategy, finances, execution and marketing.
  • Boardroom Presentation: Teams present their proposed solution to the judging panel. Each member explains the decisions relevant to their executive role and responds to questions.
  • Twist Round: Shortlisted teams receive an unexpected change in the business situation, such as a budget reduction, a new competitor or a shift in customer demand. They must revise their strategy and defend their decisions before the panel.

Rules and Regulations

Team Participation

  • Each team must consist of 3–4 members.
  • Intercollege teams are permitted.
  • A participant cannot register with more than one team.
  • Executive roles must be assigned before preparation begins and remain unchanged throughout the competition.
  • All members must be present for the briefing and participate in the presentation.
  • Teams must report according to the schedule communicated by the organisers.

Case Analysis and Preparation

  • All teams receive the same initial problem statement and preparation time.
  • Solutions must address the stated problem and comply with the provided budget and constraints.
  • Teams may make reasonable assumptions where information is unavailable, but must clearly identify and justify them.
  • Financial estimates, projections and calculations must be explained when questioned.
  • Technical recommendations must be understandable and feasible; coding or a working prototype is not required.
  • Teams must develop their solutions independently. Collaboration between teams or assistance from non-participants is prohibited.
  • The policy on internet access and AI tools will be communicated before preparation begins and will apply equally to all teams.

Presentation and Twist Round

  • Every team member must contribute to the presentation and be prepared to answer questions related to their role.
  • Presentation format, preparation time and speaking limits will be communicated during the briefing.
  • Teams must submit any required presentation materials by the announced deadline.
  • Only shortlisted teams advance to the twist round.
  • All finalists receive the same twist and equal time to revise their solutions.
  • Revised solutions must address the new constraints and explain the trade-offs involved.

Evaluation and Conduct

  • Teams will be evaluated on problem understanding, practicality, financial reasoning, execution, creativity and coordination.
  • In the twist round, adaptability and the justification of revised decisions will also be considered.
  • Plagiarism, fabricated claims presented as facts, misconduct or disruption may result in penalties or disqualification.
  • The judging panel’s decision will be final.
prizes_summary: Cash prizes, certificates, official mentorship, and PPI hiring opportunities.

title: Bargain Battles
problem_statement:
Event Guidelines

Bargain Battles is an auction and sales-pitch competition at PEC’s E-Summit 2026. The competition begins with an online quiz round, followed by an offline auction and pitching round for shortlisted teams.

Teams bid for imaginative fictional products using virtual money and then persuade a judging panel to buy them. From an eraser that removes past mistakes to a watch that pauses time, every product challenges participants to turn imagination into a convincing sales pitch.

Event Details

  • Event dates: 14–15 November 2026.
  • Round 1: Online quiz; the schedule will be communicated to registered teams.
  • Subsequent rounds: Offline at PEC Campus, Chandigarh.
  • Team size: 3–4 members.
  • Intercollege teams are allowed: Members of a team may belong to different colleges.

Competition Format

  • Online Quiz: Registered teams participate in an online quiz. Shortlisted teams advance to the offline rounds.
  • Briefing and Auction: Qualified teams receive details of the fictional products, including their abilities and limitations. Teams must purchase at least one and no more than two products. Teams that purchase no products are eliminated.
  • Pitch Preparation: Teams receive 25 minutes to develop their sales pitches, covering target customers, benefits, applications and proposed selling prices.
  • Pitch and Negotiation: Teams present their purchased products to the judging panel, followed by questions and negotiation. Teams purchasing two products must pitch both products.

Rules and Regulations

Team Participation

  • Each team must consist of 3–4 members.
  • Intercollege teams are permitted.
  • A participant cannot register with more than one team.
  • Only teams shortlisted through the online quiz may participate in the offline rounds.
  • All shortlisted team members must attend the offline briefing and participate in the pitching round.
  • Teams must report according to the schedule communicated by the organisers.

Online Quiz

  • Teams must complete the quiz within the announced quiz window.
  • The quiz format, duration and participation instructions will be shared before the round.
  • Collaboration between different teams or assistance from non-participants is prohibited.
  • Teams must ensure access to a stable internet connection.

Product and Pitch Rules

  • Each team may purchase a maximum of two products and must purchase at least one product to remain in the competition.
  • Teams that do not purchase any product will be eliminated.
  • Teams must pitch every product they purchase: one product if they buy one, and both products if they buy two.
  • Teams may create their own branding, customer segments and applications, but cannot alter or add to the products’ stated powers or limitations.
  • Slides are not required.
  • Teams must prepare their pitches independently; assistance from non-participants is prohibited.
  • All money used in the competition is fictional and has no real monetary value.
  • Misconduct, disruption or violation of the rules may result in disqualification.
prizes_summary: Cash prizes, certificates, official mentorship, and PPI hiring opportunities.

title: PromptX - AI Prompt Battle
organizer: Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology (MMMUT), Gorakhpur
venue_address: Madan Mohan Malaviya University of Technology
problem_statement:
Continuum 2026 AI Prompt Battle is a competitive Generative AI challenge focused on prompt engineering, reasoning, creativity and the ability to produce high-quality outputs from AI systems.

Participants will be given a series of AI-based challenges requiring them to understand the task, design effective prompts, iterate strategically and achieve the best possible result. The competition is designed to test not only how participants use AI, but how well they think, structure instructions and control AI-generated outputs.

What the challenge tests

  • Prompt engineering and prompt optimization
  • Logical reasoning and problem-solving
  • Understanding of Generative AI systems
  • Creativity and structured thinking
  • Output quality and relevance
  • Ability to refine prompts through experimentation
  • Effective use of AI tools

Competition Format

Participants will compete through a series of prompt-based challenges. Each challenge will present a specific objective or problem, and participants will have to develop and refine prompts to generate the required output.

Challenges may involve:

  • Text generation and transformation
  • Reasoning and problem-solving
  • Creative generation
  • Structured output generation
  • AI-assisted analysis
  • Instruction following and prompt optimization

Participants may iterate on their prompts where permitted. Evaluation will consider the effectiveness, accuracy, relevance, creativity and quality of the resulting output.

Rules

  • Participants must use the AI tools/platforms specified by the organizers for each challenge.
  • Prompts must be created and submitted by the participant/team during the competition unless a challenge explicitly permits otherwise.
  • Participants must follow all challenge-specific instructions and submission requirements.
  • Exploiting platform vulnerabilities, bypassing competition restrictions or using unauthorized methods is prohibited.
  • Plagiarism, impersonation, submission of another participant's work or deliberate misrepresentation may lead to disqualification.
  • External resources may be restricted for particular challenges; participants must follow the instructions announced by the organizers.
  • The organizing team reserves the right to modify individual challenge conditions when required for fair competition.
  • Decisions of the authorized jury/organizing team regarding evaluation and rankings will be final.

Eligibility

The competition is open to participants interested in Generative AI, prompt engineering, reasoning and emerging AI technologies. Participants from eligible colleges/universities may participate, subject to the final registration conditions published by the organizers.

title: Tech Debate
problem_statement:
Tech Debate Website Registration

All participants must register through the official Tech Habba platform using the link below.

Tech Habba Website: https://tech-habba26.vercel.app/

About the Event

Challenge your critical thinking, technical knowledge, and public speaking skills in a competitive debate on technology and society. Debate motions covering topics such as artificial intelligence, digital privacy, automation, the future of work, and emerging technologies.

Participants will be judged on the strength and clarity of their arguments, use of evidence, rebuttal skills, logical structure, and delivery. Motions and team positions will be announced on the day, so participants must be prepared to argue either side. Think critically, defend your position, challenge opposing arguments, and make your case!

Guidelines

  • Eligibility: Open to students from any college.
  • Team Formation: Each team must consist of exactly 2 participants.
  • Identity Verification: A valid college ID card is mandatory.
  • Debate Format: Each round features a Proposition team arguing in favor of the motion and an Opposition team arguing against it.
  • Topics: Motions will cover technology and society, including AI, privacy, automation, the future of work, and other relevant topics.
  • Preparation: Motions and sides will be assigned on the day, with a short preparation period before each round.
  • Judging Criteria: Teams will be evaluated on argument quality, evidence, rebuttals, logical structure, and delivery.

Event Schedule

  1. 11:00 AM – 11:20 AM: Reporting and briefing.
  2. 11:20 AM – 12:50 PM: Preliminary rounds.
  3. 1:00 PM – 1:45 PM: Final debate.
  4. 1:45 PM – 2:00 PM: Results announcement.

Rules

title: Business Model Canvas (Start-up Idea Pitching)
problem_statement:
Date of Event : 20 November 2026

Pitching Requirements

PITCHING REQUIREMENTS
Team Size 1–4 participants
Eligibility Students of Classes 9–12 with valid school/student identification
Format Live pitch to a panel of judges
Mandatory Document A completed Business Model Canvas covering all nine building blocks
Visual Aids (optional) Presentation of up to 8 slides, printed canvas, poster, or simple prototype
Equipment Teams bring their own files and materials. A projector may be provided, subject to venue availability.

 

TIME LIMIT Up to 6 minutes to pitch, followed by up to 4 minutes of questions from the judges. A timekeeper will signal when 1 minute remains. The pitch stops when the time limit ends.

 

SCORING Teams are scored out of 100 by the judging panel using the criteria in this section.

 

SAFETY Any prototype or demo material must follow the General Rules: safe batteries and electrical connections, and no hazardous materials or mechanisms.

 

THE BUSINESS MODEL CANVAS

Every team must complete all nine blocks of the canvas below. Use the guiding question in each block as a prompt.

KEY PARTNERSHIPSWho are your key partners and suppliers? KEY ACTIVITIESWhat must you do to deliver your idea? VALUE PROPOSITIONSWhat problem do you solve, and why is your solution better? CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIPSHow will you win and keep customers? CUSTOMER SEGMENTSWho are you creating value for?
KEY RESOURCESWhat people, tools, and money do you need? CHANNELSHow will you reach your customers?
COST STRUCTUREWhat will be your main costs? REVENUE STREAMSHow will you earn money?
           

 

Rules:

  • Each team may consist of 1–4 participants.
  • Each team must present one original start-up idea developed by its members. Presenting an existing company, product, or someone else's idea as your own is not permitted.
  • Every team must prepare a Business Model Canvas that covers all nine building blocks.
  • The completed canvas must be submitted to the organizers by the deadline announced at registration. Late or incomplete submissions may receive a penalty or may not be accepted.
  • Teams will pitch in the order drawn by the organizers. A team that is not ready when called may lose its slot or be disqualified.
  • The pitch should clearly explain the problem, the target customers, the proposed solution, and how the idea can grow into a sustainable business.
  • Each team has a maximum of 6 minutes to pitch, followed by up to 4 minutes of questions. Teams that exceed the time limit may be stopped by the judges and may receive a score deduction.
  • All team members should take part in the pitch or the question-and-answer session.
  • Teams may use a presentation of up to 8 slides, the printed canvas, posters, or a simple prototype as visual aids. Teams must bring their own files and equipment.
  • Teachers, mentors, and parents may not speak for, prompt, or assist the team during the pitch or the question-and-answer session.
  • Ideas must be appropriate for a school-level event. Ideas that are illegal, harmful, hateful, or unsafe are not permitted.
  • Ideas remain the property of the presenting team. Teams should avoid sharing confidential details they are not comfortable discussing in public.
  • Copied content, plagiarism, or deliberately false claims may lead to disqualification.
  • The team with the highest total score will be declared the winner. If scores are tied, the team with the higher Business Model Quality score ranks first, followed by Innovation & Originality.
  • The judges' decision will be final and binding.

Judging Criteria:

CRITERIA WHAT JUDGES LOOK FOR
Problem & Customer Understanding A clearly defined problem and a well-understood target customer.
Innovation & Originality A fresh, creative idea developed by the team.
Business Model Quality A complete, logical canvas where all nine blocks fit together.
Market & Revenue Viability A realistic way to reach customers and earn revenue.
Presentation & Communication A clear, confident, well-organized pitch delivered within time.
Q&A and Team Coordination Thoughtful answers and a team that works together.

problem_statement:
About AdVenture

AdVenture is a three-round marketing and brand strategy competition conducted as part of Strategia 2027. The event places participants in the role of an advertising and marketing agency, challenging them to develop, defend, and adapt a campaign for a real product from a real brand.

The competition tests participants’ ability to understand consumers, identify market opportunities, think creatively, and make strategic decisions under pressure. Across three progressively challenging rounds, teams will develop a campaign strategy, respond to a marketing crisis affecting the same brand, and defend their decisions in an undisclosed live finale.

Focus Areas

  • Brand and Market Relevance
  • Creative Thinking
  • Strategic Thinking
  • Problem Diagnosis

Rounds and Competition Structure

  • Participants must submit either a slide deck (PPT/PDF) or a single poster, strictly following the format specified in the round brief.
  • The highest-performing teams, with the number to be announced, will advance to Round 2.

Round 2: The Red Alert: Crisis (Online)

  • Teams will receive a marketing crisis or product-related problem connected to the same brand and case used in Round 1. The crisis may involve a public relations setback, declining brand relevance, a repositioning requirement, or a failed product launch.

Teams must diagnose the problem and develop a revamped marketing brief containing:

  • Problem Diagnosis and a Fresh Strategic Direction
  • Key Messaging and a Proposed Course of Action

This round evaluates the ability to respond to unexpected challenges, rethink campaign strategies, and propose practical, relevant solutions while maintaining brand alignment.

Round 3: The Full Throttle (Offline)

  • The final round will be an undisclosed surprise challenge, revealed only when the round begins.
  • Finalists must think on their feet and defend the campaign developed in Round 1 and the crisis response developed in Round 2 before the judging panel.
  • This round tests strategic clarity, adaptability, confidence, and the ability to justify marketing decisions under pressure.

The AdVenture Challenge

AdVenture goes beyond conventional marketing exercises by challenging participants to think like real-world brand strategists. From building a compelling campaign to navigating a brand crisis and defending their decisions in a live finale, teams must demonstrate creativity backed by strategic reasoning.

Bring your ideas, challenge conventions, and prove that you can turn a brand brief into a winning strategy.

title: FrAudit
problem_statement:
FRAudiT – Where the Numbers Never Lie, But People Do:

FRAudiT is the flagship auditing and forensic accounting competition at Strategia’27, designed to take participants beyond textbook learning and into the real-world workings of a statutory auditor and forensic investigator.

The competition challenges participants to work with incomplete information, conflicting evidence, time pressure, financial statement risks, internal control weaknesses, and fraud scenarios.

Across three progressively challenging stages, participants move from an online audit knowledge qualifier to an intensive forensic investigation and finally to a live “Cook & Catch” Showdown, where one team creates a realistic financial manipulation and another team must detect it.

Evaluation Criteria:

Participants will be evaluated on the following parameters:

  • Accuracy and analytical reasoning
  • Professional skepticism
  • Financial statement analysis
  • Quality of audit evidence and documentation
  • Ability to identify fraud and control weaknesses
  • Appropriateness of audit procedures
  • Professional judgment and decision-making
  • Teamwork under time pressure
  • Clarity and professionalism of reporting

Guidelines:

  • The competition is open to bona fide undergraduate, postgraduate, and professional-course students pursuing Commerce, Accountancy, Finance, and allied programs.
  • Each team must consist of 2–3 members. Individual participation is not permitted at any stage.
  • Team composition cannot be changed after the Round 1 registration deadline, except in documented emergencies and subject to approval by the Organizing Committee.
  • Participants must carry valid institutional identification and may be required to produce it at any stage of the competition.
  • Plagiarism, impersonation, misrepresentation, collusion, or any form of dishonest assistance is strictly prohibited.
  • The use of AI tools, chatbots, automated reasoning assistants, internet access, or unauthorized reference material is prohibited unless specifically permitted for a particular round.
  • Participants may communicate only with members of their own team during active competition windows.
  • Only submissions made in the officially prescribed format will be evaluated.
  • Once a submission has been made, it cannot be edited or resubmitted unless specifically permitted under the rules of that round.
  • Any attempt to access confidential case content before the official commencement of a round may result in disqualification.
  • Decisions of the judging panel and the Organizing Committee regarding scoring, rules, and disputes shall be final and binding.
  • The Organizing Committee reserves the right to modify the format, schedule, scenario content, or rules wherever necessary. Any material changes will be communicated to participants.

Stages and Timelines:

Stage 1: Online Qualifier – Audit IQ: Concept and Case Challenge:

Date: To Be Announced (TBA)
Time: To Be Announced (TBA)
Duration: 30–45 minutes (TBA)
Platform: Online Examination Portal

The first stage is an online qualifier designed to test participants’ understanding of auditing concepts and their ability to apply audit knowledge to practical business situations.

The qualifier combines conceptual auditing questions with short case studies and scenario-based questions. The focus is on application, reasoning, and professional judgment rather than simple memorization.

Part A – Audit Concepts:

Questions may cover the following areas:

  • Fundamental and intermediate auditing concepts and principles
  • Audit planning and risk assessment
  • Internal controls and control risks
  • Audit evidence and documentation
  • Audit procedures and assertions
  • Materiality and professional skepticism
  • Fraud risk
  • Ethics and auditor independence
  • Substantive testing, vouching, and verification
  • Analytical procedures
  • Revenue, inventory, receivables, and payables
  • Basic forensic audit awareness

Part B – Audit Case Studies:

Teams will encounter practical audit scenarios involving:

  • Financial statement risks
  • Internal control weaknesses
  • Fraud risks
  • Audit evidence and documentation
  • Revenue, inventory, receivables, purchases, and payroll
  • Selection of appropriate audit procedures
  • Identification of appropriate auditor responses

Question Pattern and Selection:

  • Approximately 40–50 objective questions are expected.
  • Around 60% of the questions will be conceptual or application-based.
  • Around 40% will be case-study or scenario-based.
  • The difficulty level will progress from basic and intermediate concepts to application-based questions and challenging professional judgment scenarios.
  • The round will be strictly time-bound. The online portal will automatically submit responses when the allotted time expires.

Qualification Criteria: The top 50 teams will qualify for Stage 2.

Stage 2: The Red Flag Files – Forensic Investigation Round:

Date: 15th February, 2026
Format: Offline / In-Person Investigation Round
Duration: 60 minutes

The Red Flag Files is the centrepiece of the FRAudiT forensic investigation experience.

Teams will receive a sealed Audit File containing a realistic collection of business documents and must investigate the records to uncover interconnected fraud schemes.

Rather than simply identifying an isolated error, participants must connect the dots across multiple documents and build an evidence trail demonstrating how the records relate to a potential fraud.

The Audit File:

The file may contain documents such as:

  • Purchase Orders
  • Tax Invoices
  • GST Returns
  • Salary Registers
  • Bank Statements
  • Ledger Extracts
  • Inventory Records
  • Vendor Master
  • Email Communications
  • Delivery Challans
  • Payment Vouchers
  • Journal Entries
  • Fixed Asset Register
  • Audit Trail
  • Cash Book
  • Trial Balance

Investigation Tasks:

Teams will be required to:

  • Cross-reference multiple documents to trace transactions.
  • Identify numerical, date, and authorization inconsistencies.
  • Detect suspicious transactions and potential fraud schemes.
  • Build an evidence trail connecting anomalies to the suspected fraud.
  • Explain why each identified item is suspicious.
  • Recommend appropriate audit procedures, such as vouching, confirmation, and physical verification.
  • Prepare a structured Audit Observation Sheet documenting their findings.

The round is designed to replicate the working environment of a forensic audit engagement, where fraud is rarely contained within a single document and must instead be established through corroborating evidence.

Evaluation Criteria:

Teams will be evaluated on:

  • Red Flag Identification
  • Cross-Referencing Quality
  • Reasoning and Explanation
  • Recommended Audit Procedures
  • Presentation and Documentation

Qualification Criteria: The top 10 teams will advance to the Grand Finale.

Stage 3: Grand Finale – Crooked Books: The Cook & Catch Finale:

Date: 15th February, 2026
Format: Live Two-Phase Forensic Simulation

The Grand Finale transforms participants from investigators into both fraud creators and auditors, challenging them to understand not only how financial manipulation occurs but also how it can be detected.

The top 10 teams will be divided into two groups:

  • Group A – Fraud Accountants
  • Group B – Auditors

Teams will be paired head-to-head, with each pair receiving the same business scenario.

Phase 1 – The Cook:

Role: Fraud Accountants
Duration: 90 minutes

The Fraud Accountant teams will receive a genuine and internally consistent set of books and will have 90 minutes to introduce deliberate financial manipulation.

Possible manipulation techniques include:

  • Window dressing of financial statements
  • Revenue manipulation or premature revenue recognition
  • Fictitious or inflated expenses
  • Inventory inflation
  • Fake or shell vendors
  • Payroll manipulation
  • Unsupported or backdated journal entries
  • Concealment of liabilities
  • Artificial profit creation

The objective is not simply to falsify numbers but to construct a fraud scenario that appears believable, remains internally consistent, and is difficult to detect.

At the end of this phase, teams must submit their manipulated books and supporting fabricated documentation in a sealed and anonymized format.

Phase 2 – The Catch:

Role: Auditors
Duration: 90 minutes

The paired Auditor teams will receive the anonymized manipulated books and conduct a simulated audit investigation to uncover the financial manipulation.

Teams will be required to:

  • Investigate the records using audit techniques such as vouching, verification, analytical review, and ratio analysis.
  • Detect fraudulent activities.
  • Gather and document supporting evidence.
  • Prepare a structured Audit Observation Sheet.
  • Recommend further audit procedures.
  • Quantify the financial impact of identified frauds wherever possible.
  • Recommend corrective actions and internal control improvements.

Evaluation Criteria:

Fraud Accountant Teams will be evaluated on:

  • Creativity
  • Realism
  • Complexity
  • Ability to Conceal
  • Consistency
  • Documentation Quality

Auditor Teams will be evaluated on:

  • Detection Accuracy
  • Investigation Quality
  • Audit Approach
  • Evidence Collection
  • Professional Skepticism
  • Reporting Quality
  • Root Cause Analysis

Final Results:

  • At the conclusion of the Grand Finale, the strongest performances across the head-to-head matchups will be considered to determine the final Winner, Runner-Up, and Third Place.

The FRAudiT Experience:

  • FRAudiT is more than an auditing competition. It is a test of analytical thinking, professional skepticism, investigative ability, and the judgment required to distinguish credible financial reporting from deliberate manipulation.
  • From identifying risks in an online qualifier to tracing fraud through complex audit files and finally creating or uncovering manipulated financial statements, every stage challenges participants to think like real-world professionals.

FRAudiT – Where the Numbers Never Lie, But People Do.

title: CaseQuest
problem_statement:
CaseQuest is a business strategy and case-study competition, in Strategia'27 that brings together sharp analytical thinking, decision-making under pressure, and live presentation skills, testing participants across a series of progressively challenging rounds.

The competition begins with a two-part online qualifier, followed by a live branching case-study round, and concludes with a Grand Finale where the top teams present a brand-new case before a judging panel.

Participants will be evaluated on:

  • Depth of analysis
  • Clarity and structure of explanation
  • Quality of decision-making
  • Awareness of Trade-Offs and Risks
  • Ability to adapt strategy 
  • Consistency of decisions 

Guidelines:

  • Open to all registered UG/PG students.
  • Every round is played in teams of exactly 2 members - individual participation is not allowed at any stage.
  • Both members register together, and the same two-member team continues across all rounds; changes are allowed only in exceptional cases, at the Organizing Committee's discretion.
  • Carry a valid institutional ID card at all times - it may be checked at any stage.
  • Use of AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, etc.), internet search, or unauthorized notes/textbooks is strictly banned unless a round specifically allows it.
  • Teams may only communicate with their own teammate - contact with other teams or outside help is not permitted.
  • Only the materials explicitly permitted for a round may be used; all other devices and references are prohibited.
  • Only responses submitted in the official format/portal are evaluated - loose sheets or unofficial submissions are not considered.
  • Once submitted, responses are final and cannot be edited or resubmitted.
  • Violations such as AI use, plagiarism, impersonation, or unauthorized assistance lead to immediate disqualification.
  • Decisions of the Judges and Organizing Committee on evaluation, rules, and disputes are final and binding - no re-evaluation requests are entertained after results are declared.
  • The Organizing Committee may revise rules, format, or schedule if required, and will inform all participants in advance.

Stages & Timelines:

Stage 1: Online Qualifier (Dec'26)

  • Date: TBA
  • Time: TBA
  • Duration: TBA
  • Platform: Unstop
  • Guidelines: A two-part quiz that narrows the full field of registered teams down to the 50 teams who advance to Stage 2.
    • Part A - General Round (Current Affairs & Business Awareness): 
      • Open to all registered teams. Questions cover general current affairs together with foundational business and economic awareness.
      • All registered teams compete in Part A.
      • Each part includes a mix of regular questions and Star Questions - Star Questions carry bonus/higher marks than regular questions.
      • Scored on total marks earned (regular + Star Questions); the top teams (by cumulative score) advance to Part B.
      • Ties are broken by time taken to complete the round - the faster team is ranked higher.
    • Part B - Advanced Business Round:
      • A more in-depth quiz restricted to the top teams who cleared Part A, testing deeper business, finance, and industry knowledge.
      • Open only to the teams that qualify from Part A.
      • As in Part A, a mix of regular questions and higher-value Star Questions is used; Star Questions carry bonus marks.
      • Scored on total marks earned (regular + Star Questions); the top 50 teams (by cumulative score) advance to Stage 2.
      • Ties are broken by time taken to complete the round - the faster team is ranked higher.

Stage 2: The Case Study Round (15 Feb'27):

  • The centrepiece of the event. Teams work through a live, branching business case and are evaluated on the judgment behind every decision - not just the decisions themselves.
  • The Stage 2 case is released to the qualifying teams only once Stage 1 (Parts A and B) has concluded and the qualifying teams are confirmed.
  • Format:
    • Each case presents a company facing a real-world business challenge.
    • Each case consists of four sequential decision points. At every stage, participants choose one of the available strategic options.
    • The case follows a branching format - the option selected at each decision point determines the scenario and question presented next. Different teams may therefore encounter different paths through the same case.
    • At each decision point, teams must select one option, and justify the decision using logical reasoning, relevant business concepts, and practical considerations.
    • Once a decision is made at any stage, it is final and cannot be changed. Teams must continue the case based on the consequences of their previous choice.
    • Reasonable assumptions are permitted where necessary - they must be clearly stated and must align with the information given in the case.
    • Answers should be concise, focused, and directly relevant to the case facts; unrelated theory without practical application may not receive marks.
    • There is no single correct path or perfect answer - each option carries its own advantages and limitations.
    • Strong, well-supported reasoning is rewarded regardless of the path chosen; selecting an option without adequate justification receives limited marks even if the decision itself was appropriate.
    • At the conclusion of the case, each team presents and justifies its complete sequence of decisions to the judges - explaining the rationale behind their strategy and how their choices addressed the evolving business challenge.
    • Top teams (by cumulative score) advance to Stage 3, the Grand Finale.
    • The decision of the evaluators is final and binding.

Stage 3: Grand Finale (16 Feb'27) :

  • Held on Day 2 of the event - the final 25 teams receive a brand-new case study and present their analysis live before the judging panel.
  • A new case study, not seen in Stage 2, is introduced exclusively for the Grand Finale.
  • Finalist teams work through the new case and prepare their strategic recommendation and supporting reasoning.
  • Each team then presents and defends its analysis and decisions live before the judges.
  • Judges may question teams on their assumptions, trade-offs, and the consistency of their overall strategy.
  • Case format, preparation time, presentation time per team, and the final marking scheme: to be finalized by the Organizing Committee.

Think Strategically. Decide Boldly. Win the Case.

title: Wiki-Race
organizer: International Institute of Information Technology (IIIT), Bangalore
problem_statement:
Traverse the World's Largest Encyclopedia Using Nothing But Pure Lateral Thinking!

About the Event

Navigate the world's largest encyclopedia in the Wikipedia Race, an exciting and fast-paced online navigation challenge at Synergy ’26!

Teams race against the clock to traverse from a designated starting article to a seemingly unrelated target page using nothing but internal hyperlinks. With no search bars, no back buttons, and no external help allowed, it is a pure test of associative logic, lateral thinking, structural intuition, and rapid reading.

Race Rules & Navigation Constraints

  • Hyperlinks Only: Teams must navigate from the Start Page to the Target Page exclusively by clicking internal Wikipedia hyperlinks embedded within the article text.
  • Strict Prohibitions:
    • NO use of the search bar or search function inside or outside Wikipedia.
    • NO external websites, search engines, or secondary tools.
    • NO use of the browser’s "Back" or "Forward" buttons, history navigation, or keyboard shortcuts.
  • ️ Environment: Teams must operate within the Wikipedia ecosystem in full-screen mode for the entire duration of the race.
  • Single Screen Rule: The use of multiple browser tabs, split-screen searches, or distributing searches across different devices is strictly prohibited.

Rules & Regulations

  • Team Size: Teams must consist of exactly 3 members.
  • Fair Play: Any attempt to manipulate the browser, use script automation, or violate fair play rules will result in immediate disqualification.
  • Decisions: Organizers' decisions regarding disputes, time logs, or rule violations are final and binding.

Evaluation Criteria

  • Primary Metric: Time taken to successfully reach the designated Target Page from the Start Page.
  • Secondary Tie-Breaker: Total number of clicks / total links traversed to reach the target page.

problem_statement:
Official Competition Guidelines

Theme: The Things We Don’t Question

Organized Collaboratively by: D-LAB, Design Community (IISER Berhampur) with Art Clubs of Other IISERs

Overview & Thematic Brief:

We navigate daily life governed by unexamined habits, systemic norms, invisible social defaults, and unquestioned cultural agreements. ARTICULATE invites designers to interrogate the familiar challenging viewers to pause, reflect, and ask critical questions about the everyday realities we take for granted.

The Theme: The Things We Don't Question:

The Things We Don’t Question: Use the medium of graphic design to explore an assumption, belief, behaviour, practice, or system that has become so familiar that we rarely stop to question it. Your poster should make the familiar feel unfamiliar, something that makes people pause, think, and question what they usually take for granted.

ARTICULATE invites thinkers, illustrators, graphic designers, and creative minds across India to disrupt this visual complacency. Your artboard is an analytical instrument to surface hidden paradoxes, challenge accepted defaults, and construct visual metaphors that make viewers reconsider their everyday assumptions.

Prohibition on Use of Direct Personalities & Real-World Entities’ Identities.

    • @artclub_iisertirupati

Originality, Intellectual Property & Ethical Standards:

title: RoboRun 2027
venue_address: Student Activity Centre ,Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras
problem_statement:
All that you need to know about Robo Run

Guidelines:

  • A team shouldn't contain more than 5 members.
  • Bot Dimensions:  Smaller than 20 * 20  cms.

Participants are required to build an autonomous (not to be operated by a remote controller) line follower Bot, which can reach the end point of a maze in the shortest possible time. ( The line thickness will be 3-4 cm)

Video submission round:

This will be a submission round! You will have to prepare a small maze with two curves and show your line-following bot running on it. Shoot a video clip and attach the file.

Round -1:

  • In round 1, every team will be given a chance to run through the maze.
  • The top set of teams will be qualified to final round.
  • Shortlisting will be done based on the points you acquire. Refer to the problem statement for scoring criteria.

Round -2:

  • In round 2, the maze will additionally contain yellow blocks (10cm*10cm*10cm) directly placed on top of yellow squares.
  • These yellow blocks are to be displaced from the square. The sqaures will act as a checkpoint only if the block is displaced completely.
  • The maze and scoring pattern will be different between the two rounds.

Robo Run Description:

  • A Bot shall not be larger in length or width than 20 cm.
  • There are no restrictions on the height of a Bot.
  • A Bot should essentially comprise a drive motor to move it; a steering and turning method; sensors to detect the maze turns; sensors to ignore the action of the rest Bots and a source to provide power.
  • A Bot shall be self-contained (no remote controls). A Bot shall not use an energy source employing a combustion process.
  • Required sensors may be used for identifying the block and the maze line.
  • A Bot shall not leave any part of its body behind while navigating the maze.
  • A Bot shall not jump over, fly over, climb, scratch, cut, burn, mark, damage, or destroy the line of the maze. Judges can debar any machine if it is likely to cause damage to the maze in any way.

Registration Start: 28-10-2026

Registration deadline: 01-12-2026

Video submission round deadline: 15-12-2026

problem_statement:

INNOVISION 2026 | NIT Rourkela

Technology Beyond the Horizon:

Aetherhack is the national ideathon of INSPIRE, the Science and Research Club of NIT Rourkela, held as part of INNOVISION 2026. It gives college students across India a stage where original ideas are heard, questioned, and mentored by professors.   • Robotics: Machines, automation, and assistive systems that solve real problems.
  • Healthcare: Accessible, affordable, and assistive health-tech.
  • Open Track: Any bold idea that does not fit the themes above.

Eligibility:

    • Open to any college student from any institute across India.

    • Registration is only through the AetherHack page on Unstop.

    • Each team may submit only one idea.

    • All team members must attend the offline finale and represent the team.

    • Finalists must carry a valid college ID card to the finale.

Competition Structure:

Round 1 – Launch (Online, Unstop)

Teams submit one written idea abstract in PDF format. The abstract must state the theme, the problem, the proposed solution, how it works, and its expected impact, within a maximum of 2 A4 pages. Abstracts are screened on innovation, feasibility, and impact, and the top 10 teams are shortlisted and informed through Unstop and email.

Round 2 – Orbit (Offline, INNOVISION Finale)

Ten finalist teams compete at NIT Rourkela during INNOVISION, and all members of each team must be present and represent the team. Each team pitches the idea shortlisted in Round 1 for 7 minutes, followed by a 3-minute Q&A with the professor panel. Timings are strict. Slides are optional, and demos or prototypes are welcome but not required.

Sponsorship & Innovision Registration:

INSPIRE will sponsor one participant from each finalist team. All other team members must register separately on the official INNOVISION website to attend.

Judging Criteria:

    • Innovation (25): Originality of the idea and approach

    • Feasibility (25): Technical soundness and a realistic path to build it

    • Impact (25): Relevance to the theme and value to real users

    • Pitch & Q&A (25): Clarity of the pitch and quality of answers

Rules & Guidelines:

  • Register only through the official AetherHack page on Unstop.
  • Submit one abstract in PDF format before the deadline. Late, incomplete, or non-PDF submissions are not considered.
  • The idea must be your own work. Copied or plagiarised abstracts are disqualified.
  • Finalist teams must pitch the idea shortlisted in Round 1. Switching to a different idea is not allowed.
  • All team members must attend the offline finale and represent the team.
  • Only one participant per finalist team is sponsored by INSPIRE. Remaining members must register on the INNOVISION website.
  • Report to the venue by the announced reporting time. A no-show forfeits the slot.
  • Bring your slides (if any) along with a backup copy.
  • Any breach of these rules can lead to disqualification at any stage.
  • The decisions of the judges and the INSPIRE organising team are final.
  • Registering for AetherHack means you accept the rules.

Rewards & Support:

  • 3-day INNOVISION experience for winners
  • Mentorship and support from professors to develop your idea further
  • Sponsorship for one participant from each finalist team, arranged by INSPIRE
  • Recognition at a national-level student ideathon

problem_statement:
Treasure Restoration

Find the forgotten. Fuse the familiar. Create the future.

What if yesterday’s failed products could become tomorrow’s breakthrough innovations?

Every discontinued product has a story, and every unsuccessful idea holds the possibility of a comeback. Treasure Restoration challenges you to uncover that hidden potential, combine forgotten products, and transform them into innovative concepts with real market potential.

This is your opportunity to think creatively, solve problems, and prove that a product’s story doesn’t have to end when it leaves the market.

Round 1: The Quiz

  • Test your analytical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving skills through set of questions:
  • Qualifying participants will advance to the next round.

Round 2: The Product Redesign Challenge

  • One forgotten product. One fresh idea. A second chance at success.
  • Choose any one legacy/commercially matured tech innovation (for eg: Pendrive, Landline telephone, CD's, Cassette, etc) of your choice and redesign it into an innovative product concept that offers a unique value proposition and demonstrates real market demand.
  • But there’s a twist: you must choose one target age group and consumer archetype that you would like to target from the below options given below while redesigning your product.

Target Age Group:

  • Option 1: Gen Z  (aged 14-29 years)
  • Option 2: Gen X  (aged 46-61 years)

Target Consumer Archetype:

  • Option 1: Value Seekers- those that look for maximum benefits at a reasonable price.
  • Option 2: Premium Spenders- those that are willing to pay more for quality, experience and innovation.

Your submission: PPT deck of up to 5 slides

Submit your PowerPoint deck on Unstop. Make every slide count!

  • Slide 1: Title slide: Your new product’s name, logo, and tagline.
  • Slide 2: The Legacy & The Opportunity -  Identify the original technology and it's purpose, highlighting its limitations, and explain the opportunity to reinvent it for today's market.
  • Slide 3: The Product Reimagined - Showcase the redesigned product through a sketch, digital mockup, 3D render or AI-generated visual.Highlight its key features and technological innovations.Explain its unique selling proposition.
  • Slide 4: Target Audience & Commercial Feasibility-  Identify your intended customers, their needs, and the problem your product solves and the pricing strategy. Propose a price and explain why it is reasonable.
  • Slide 5: Go To Market Strategy for your product.
  • Your concept will be evaluated on creativity, relevance to the condition chosen, customer value, feasibility, pricing, and marketing potential. The top teams will qualify for Round 3.

Round 3: The Restoration Pitch

  • You’ve built the idea. Now, test whether people believe in it.
  • Shortlisted teams must submit a 30-60 second AI-generated advertisement demonstrating the product concept, its key benefits, and its appeal to the target audience.
  • This round will assess:
  • Creativity: Present your redesigned product in an original and memorable way.
  • Understand Your Audience: Tailor your advertisement to the chosen age group and consumer archetype.
  • Tell a Compelling Story: Capture attention and communicate your message effectively with AI-generated advertisement.

Important Guidelines:

  • Follow the condition assigned to your team throughout Round 2.
  • The Round 2 PPT must contain no more than 5 slides.
  • The Round 3 video must be 30-60 seconds long.
  • Obtain permission before recording or using another person's feedback.
  • Explain how both original products contribute to your final concept.
  • Ensure that your proposed pricing and feasibility are supported by reasonable assumptions.
  • Follow the submission deadlines and instructions announced by the organisers.

The mission: Don't just bring products back. Restore their purpose, reinvent their value, and give forgotten ideas a future.

Are you ready to turn yesterday’s failures into tomorrow’s treasures?

title: True Fan AI - The Synthetic Scale-Up
problem_statement:
About the Case:

TrueFan AI: The Synthetic Scale-Up is a strategic business case challenge under the Founders’ Office, Executive Operations & Corporate Strategy track, in association with Masters’ Union School of Business.

Founded in Gurugram in 2020, TrueFan AI evolved from a B2C celebrity fan-engagement platform into a B2B enterprise generative AI video infrastructure company. With over 100 enterprise clients, support for 175+ localized languages, and ₹17.1 crore in FY25 revenue, the company is experiencing rapid growth alongside critical operational, financial, and strategic challenges.

Participants will step into the role of Chief of Staff to TrueFan AI’s CEO, tasked with eliminating executive bottlenecks, redesigning monetization and unit economics, and resolving a high-stakes investor conflict while preparing the company for global expansion.

Problem Statement:

With only 12 months of runway and significant GPU infrastructure requirements, how can TrueFan AI transform its rapid growth into a profitable, operationally efficient, and globally scalable enterprise AI business?

Participants must address three key pillars:

Executive Operations & Resource Allocation

  • Design a three-tier delegation matrix to reduce the CEO’s workload from 110 to 45 hours per week.
  • Optimize GPU compute and engineering bandwidth between batch video generation and real-time AI video agents.
  • Evaluate the ₹20 lakh charity-bond Chief of Staff recruitment model, considering its impact on talent quality, brand perception, socioeconomic diversity, and operational effectiveness.

Monetization, Unit Economics & AI Governance

  • Calculate baseline Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) and the LTV ratio.
  • Redesign pricing for light, mid-market, and power enterprise customers through platform fees, usage-based GPU charges, and celebrity-avatar surcharges.
  • Develop a financial model targeting at least 60% gross margin, monthly churn of 2.5% or less, and an LTV ratio of at least 3×.
  • Establish robust celebrity image-rights, approval SLA, and AI-generated content safety frameworks to prevent deepfake misuse and unauthorized endorsements.

Boardroom Mediation & Strategic Alignment

  • Resolve the conflict between Bajaj Finance’s demand for exclusive BFSI rights and Series A investors’ push for global SaaS expansion.
  • Protect relationships with existing BFSI clients while addressing strategic investor requirements.
  • Calculate TrueFan AI’s post-money valuation and develop a three-step boardroom compromise plan that balances commercial partnerships, data security, and global scalability.

Flow of Events:

Round 1: Executive Screening Deck — Online Submission

Participants submit a 2-slide PDF proposal covering:

  • The CEO delegation matrix and operational restructuring.
  • Baseline LTV and LTV calculations.

Round 2: Strategic Pitch Deck & Financial Model — Virtual Submission

Shortlisted participants submit a 5-slide strategic deck supported by a financial model covering:

  • Monetization redesign and financial projections.
  • Unit economics and profitability improvement.
  • The boardroom compromise plan and strategic investor alignment.

Round 3: Live Boardroom Simulation — National Finals

The top 5 finalist teams present their recommendations live to a panel of venture capital investors and startup founders, demonstrating strategic thinking, financial rigour, and executive decision-making.

Mystery Box Challenge: The Spot Crisis

Exactly 10 minutes before presenting, each finalist team receives an emergency regulatory alert concerning the MeitY Synthetic Media & Deepfake Transparency Directive 2026, as described in the case brief.

Teams must rapidly adapt their real-time AI video agent roadmap, estimate compliance costs, and propose cryptographic watermarking and mandatory 24-hour ethical verification while preserving a low-latency user experience.

Evaluation Criteria — 100 Marks:

Operational Realism & Delegation Matrix — 35 Marks

  • Feasibility of reducing CEO workload from 110 to 45 hours per week.
  • GPU capital expenditure (CAPEX) roadmap and engineering resource allocation.
  • Critical evaluation of the talent acquisition model.

Unit Economics & Strategic Pricing Redesign — 30 Marks

  • Accuracy of baseline LTV and LTV calculations.
  • Innovation in pricing architecture and quantitative financial modelling.
  • Achievement of gross margin, churn, and LTV targets.
  • Celebrity service-level agreements (SLAs), image-rights governance, and brand-safety controls.

Board Governance & Equity Valuation Math — 25 Marks

  • Correct calculation of the $40 million post-money valuation.
  • Strategic positioning against global AI video competitors.
  • A practical three-step investor compromise plan.
  • Protection of existing BFSI client relationships and recurring revenue.

Presentation & Mystery Box Spot Crisis — 10 Marks

  • Clarity of presentation, slide design, and executive storytelling.
  • Adaptability, compliance-cost estimation, and response to the regulatory crisis.

What Participants Will Gain:

  • Hands-on experience in executive decision-making and operational restructuring.
  • Practical exposure to SaaS monetization, financial modelling, and unit economics.
  • Experience in investor negotiations, stakeholder management, and boardroom decision-making.
  • Insights into AI governance, deepfake safety, image-rights management, and regulatory preparedness.
  • The opportunity to demonstrate strategic thinking, problem-solving, and adaptability under time pressure.

The Challenge: Build a roadmap that balances growth, profitability, operational excellence, and investor alignment to transform TrueFan AI into a sustainable, globally scalable enterprise AI business.

Track: Founders’ Office, Executive Operations & Corporate Strategy

Mantravat is a case study competition (strategy-based) organised by ConsultU,Consulting and Strategy Club of IIM Udaipur, in which students from across the country can showcase their consulting skills and compete against the best minds.

  • The competition will last three rounds and will put all participants' diverse skill sets to the test.
  • At the end of each round, the shortlisted teams will be invited to participate in the subsequent rounds.

Round 1: Strat Hunt

A quiz that demands a broad analytical mindset and primarily revolves around consulting frameworks and aptitude

Round 2: Case Crunch Challenge

Teams that advance from the initial round will move on to the second round, where they will be presented with an actual case study challenge provided by a global company. In this phase, teams will be required to thoroughly assess the case and submit their recommendations through a PowerPoint presentation

Round 3: Consult Finale

Teams that successfully make it through the second round will progress to the final stage, during which they will present their comprehensive case solution to the jury via an online platform.

Rules and Guidelines:

  • The competition is open to all students pursuing postgraduate and undergraduate degrees
  • No participant should be a member of more than one team
  • A team can have 3 to 4 members
  • Only one response per team will be entertained
  • You cannot modify your answer post-submission
  • In the event of a dispute, the organizer's and judging panel's decisions shall be final

Details of individual rounds:

  • The competition is divided into three rounds, with the first round consisting of a quiz that requires general analytical thinking and is primarily focussed on developing sustainable solutions.
  • The shortlisted teams from round one will compete in the second round, which will feature a real case study problem statement from a global firm. The teams must analyze this case and make a recommendation in the form of a PowerPoint presentation with holistic solutions in 4-5 slides.
  • Shortlisted teams from the second round will advance to the final round, where they will present their complete case solution to the Jury.
  • All teams that qualify for round 2 will be awarded a participation certificate from IIM Udaipur.
