title: Follow The Money: Innovation Challenge Powered by PayU
problem_statement:
All that you need to know about Follow the Money: Innovation Challenge Powered by PayU

Official WhatsApp: https://chat.whatsapp.com/DqZ5BeA0Pd19FODfbdppFI

The Follow the Money: Innovation Challenge is a national innovation competition organised by the Centre for Software and Information Technology Management (CSITM), IIM Bangalore, in partnership with PayU. The challenge invites students from all disciplines to tackle a real-world problem in digital payment security and financial fraud, and to develop innovative, practical solutions that bridge technology, business, policy and human behaviour.

Every day, fraudsters find new ways to slip past the systems built to stop them. What if the next solution came from you?

Problem Statement: The Bakery That Takes Bets
Payment providers onboard thousands of new merchants every day. Some use genuine documents to open accounts, then use them to collect money for banned activities such as illegal betting. How can a payment provider detect and respond to when a merchant's transactions stop matching the business it claims to run, without penalising honest merchants whose sales change for valid reasons?
**Full problem statement with background is available in the rulebook.**

Eligibility:
• Open to college students from all disciplines across India
• Team size: 1–4 members per team
• Inter-college teams are allowed
• Each student may be part of only one team

Competition Structure:

Round 1 – Online Submission
Teams must submit a presentation deck of up to 8 slides (PDF) describing their solution and a video of up to 2 minutes explaining their solution. The video can take any creative format. Submissions will be evaluated on problem understanding, innovation and originality, solution design and approach, feasibility and real-world impact, and presentation and communication. The top teams will advance to the on-campus finale.

Round 2 – On-Campus Grand Finale
Finalist teams will be invited to IIM Bangalore on 26 November 2026 to present their solutions at a live exhibition. Each team will showcase its solution at its own stall, through a pitch, poster and demo or walkthrough, as judges visit each stall to evaluate the ideas and interact with the team. Displaying a working prototype is mandatory for technical solutions. The event will conclude with the announcement of winners.

Note:

  • Finalists must arrange and bear their own travel and accommodation expenses for the on-campus event.
  • Check out the rulebook attached for more details.

Submission Requirements:

Each team must submit a single Google Drive folder link containing:
• Presentation (PDF, up to 8 slides), named TeamName_Presentation.pdf
• Video (up to 2 minutes), named TeamName_Video

Folder requirements: 
• Name the folder with your team name, e.g. TeamName_FollowTheMoney
• Set the folder's sharing access to "Anyone with the link can view"
• Submit only the folder link on Unstop before the Round 1 deadline
• Do not edit or add files to the folder after the deadline

Presentation requirements:
• Maximum length: 8 slides, submitted as a PDF.
• Should cover your idea and what makes it distinctive, how the solution works, how it addresses      fraudulent activity, how it could be implemented in practice, and its expected impact.
• Should be clear, well structured and easy to follow

Video requirements:
• Maximum length: 2 minutes
• Any creative format, such as a short film, mock advertisement, scenario-based demonstration, animation, storytelling piece or product pitch. Technical teams must also build and demonstrate a working prototype.
• Should clearly explain or demonstrate the solution 

(Optional)
• GitHub repository (for technical solutions)
• Supporting documents, such as a policy draft, process flow or business model (as a PDF in the folder.)

Evaluation Criteria:
Solutions will be assessed on:
• Problem Understanding
• Originality of Idea
• Solution Design and Approach 
• Feasibility
• Real-World Impact
• Presentation Quality

Use of AI:
AI tools are allowed, as long as your team is the one creating the solution. Submissions are judged on originality, so generic AI-generated ideas without your own insight and contribution will score lower.

Prizes:
PayU Prize Pool of ₹70,000
• First Place: ₹40,000
• Second Place: ₹20,000
• Third Place: ₹10,000
• Certificates from IIM Bangalore for all participants
• Goodies, including T-shirts and badges, for finalists on campus.

For more information, including the full problem statement, evaluation weightage and rules, please refer to the Rulebook.

title: Capital Quest
problem_statement:
About the Opportunity

Capital Quest is a finance competition organized by Finomina, the Finance Club of IIM Udaipur, as part of Solaris, IIM Udaipur’s Annual Management Fest. The competition tests participants’ analytical thinking, logical reasoning, and financial decision-making through puzzles and portfolio creation. Open to B-School students across the country, it gives participants a chance to apply practical finance concepts and investment skills in a competitive setting.

Guidelines:

  • Team Size: 2 members.
  • No changes in team composition will be allowed after registration closes.
  • Participants must follow the submission requirements for each round.
  • All submissions must be the team’s original work.
  • Any form of plagiarism, malpractice, or unfair means will lead to disqualification.

Structure and Rounds:

Round 1: Puzzles & Aptitude Test

  • Format: Logic and Aptitude Puzzles.
  • Task: Participants will solve a set of logic and aptitude puzzles testing clarity of thought, reasoning ability, and speed.
  • Progression: Top scorers will qualify for Round 2.

Round 2: Portfolio Formation

Part 1: Portfolio Creation

  • Virtual Capital: ₹100 Crore per team.
  • Task: Teams will allocate the given capital across a set of assets provided by the organizers.
  • Submission: An Excel sheet containing the available assets and their fixed prices will be shared. Teams must enter the amount they wish to invest in each asset and submit the completed sheet.
  • Cash Holding: Teams may keep a portion of the ₹100 Crore as cash for use in Part 2.
  • Objective: Build an optimal and diversified portfolio focusing on growth potential, valuation accuracy, and risk balance.

Part 2: Portfolio Rebalancing

  • Task: Teams will revisit and optimize their original portfolio based on updated market conditions and asset prices.
  • Original Portfolio: Teams must first re-enter their previous portfolio with the same assets and capital allocation to view its performance.
  • Reallocation: Teams can reallocate up to 40% of their initial portfolio value, excluding unallocated cash.
  • Changes Allowed: Teams may fully or partially sell previously held assets or add new securities.
  • Rationale: Teams must submit the reasoning behind both their initial investment decisions and their portfolio reallocation in the dedicated sheet.
  • Final Results: Results will be based on asset prices at a cutoff date and time communicated separately.

Evaluation Criteria:

Teams will be evaluated based on predefined criteria including portfolio diversification, valuation accuracy, risk balance, and returns.

Rules:

  • Participants must follow all timelines and submission requirements. Late submissions will not be accepted.
  • Participants must arrange the required internet connection, system, and other technical requirements in advance.
  • Plagiarism, malpractice, unfair means, or external help during quiz or proctored rounds will result in disqualification.
  • All portfolio submissions must be the team’s original work.
  • Teams must follow the specified submission format, including Excel/Sheets for portfolio allocation and PDF/Word wherever applicable.
  • Incomplete or corrupt files will not be evaluated.
  • All official communication will be through the registered email IDs or event platforms.
  • Teams are responsible for regularly checking updates and instructions.
  • Queries should be raised well before the respective deadlines.
  • The decision of the judges and organizers will be final and binding.
  • Requests for re-evaluation will not be entertained.
  • Participants are expected to maintain professionalism and decorum throughout the event.

title: Saudagar 2026
problem_statement:
About the Opportunity

Saudagar 2026 is the flagship business strategy competition organized by Saksham, the Entrepreneurship Cell of IIM Udaipur, as part of Solaris 2026, IIM Udaipur’s Annual Management Fest. Built around “Build. Acquire. Integrate.”, Saudagar challenges participants to think like entrepreneurs, build a commercially viable business proposition, defend their decisions, and adapt their strategy as the competition progresses.

Guidelines:

  • Eligibility: Open to undergraduate and postgraduate students.
  • Team Size: Teams can consist of 1 to 3 members.
  • Participation: A participant can be a member of only one team.
  • Mode: All rounds will be conducted online.
  • Originality: All submissions must be the team’s original work.
  • Shortlisting: Only shortlisted teams will advance to subsequent rounds.

Structure and Rounds:

Round 1: Business Intelligence Challenge

  • Format: Online timed quiz.
  • Number of Questions: 30 questions.
  • Duration: 10 minutes.
  • Coverage: Business and corporate awareness, strategy, marketing, finance and economics, startups, logical reasoning, data interpretation, and business situations.
  • Attempts: Each team will get one attempt.
  • Progression: The bottom 10% of teams will be eliminated. The remaining teams will qualify for Round 2.

Round 2: Build the Business

  • Format: Business Case Analysis and PPT Submission.
  • Duration: 5 days.
  • Task: Qualified teams will receive a common business case and develop an original and commercially viable business proposition.
  • Submission: Maximum 5 slides, excluding the title slide and appendix.
  • Submission Focus: Core business problem | Customer and market opportunity | Proposed solution | Business model and revenue logic | Competitive landscape | Go-to-market strategy | Financial viability | Implementation | Key risks and mitigations
  • Progression: Submissions will be evaluated by the judging panel. The strongest teams will qualify for the Boardroom

Round 3: The Boardroom

  • Format: Live Business Presentation and Panel Q&A.
  • Duration: 15 minutes per team.
  • Task: Teams will present their business proposition and defend their assumptions, choices, financial logic, competitive position, and execution plan before the judging panel.
  • Progression: The strongest teams will advance to the Marketplace.

Round 4: The Marketplace

  • Format: Live Marketplace and Capability Acquisition Round.
  • Duration: 2 hours.
  • Virtual Capital: ₹1 Crore per team.
  • Task: Teams will identify capabilities they need, such as distribution, customer acquisition, technology, marketing, partnerships, pricing, or supply chain, and compete to acquire them from other teams.
  • Bidding: Each team can make a maximum of 2 bids.
  • Integration: Acquired capabilities must be meaningfully integrated into the team’s original business proposition.
  • Progression: Teams will use their Marketplace decisions to revise their business proposition for the Final Pitch.

Round 5: Final Pitch

  • Format: Final Business Presentation and Q&A.
  • Duration: 15 minutes per team.
  • Task: Teams will present their revised business proposition and explain what they acquired, why they acquired it, how they allocated their capital, how it was integrated, and how it strengthened their business.
  • Outcome: Final winners will be determined by the strength of the business proposition and the decisions made throughout the competition

Evaluation Criteria:

Teams will be evaluated on problem understanding, quality of analysis and insights, strategic thinking, commercial viability, feasibility and execution, differentiation, decisions under constraints, Marketplace strategy and capital allocation, integration of acquired capabilities, clarity of communication, and response to questions.

Prizes:

Total Prize Pool: ₹15,000

  • Winner: ₹10,000
  • Runner-up: ₹5,000

Rules:

  • Each participant can be a part of only one team.
  • All submissions must be the team’s original work.
  • Plagiarism, fabrication of data, misrepresentation, or use of another team’s work will result in disqualification.
  • Teams must follow the prescribed submission format and deadlines.

title: Gambit 2035: The Great Power Game
problem_statement:
How the Game Works

Leverage Points (LP)

Leverage Points are the primary in-game currency.

Each nation begins with a different level of power and has a different maximum possible LP score. Final performance is therefore measured relative to each nation's own maximum potential, keeping the competition balanced across nations.

Secret Agendas

  • Every nation receives a confidential objective that can earn bonus LP.
  • Your Secret Agenda may force you to pursue an objective that conflicts with your nation's obvious interests, creating an additional layer of strategic decision-making.

Treaty Registry

  • If it isn't registered, it isn't real.
  • Only agreements submitted through the official Treaty Registry are enforceable.
  • Promises made in private chats are cheap talk unless backed by a registered agreement.

PNN: PiE News Network

  • The PNN will deliver breaking developments throughout the game.
  • Expect market shocks, diplomatic leaks, surprise events, rival moves and changing conditions through Discord and Solaris Instagram Stories.

Day 1 Scoring

  • Game Performance: 50%
  • Diplomatic Cable: 50%

Advancement:

  • The winner of each world + the 4 highest-scoring runners-up advance.
  • 12 teams advance to Day 2.

Day 2 Scoring

  • Game Performance + Secret Agenda: 40%
  • Crisis Report: 60%
  • Top 3 teams from each world advance.
  • 6 finalists reach Day 3.

Day 3 Scoring

  • 2035 Accord: 30%
  • Summit Address: 40%
  • Press Conference: 30%

Participation

  • Team Size: 2 to 3 members
  • Maximum Teams: 48

The 48 teams will be divided into 8 worlds, with 6 nations in each world.

If registrations exceed the cap, participants will be shortlisted through a 20-minute entry quiz covering game theory and geoeconomics.

WHY PARTICIPATE? 
GAMBIT 2035 isn't a conventional case competition. 
You won't receive a case and simply present a solution. 
You will create the case yourself through your decisions. 
You will have to:

  •  Make decisions with incomplete information 
  • Negotiate with competing interests
  • Build and break alliances
  • Understand incentives 
  • React to unexpected shocks 
  • Quantify economic consequences 
  • Read your rivals 
  • Apply game theory in real time 
  • Defend your decisions under pressure

In GAMBIT 2035, there is no fixed solution. 
There is only the move you make and the world it creates. 
Enter the game. Shape the world.

title: Your Idea. Our Capital: 50k Sprint (Season 2)
problem_statement:
About the Opportunity:

Idea to Income: 50K is an entrepreneurship challenge by the InteractUP Startup Committee that gives selected teams the opportunity to turn their business ideas into revenue-generating ventures. Selected teams can receive ₹10,000 per month for 5 months, amounting to up to ₹50,000 in funding, to build, execute, and validate their ideas.

Unlike a traditional business plan competition, this challenge focuses on execution, revenue generation, and measurable business outcomes.

What Is the Challenge?

  • Pitch a practical and scalable business idea.
  • Explain how you will start and operate the business.
  • Show how you will use the ₹10,000 monthly funding.
  • Generate real revenue and profits through execution.
  • Track your business performance every month.
  • Demonstrate how you can recover the investment and generate profit.

This isn't just an idea-pitching competition. Your idea will be tested through execution and numbers.

Make sure you are part of the following group for regular updates: https://chat.whatsapp.com/HrgxdxPQEn9DAlp4PFH6d0

Round 1 - 90-Second Business Pitch

Submit a 1 to 1.5-minute video covering:

  • Business Idea - What are you planning to build?
  • Problem - What problem or need are you addressing?
  • Launch Plan - How will you start the business? Outline the expenses you expect to incur and the revenue you aim to generate, month by month, over the five-month period.
  • Detailed 1st month description
  • Capital Plan - How will you use the ₹10,000 received each month?
  • Revenue Model - How will you generate revenue? What will your costs, revenue and expected profits look like?
  • 5-Month Plan - How will you grow and improve the business?
  • Investment Recovery - How will you recover the investment while generating profit?

Your video should demonstrate a clear, practical, and financially viable plan. We are more interested in the numbers and execution strategy than just the business idea. Explain how you will acquire customers, what you will pitch to them, your expected ticket size, and who your target customers are. If you are proposing a product, explain the per-unit cost, sourcing or manufacturing process, pricing, and expected profit margin.

Round 2 - Interview:

Shortlisted participants will move to the interview round.

The interview will evaluate:

  • Practicality of the business idea
  • Financial viability
  • Execution strategy
  • Revenue potential
  • Scalability
  • Understanding of the target market
  • Ability to use limited capital effectively

Round 2 dates will be announced soon.

Based on the interview evaluation:

  • Final teams will be selected.

The ₹50,000 Opportunity:

₹10,000 × 5 MONTHS = ₹50,000

Selected teams can receive:

  • ₹10,000 every month
  • For 5 consecutive months
  • Up to ₹50,000 total funding
  • Funding released progressively based on the agreed plan and evaluation framework

Monthly Performance Tracking:

Every month, the business will be evaluated on:

Capital Used → Revenue → Costs → Profit → Growth

You will be expected to demonstrate:

  • How the capital was utilised
  • Revenue generated
  • Customer/business growth, Progress against the original plan
  • The opportunity will operate on a profit-sharing basis.
  • Profit sharing will continue as per the terms agreed with the selected teams until the applicable recovery/profit objective is achieved.
  • Detailed terms will be communicated to shortlisted/final teams.

What Can You Build?

You are not restricted to a particular industry.

Healthy Food:

  • Meal concepts
  • Beverages
  • Nutrition-focused products

Experiences & Events:

  • Stranger meets
  • Cultural events
  • Community experiences
  • Curated social gatherings

️ Travel & Experiences:

  • Strangers' trips
  • Weekend experiences
  • Local tours
  • Curated group activities

These are only examples. Your idea can come from any sector, provided it has a practical path to execution and profitability. 

Preferred Location:

Idea → Execution → Revenue → Profit

title: ECOGEN: National Sustainability Case Competition, 2026
problem_statement:
Overview

ECOGEN 2026 is a nationwide B-school case competition designed to challenge students with authentic business challenges viewed through an Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework. Organised at IMT Nagpur, the competition brings together participants to demonstrate strategic foresight, analytical depth, and effective communication. The journey begins with an online assessment of foundational ESG knowledge, moves to the analysis of a short business case, and culminates in a live presentation of strategic solutions before an industry professional.

Why Participate?

  • Solve realistic ESG dilemmas faced by Indian and global companies.
  • Build skills in strategy, sustainability, and stakeholder analysis.
  • Present your recommendations before industry professionals at the grand finale.
  • Compete for cash prizes and certificates.
  • Strengthen your profile through participation in a national-level B-school competition.

Eligibility

  • Open to all MBA/PGDM students across India.
  • Team size: 2–3 members.
  • Intra-college and cross-specialisation teams are allowed; teams must be from the same college.
  • A valid college ID is required for verification.
  • One participant may be part of only one team.

Competition Structure

The competition consists of three rounds. Teams will first complete an online ESG quiz. Shortlisted teams will then analyse a mini case and submit a concise recommendation deck. Finalists will present their strategic solutions before an industry jury at the grand finale.

Round Details

Round 1 – ESG Quiz (Online)

  • An objective quiz covering ESG concepts, frameworks, regulations, and current business-sustainability news.
  • Topics may include GRI, SASB, TCFD, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs).
  • The quiz will contain 45 questions to be completed in 30 minutes.
  • There is no negative marking.

Round 2 – Mini Case Challenge (Online)

  • Shortlisted teams will receive a 1–2 page ESG case with data exhibits.
  • Teams must submit a recommendation in a deck of no more than 5 slides, in PDF format, within 36 hours.
  • Submissions will be evaluated by a panel of judges.
  • Teams should identify the core problem, analyse stakeholders, compare options and trade-offs, recommend a course of action, and outline risks and implementation steps.

Round 3 – Grand Finale (Offline/Online at IMT Nagpur)

  • Finalists will present their solutions live before an industry jury.
  • A new case will be released one day before the competition.
  • Each team will have 10 minutes to present, followed by 5 minutes of Q&A.
  • Travel and accommodation will not be provided.

Guidelines

Round 1: Quiz Guidelines

  • The quiz will be hosted on Unstop. Attempt limit: one attempt per team, or per member as decided by the organisers.
  • Use only one device per participant and keep the quiz tab in focus. Tab switching may lead to disqualification.
  • In the event of a tie, the time taken will be used as the tiebreaker.
  • External assistance and AI tools are prohibited during the quiz.

Round 2: Mini Case Submission Guidelines

  • Submit a maximum 5-slide deck in PDF format.
  • The deck should cover problem identification; key stakeholders and their interests; options considered and trade-offs; the final recommendation; and risks with an implementation plan.
  • Use relevant ESG frameworks and quantify your analysis wherever possible.
  • Plagiarism or AI-copied content will lead to disqualification.

Round 3: Grand Finale Guidelines

  • Finalists must carry a valid college ID for the campus event.
  • Travel and accommodation arrangements are the responsibility of participants.

title: Mark to Market : The Arbitrage Principle
organizer: Kirori Mal College (KMC), University of Delhi, Delhi
problem_statement:
The Commerce Society of Kirori Mal College presents Mark to Market : The Arbitrage Principle, a high-stakes valuation simulation where sharp analysis is your greatest asset and every decision comes at a price. In a market where perception can be misleading and information can change everything, you are handed one challenge: identify what an asset is truly worth before the rest of the market catches on.

  • Step into a world where every asset holds a different promise and every valuation carries a risk. From uncovering the nature of unfamiliar investments to decoding market signals, weighing competing financial attributes, and navigating a live auction, you will work with limited capital, incomplete information, and very little room for error. Here, one wrong assumption can distort an entire valuation, an inflated bid can drain your purse, and an overlooked opportunity can cost you the win.
  • Across a journey of analysis, negotiation, and strategic decision-making, your choices will shape the outcome. You must interpret the market, assess the value beneath the surface, and decide when to commit and when to hold back. This is a test of financial understanding, commercial instinct, and the ability to make calculated decisions under pressure. Will you recognise an undervalued opportunity, or pay a premium for an asset the market has already overrated?
  • Details will be revealed in time. All you need to know is that price and value are rarely the same, information is never the whole picture, and the smartest move is not always the highest bid. Your greatest tools will not just be your calculations, but your judgment, your adaptability, and your ability to read the room.
  • Think like an analyst, bid like an investor, and know the worth of what others overlook. Every assumption, every alliance, and every bid will decide whether your portfolio becomes a masterstroke or an expensive mistake.

title: Pixel2Path 2027
problem_statement:
Event Description:

  • Pixel2Path is an autonomous robotics competition where teams build a robot that turns digital images into physical drawings on paper, with no human intervention.
  • It combines Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Path Planning, Robotics, and Mechatronics.

Online Submission: The teams have to submit the 'Documentation', 'BOM', and 'Video-Demonstration' of the bot. (Non-Eliminatory Round)

  • Round 1: The robot receives an unseen image (PNG/NPY), processes it, plans an optimized path, and draws it on an A3 sheet within the allotted time.
  • Round 2 (Draw): Each team gets an image with 40% of its strokes randomly removed. Their trained AI model predicts the missing strokes, and the robot draws the completed image (visible and predicted strokes) on A3 sheet.
  • Round 2 (Predict): Teams get 10 unseen masked images and predict the originals. Each is scored by SSIM.

Teams get 100 image pairs two weeks before the event. On event day they get the full 5,000-pair dataset and a 60-minute window to train their model on Kaggle.

Rules:

  • Teams must have 3 to 5 members, with one designated Team Lead for official communication.
  • Teams must bring a fully assembled and tested robot (no on-day mechanical builds), a laptop with all software pre-installed, the trained model weights file, a 12V DC power supply, and a USB cable for Arduino.
  • It must be a 3-axis plotter (X, Y, and a Z pen-lift) with independent control of each axis.
  • The robot must have an Emergency Kill Switch that completely stops all motion.
  • Training must be done in a Kaggle Notebook on event day with GPU acceleration, with Internet toggled OFF.
  • Training must be from scratch, using only the provided 5,000-image dataset. Data augmentation is allowed.

title: EconoNations
organizer: Shaheed Bhagat Singh Evening College (SBSEC), University of Delhi (DU), New Delhi
problem_statement:
Overview

Negotiate. Strategise. Shape the Global Economy.

What if you were responsible for running an entire country's economy? Could you manage scarce resources, navigate global crises, negotiate trade deals, and secure economic growth while protecting your nation's interests?

EconoNations is an economics-based simulation competition that places participants in the role of national policymakers navigating an interconnected global economy. Through strategic resource trading, negotiations, and responses to changing global developments, teams must make decisions that shape their country's economic performance and long-term prospects.

The competition combines economic reasoning, international trade, resource management, geopolitical strategy, and decision-making in a dynamic simulation of the global economy.

Structure

Round 1: The Economics Quiz

Format: Quiz | Elimination Round

  • The competition begins with an economics quiz designed to test participants' understanding of economic concepts, international trade, global affairs, and their real-world applications.
  • Participants will be assessed on their conceptual clarity, analytical thinking, and awareness of the economic forces shaping the world.
  • Objective: Shortlist the 12 qualifying teams that advance to the next stage.

Round 2: Nation Allocation and Economic Setup

Format: Country Allocation | Strategy Formation

  • The 12 qualifying teams will be assigned countries through a random allocation process. Each team will represent its assigned nation and receive an initial economic profile consisting of resources, financial capacity, and other economic strengths and limitations.
  • Teams must study their country's starting position, identify its comparative advantages and dependencies, and formulate an initial strategy for navigating the global economy.

Round 3: The Global News Simulation

Format: Three News Rounds | Negotiation and Resource Trading

  • This is the core of EconoNations.
  • Across three rounds, teams will respond to changing global developments that influence resource availability, market demand, trade relations, and economic priorities.
  • Each round will introduce a new news event or global economic situation. Teams must interpret its implications, identify the resources and economic relationships that become more important, and negotiate with other countries to secure their national interests.
  • During each round, teams will have a limited period to negotiate trade deals, exchange resources, manage their financial capacity, and adapt their strategies to the evolving global environment.
  • Every decision carries consequences. A resource that seems less valuable today may become essential tomorrow, while excessive dependence on another country could leave a nation vulnerable to sudden disruptions.
  • Objective: Build a resilient and competitive economy through strategic negotiation, efficient resource allocation, and the ability to adapt to changing global conditions.

Final Round: The Future of Nations

Format: Strategic Presentation | 4 Minutes per Team

  • The final round moves beyond immediate trading decisions and challenges teams to think about the future of their economies.
  • Each team will deliver a four-minute presentation outlining its country's future economic strategy, based on the position it has built throughout the simulation.
  • Teams should explain how they intend to utilise their available resources, develop economic opportunities, establish strategic international relationships, and strengthen their country's long-term economic prospects.
  • The presentation should demonstrate forward-thinking economic reasoning, a clear understanding of resource interdependence, and the ability to connect present decisions with future outcomes.
  • Objective: Evaluate each team's long-term vision, strategic thinking, and understanding of how resource management and international economic relationships can shape national development.

title: The State Craft Challenge

problem_statement:
Overview

Think Strategically. Bid Wisely. Build Solutions.

Can you solve a state's most pressing challenges with limited resources, strategic decisions, and economic reasoning?

State Craft Challenge is an economics-based case competition that puts participants in the role of policymakers responsible for addressing real-world challenges faced by Indian states. From managing resource constraints to making strategic investments, teams must think critically, allocate resources efficiently, and develop practical solutions under a limited budget.

The competition combines economic knowledge, case-study analysis, auction-based resource allocation, teamwork, and presentation skills in an engaging simulation of policymaking.

Structure

Round 1: The Economics Quiz

Format: Online Quiz | Elimination Round

  • The competition begins with an economics quiz designed to test participants' understanding of economic concepts, current affairs, and their practical applications.
  • Participants will be assessed on their conceptual clarity, analytical thinking, and ability to connect economic principles with real-world situations.
  • Objective: Identify the 12 qualifying teams that advance to the next round.

Round 2: The State Challenge

Format: Case Study + Resource Auction + Presentation

  • The 12 qualifying teams will enter the main competition, where each team will be assigned an Indian state through a chit-based allocation system.
  • Each team will receive a case study outlining a specific problem faced by its assigned state. The challenge could involve issues such as unemployment, inadequate infrastructure, agricultural distress, water scarcity, industrial development, or other socioeconomic concerns.
  • Teams must analyse their case, identify the key challenges, and determine which resources are essential to developing an effective solution.

The Resource Auction

  • Participants will then compete in an auction to acquire the resources required to address their state's challenges. Working within a limited budget, teams must decide which resources to prioritise, how much to bid, and how to allocate their available funds efficiently.
  • The auction will test strategic thinking, resource management, decision-making, and the ability to balance competing priorities.

The Solution Presentation

  • After the auction, each team will present its proposed solution, explaining how the resources acquired will be used to address the assigned problem.
  • Teams should demonstrate the feasibility of their recommendations, justify their resource allocation decisions, and explain the expected economic and social impact on their state.

title: SustainX 2026: The Sustainability Hackathon
organizer: Great Lakes Institute of Management (GLIM), Gurgaon
venue_address: Great Lakes Institute of Management, Bilaspur Tauru Road, Near Bilaspur Chowk, Gurgaon, Haryana, 122413
problem_statement:
Overview

Design an AI-powered urban flood forecast system that Gurgaon's civic body could actually implement — and present it to the officials who can.

About the Competition

SustainX 2026 is a Delhi NCR inter-institutional hackathon hosted by the Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Development at Great Lakes Institute of Management, Gurgaon, as part of the 5th International Winter Conference on Sustainable Business (WCSB 2026).

WCSB is one of Great Lakes Gurgaon's flagship events, bringing together researchers, policymakers, and industry leaders each December to examine the intersection of Business and Sustainability. This year's conference theme is "Beyond Automation: AI, Human-Centricity, and Sustainability" — and SustainX is its student-facing counterpart: a solution-focused hackathon designed to turn that theme from conference panels into actionable civic solutions.

The Problem We're Solving

Every year, MCG releases a 'flood preparedness plan.' Every year, the same underpasses flood, and the same roads become rivers. On September 1, 2025, 133mm of rain in four hours caused a 20km traffic jam and a 51-hour power outage across the city. By late June 2026, the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) had completed desilting at just 16 of 36 hotspots against a May 31 deadline with monsoon already underway. MCG has identified 159 waterlogging hotspots across Gurgaon. It has no system that predicts which of them will flood before the rain arrives.

This year's SustainX 2026 asks one focused question: Can you design an AI-powered predictive flood management system for Gurgaon that MCG can actually build and operate?

Why Participate

The judging panel will include officials from Gurgaon's civic administration. Solutions that demonstrate genuine implementability — technically credible, operationally feasible, and grounded in how MCG actually functions — will be formally presented by GLIM-G to civic stakeholders as a policy brief. This is one of the few student competitions where your solution has a realistic path from a slide deck to a government briefing room.

Who Should Participate

This problem sits at the intersection of analytics, urban infrastructure, civil engineering, public policy, environmental science, and business strategy. We actively encourage interdisciplinary teams. You do not need to be from a business management background, you need to understand the problem and design something that works.

Prizes

  • Winner: ₹25,000 + Certificate of Excellence + Solution formally submitted to MCG/GMDA by Great Lakes Gurgaon
  • 1st Runners Up: ₹15,000 + Certificates of Excellence
  • 2nd Runners Up: ₹10,000 + Certificates of Excellence
  • All Round 1 submitters: Participation Certificate

Key Dates

  • Registrations + Round 1: Open now
  • Round 1 submission deadline: November 5, 2026, 11:59 PM IST
  • Round 1 shortlist announced: November 10, 2026
  • Round 2 submission deadline: November 24, 2026, 11:59 PM IST
  • Top 10 finalists announced: November 28, 2026
  • Final Presentation on campus: December 8, 2026

Background & Context

The Gurgaon Flood Forecast System — From Reactive Pumping to Predictive Drainage

Every year, MCG releases a flood preparedness plan. Every year, the same underpasses flood, the same roads become rivers, and the same residential sectors report basement damage. On September 1, 2025, 133mm of rain in four hours caused a 20km traffic jam and a 51-hour power outage. By late June 2026, MCG had completed desilting at just 16 of 36 identified hotspots against its own May 31 deadline — despite a mandate to desilt 607km of drainage network.

The failure is one of operations rather than budget: maintenance is reactive, data collection is manual, and resource allocation is driven by political pressure rather than hydrological risk modelling. Gurgaon's 159 identified waterlogging hotspots behave differently under different rainfall intensities, upstream blockage conditions, and seasonal silt accumulation rates. MCG currently has no system that predicts which hotspot will flood given a specific rainfall forecast — meaning pump deployment and emergency response are always chasing the flood rather than anticipating it.

Problem Statement

Design an AI-powered predictive flood management system for Gurgaon that enables MCG to move from reactive flood response to pre-emptive resource deployment — one that is operationally viable within MCG's existing technical and administrative capacity, without requiring a complete infrastructure overhaul.

What Participants Must Do

  • Map the drainage network topology: Identify which of Gurgaon's 159 waterlogging hotspots are upstream vs. downstream of each other, how blockages in one zone propagate flooding to others, and which 20% of the drainage network causes 80% of the city's flooding. Identify the critical intervention points that give MCG the highest flood-reduction leverage per rupee spent.
  • Design the AI predictive system: Specify the data inputs your system requires (IMD rainfall forecasts, real-time drain sensor readings, historical flood incident records, seasonal silt accumulation data) and how the AI processes these to produce a 24–48 hour flood risk map with confidence levels and recommended pre-emptive actions for each risk zone.
  • Design the MCG operations protocol: Outline the current operating procedure of MCG's maintenance and pumping crews. Given the AI's flood risk output, define exactly how MCG's maintenance crews and pump operators should allocate resources in the 12–24 hours before a forecasted heavy rainfall event. This should read as actionable SOPs — who does what, in what order, at which hotspot locations.
  • Propose the sensor and data infrastructure: Specify the minimum viable sensor network (rain gauges, drain level sensors, CCTV at key underpasses) that makes your AI system reliable. Include a capital cost estimate, a vendor-agnostic technical specification, and a maintenance model MCG can realistically sustain.
  • Design the citizen-facing alert interface: A publicly accessible system through which Gurgaon residents can see which roads and underpasses are at elevated flood risk in the coming 24 hours. Specify the communication channels (including SMS and IVR for residents without smartphones), the format of alerts, and how the system handles false positives without eroding public trust.

Expected Deliverables

  • Gurgaon drainage network topology analysis identifying critical intervention nodes
  • AI predictive system architecture: data inputs, processing logic, outputs, and confidence intervals
  • MCG pre-event operations protocol in SOP format
  • Sensor / technology infrastructure specification with capital cost estimate
  • Citizen-facing alert interface design with channel strategy

Key Design Constraints

Your solution must work within the following real-world constraints — solutions that ignore these will score poorly on viability:

  • The system must be operable by MCG's existing workforce without a dedicated data science team. If your system requires a PhD to run, it will not be implemented.
  • The sensor network must be designed for vandal resistance, outdoor weatherproofing, and low-maintenance operation in an Indian municipal context.
  • Your operations protocol must address the political economy of Gurgaon's civic administration: what happens when the AI system flags flood risk in a sector whose RWA has political influence? Your protocol must have an answer.
  • All cost estimates must be grounded in publicly available data or Indian market benchmarks — not international figures.

Eligibility

  • Open to all students currently enrolled in any undergraduate, postgraduate, or doctoral programme at a recognised higher education institution in Delhi NCR only — including Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida, Faridabad, Ghaziabad, and surrounding areas
  • All disciplines are welcome: Management, Engineering, Computer Science, Urban Planning, Civil Engineering, Architecture, Economics, Public Policy, Law, Environmental Science, Social Sciences, Design, and all allied fields
  • Interdisciplinary teams are strongly encouraged — this problem rewards diverse skill sets
  • Team size: 2 to 4 members; members may be from different institutions
  • Faculty members and working professionals may not participate as team members
  • Each participant may be part of only one team

Rounds & Submission Structure

Round 1: Problem Framing & Solution Hypothesis

Submit a 1-2 page Executive Summary of your solution (Word doc, or PDF) covering:

  • Your diagnosis of the core operational failure in Gurgaon's current flood management
  • Your proposed solution approach in brief, what your AI system does and how it is better than the current reactive model
  • The most critical design constraint your solution addresses, and how you've approached it
  • Your team's composition and the specific expertise each member brings

We are screening for quality of thinking and clarity of diagnosis. A complete solution is not expected at this stage.

  • Submissions close: November 5, 2026, 11:59 PM IST
  • File naming convention: TeamName-SustainX-R1

Round 2: Shortlisted teams submit the Full Solution

Shortlist announced: November 10, 2026

Shortlisted teams must submit both of the following:

Structured Slide Deck (mandatory, maximum 12 slides)

  • Must cover: problem diagnosis, AI system architecture, data model design, MCG operations protocol, technology / sensor infrastructure, implementation roadmap, and cost estimate.
  • Format: PowerPoint or PDF
  • File naming: TeamName-SustainX-R2

Working Prototype OR Financial Model (mandatory — either of two, or both)

  • Working Prototype: A functional demo, interactive simulation, or a working AI prediction interface, and the MCG operations dashboard. Must be demonstrable live during the final presentation.
  • Financial Model: A spreadsheet covering sensor infrastructure capital cost, system deployment cost, annual operations and maintenance cost, and projected reduction in flood-related economic damage as the financial case for implementation.
  • Format: Hosted demo of AI solution (shareable link) / ZIP (in case of multiple files) or Excel (financial model)

Submissions close: November 24, 2026, 11:59 PM IST

Final Presentation Round: December 8, 2026 at Great Lakes Gurgaon Campus, Gurgaon

Top 10 finalist teams will be announced on November 28, 2026, giving teams 10 days to plan their travel and logistics. Each team presents in a 10-minute slot followed by a 5-minute jury Q&A. Travel and accommodation are the responsibility of participating teams.

Rules & Guidelines

  • All submitted work must be original. Use of AI tools for research, drafting, and analysis is permitted — all sources and tools used must be cited.
  • Solutions must be grounded in Gurgaon's specific civic context. Generic smart city frameworks applied without local adaptation will not score well on viability.
  • Round 1 submissions are evaluated blind — do not include your institution name, team name, or any identifying information within the body of the Executive Summary inside the document.
  • All submissions must be made through the Unstop platform only. Submissions via email or any other channel will not be accepted.
  • The decision of the jury is final. No correspondence regarding results will be entertained.

title: Know Your Mind: The 7-Day Intelligence Streak Challenge

Find your intelligence. Then the career that fits it.

Most of us picked a stream, a degree or a first job before we knew how we think. This challenge gives you seven days to find out.

HireHelp AI reads how you think from your own words. It maps you across Howard Gardner's eight intelligences (words, logic, space, body, music, people, self and nature), then places 894 careers by how well they fit the way you think.

title: goSTOPS Marketing Case Study | The Road Less Booked | ₹30,000 Prize Money + Internship Opportunity
problem_statement:
goSTOPS Marketing Case Study – The Road Less Booked

₹30,000 prize pool | Internship opportunities | Real-world marketing challenge

What would it take to get young travellers to book a place they wouldn't normally consider?

At goSTOPS, we're tackling two real business challenges: driving demand for a mountain-view hostel outside Kasol's main market, and turning Alibaug into a more accessible destination for budget travellers beyond the weekend.

In The Road Less Booked, you get to choose one of these challenges and build a marketing strategy around it.

The challenge

Option 1: goSTOPS Kasol PLUS

The property is located outside Kasol's main market, away from the route most travellers typically follow. How would you turn its offbeat location and mountain views into a reason to book?

Option 2: goSTOPS Alibaug

Alibaug is often seen as a destination for villa stays and premium weekend trips. How can goSTOPS make it more appealing to budget-conscious young travellers, especially from Monday to Friday?

Choose one property and build your solution around its specific business problem.

What you'll work on

This isn't just a campaign-ideas exercise. Your solution should be grounded in consumer behaviour and practical business thinking.

  1. Consumer research: Survey young travellers aged 20–35 to understand their travel preferences, barriers, brand awareness and stay choices. Present your key insight.

  2. Marketing strategy: Define your priority audience, positioning, channels and scalable marketing ideas, supported by a campaign cost breakdown.

  3. Campaign execution: Develop a campaign concept and show 2–3 sample executions across your chosen channels.

We want to see original thinking, real consumer insights and ideas that could work in the real world.

Who should participate?

If you're interested in marketing, brand strategy, consumer behaviour, travel, growth or business problem-solving, this is your opportunity to put those skills to work.

  • Team size: 1–3 members

  • Format: Online

  • Registration deadline: 30 November 2026, 11:59 PM IST

Rewards

A total prize pool of ₹30,000, along with internship opportunities. Refer to the official competition details for confirmed reward terms and eligibility.

Ready to take on the challenge?

Choose your property, understand the traveller, and build a strategy that gets them to take The Road Less Booked.

Register on Unstop before 30 November 2026.

At goSTOPS, we believe that some of the best ideas come from people who are willing to question the obvious, look at problems differently, and turn challenges into opportunities. Through this case competition, participants will get a chance to showcase exactly that — their ability to think critically, collaborate effectively, and build solutions that are both creative and practical. Bring your ideas. Bring your curiosity. Bring your problem-solving mindset and get ready to see how far you can take your solution!

title: The Unheard Stroke - Painting Competition
problem_statement:
All That You Need to Know:

Finesse - The Art Club of IIM Ahmedabad presents The Unheard Strokes, a national-level painting competition organised as part of Palettes, our flagship annual art event held in December.

Art has the power to tell stories that words often cannot. Through this competition, we invite student artists from across India to express their creativity, share their perspectives, and bring their interpretations to life on canvas.

This year's theme, Echoes: The Past, Still Sounding in the Present, celebrates the timeless influence of memories, traditions, heritage, and imagination. We invite artists to look back, reimagine the present, or create worlds that exist beyond reality.

The competition will culminate in an exhibition at IIM Ahmedabad, showcasing selected artworks and the diverse perspectives of emerging artists.

Theme: ECHOES - The Past, Still Sounding in the Present

Some things never truly grow old. They live on in the art we create, the places we visit, the stories we tell, and the memories we carry.

From the charm of the ’80s and ’90s to the beauty of traditional art, from historic architecture to futuristic ideas inspired by the past, Echoes invites you to explore what has stood the test of time and give it a new meaning.

Whether you recreate a bygone era, reinterpret a centuries-old tradition, capture the stories hidden in heritage, or imagine an entirely new world, we want to see your unique interpretation.

Explore Echoes through the nostalgia of the ’80s and ’90s, traditional art forms passed down through generations, the stories and beauty of historic places, or imaginative blends of the past and future. You can also step beyond reality to create dreamlike landscapes and entirely new worlds. Interpret the theme through any medium or perspective that inspires you.

These are only starting points, not rules. Your imagination, your interpretation.

Look back. Reimagine. Create something that echoes.

Participation Guidelines:

  • Individual entries only.
  • Open to students enrolled in colleges and universities across India.
  • All painting mediums are welcome, including acrylic, oil, watercolour, and mixed media.
  • The artwork must be an original creation by the participant.

Submission Format and Artwork Requirements:

Round 1: Online Qualification

Participants must upload a two-page PDF on Unstop:

  • Page 1: Photograph(s) of the artwork (maximum two photographs).
  • Page 2: Artist’s Note explaining the concept, inspiration, and message behind the artwork.

The Artist’s Note must follow the prescribed template: Download Artist Note Template

Template link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Njo4AVHLpaiwpqHYwAZUYffSyzips-0_/view

Artwork Requirements for the Final Exhibition:

  • The artwork must be larger in area than an A3 sheet.
  • There is no upper size limit, subject to practical display requirements.
  • Artworks must be display-ready, either mounted, framed, or otherwise structurally supported.
  • Shortlisted participants must arrange delivery of their original artworks to IIM Ahmedabad, either in person or through a securely packed courier.

Stages and Timelines:

Round 1: Artwork Upload and Qualification

  • Participants submit their artwork photographs and Artist’s Note through Unstop.
  • A preliminary review will be conducted after the submission deadline.
  • A maximum of 25 artworks will be shortlisted for the final exhibition.

Round 2: Final Exhibition and Judging

  • Shortlisted artworks will be exhibited during Palettes at IIM Ahmedabad.
  • Winners will be announced after the exhibition and judging process.

Important Dates:

  • Registration and Round 1 submission deadline: 14 November 2026, 11:59 PM IST

  • Round 1 shortlist announcement: 18 November 2026

  • Deadline to dispatch shortlisted artworks: 22 November 2026

  • Deadline for artworks to reach IIM Ahmedabad: 1 December 2026

  • Exhibition and final judging: To be announced

Exhibit Your Art. Give It a Purpose.

Art can do more than inspire; it can also make a difference.

Participants will have the option to make their artworks available for sale during the exhibition. Those who choose to sell their work can decide what percentage of the sale proceeds they wish to contribute to a designated cause, subject to a minimum contribution of 50%.

Participants who prefer not to sell their artworks can opt for display only, with no obligation to sell or contribute.

Participation in the sale initiative is entirely voluntary. Whether an artwork is offered for sale or displayed exclusively for appreciation will have no impact on the judging criteria, evaluation, or final results.

Further details regarding the designated cause, sale process, and settlement of proceeds will be shared with shortlisted participants.

Exhibition and Judging:

Shortlisted artworks will be exhibited at IIM Ahmedabad during Palettes. Winners will be announced after the exhibition.

Judging criteria:

  • Concept and interpretation of the theme
  • Originality and creativity
  • Clarity and impact of the message
  • Artistic execution and technique

Participation in the optional sale initiative will not influence judging.

Artwork Return:

  • All submitted physical artworks will be returned within 3–5 working days after the event.
  • Participants sending their artworks by courier must bear the return shipping costs.
  • Separate arrangements will be communicated for artworks sold during the exhibition.

Originality and Authenticity:

  • Only original artworks created by the participant will be accepted.
  • AI-generated artwork, traced work, copied artwork, or work that infringes another artist’s intellectual property will be disqualified.

problem_statement:
DS Group is known for establishing benchmarks through Innovative Firsts across its businesses. Through TrenDSetter, a one-of-a-kind national-level B-school corporate challenge, DS Group brings students an opportunity to experience real-world business problem-solving, innovation, and strategic thinking.

Building on the success of its previous editions, TrenDSetter 5.0 brings an even more engaging and challenging experience for the next generation of business leaders. Get ready to put your creativity, analytical thinking, problem-solving skills, and business acumen to the test.

With the introduction of the Operations track, participants will get an opportunity to tackle real-world operational challenges, test their analytical and problem-solving skills, and develop efficient, scalable solutions that drive business performance and operational excellence.

From understanding the DS Group and its businesses to solving real-world business challenges and presenting your ideas to industry leaders, TrenDSetter 5.0 is your opportunity to step up and showcase what makes you a TrenDSetter.

  • This competition is open to the following:
    • All students pursuing a full-time MBA/PGDM programme.
    • Final-year students of a full-time Engineering programme.
  • Participants must register in teams of 2 - 4 members from the same institute.
  • Participants must fulfil all eligibility requirements specified for the competition.
  • Cross-specialisation teams are allowed, but cross-college teams are not permitted.
  • A participant can be a member of only one team.
  • There is no restriction on the number of teams that can participate from an institute.
  • Participants must fulfil all eligibility requirements specified for the competition.

Competition Structure: 

DScovery – Brand Quiz

  • Kickstart your TrenDSetter journey with DScovery, an engaging brand quiz designed to test your knowledge of DS Group, its brands, marketing, innovation, and relevant industry trends.
  • Hints for the answers will be shared through DS Group's social media handles. Stay tuned!
  • Note: Participation in this round is mandatory to proceed to the subsequent stages however it is not an eliminatory round.

MinDScan – Simulation 

  • Team Leaders will take on MinDScan, a business simulation round designed to test their ability to analyse real-world business situations and develop practical solutions.
  • Team Leaders will be presented with a business scenario and will be required to demonstrate their problem-solving, analytical, and decision-making skills.
  • The Operations Track will focus on challenges and situations relevant to Operations, enabling participants to tackle real-world operational challenges, test their analytical and problem-solving skills, and develop efficient, scalable solutions that drive business performance and operational excellence
  • Based on their performance, shortlisted participants will progress to the next round.

OdDSmaker – Executive Summary Submission

  • Shortlisted teams will participate in the OdDSmaker round, where they will be required to develop and submit a 2–3-slide PPT outlining the proposed solution in both PPT/PDF format
  • The submission should clearly communicate the problem understanding, proposed approach, and key recommendations.
  • Submissions will be evaluated based on the criteria specified for the round, and selected teams will progress to the next stage.

GranDStand – Case Discussion & Presentation

  • Shortlisted teams will present their detailed solutions to an esteemed jury panel comprising industry experts and DS Group representatives.
  • The teams will have 10 minutes to present their PPT, followed by 5 minutes of jury QnA
  • Teams will be evaluated based on the quality of their solution, problem-solving approach, strategic thinking, feasibility, and ability to effectively communicate and defend their recommendations.

Mentorship Session

  • Shortlisted finalists will get an opportunity to participate in a mentorship session with senior management and subject matter experts from DS Group.
  • The session will provide participants with an opportunity to gain insights from industry leaders and further refine their solutions ahead of the Grand Finale.

EpicDS Clash – Grand Finale

  • The finalists will present their final and refined solutions before a distinguished jury comprising industry stalwarts and DS Group leadership.
  • The Grand Finale will take place offline at DS Group’s headquarters, giving finalists the chance to pitch in person at the Group’s home office.
  • A fresh case will be released for the Grand Finale, common to participants across all tracks. Finalists will be required to develop and present their solutions within the stipulated timeline.
  • The team that emerges as the Champion TrenDSetter will be awarded the coveted title along with the applicable rewards.

Rewards & Recognition

  • Champion Team for Epic DS Clash: ₹2,00,000 + Trophies and Certificates
  • Runners-Up Team for Epic DS Clash: ₹1,50,000 + Trophies and Certificates
  • Cash Prize for Track Winners: ₹1,00,000
  • Cash Prize for Track Runners-Up: ₹50,000
  • Goodies & Merchandise: Chances to win exclusive goodies & merchandise
  • PPI/PPO Opportunities: Role opportunities may be offered to eligible participants, subject to applicable criteria and requirements

Get ready to challenge conventional thinking, solve real-world business problems, and showcase your ideas to some of the brightest minds at DS Group.

Are you ready to become the next TrenDSetter?

title: THE GENESIS: Humans Truly Merging with Tech
problem_statement:
The Last Smartphone — A National Product Case Competition

Organised by: Product Management Club, Masters’ Union

About the Event

What happens when the smartphone becomes obsolete?

Welcome to The Genesis, a national-level product management case competition that challenges students to imagine the future of human–technology interaction in the year 2050.

In a world where smartphones have disappeared, cybernetic interfaces combine spatial awareness, total memory, instant recall, and agentic intelligence to transform how humans live, learn, work, and connect. But with these advancements come critical questions about privacy, autonomy, accessibility, and the ethical boundaries of technology.

As a founding product team, your challenge is to design a cybernetic-interface product that genuinely improves human life—not merely keeps people connected. Identify a real human need, build an innovative product experience, map the technological investments required to make it possible, and define what your product will refuse to do.

The Genesis brings together aspiring product managers, innovators, and future founders to solve one of the most exciting product challenges of tomorrow.

Competition Structure

The competition consists of three rounds, taking teams from an online live quiz to product development and finally to an offline grand finale at Masters’ Union, Gurugram.

Round 1: Signal vs Noise — The Live Quiz

Mode: Online | Live and Proctored

Explore the future of augmented reality, cybernetic interfaces, brain–computer interfaces, and agentic AI through a live, timed quiz.

  • Watch curated clips showcasing futuristic technologies, real-world innovations, and dystopian possibilities.

  • Answer questions testing visual recall, technological awareness, product judgment, and second-order thinking.

  • Compete in timed quiz rounds designed to reward observation, reasoning, and quick decision-making.

  • The top 30 teams advance to the next round.

Duration: 45 minutes

Round 2: Build the Interface — The Product Challenge

Mode: Online | 10-Day Challenge

The top 30 teams will receive a unique Seed Constraint defining a specific user, location, and limitation. Teams must use this constraint to design a cybernetic-interface product experience for 2050.

Choose one of the following tracks:

  • Body & Longevity: Rethink health, wellness, and human longevity.

  • Mind & Memory: Explore memory, recall, learning, and the right to forget.

  • Learn & Work: Redesign how humans acquire skills and perform work.

  • Access & Ability: Build inclusive technology that expands human capabilities.

  • City & Movement: Reimagine urban mobility, personal safety, and everyday living.

  • Connection & Play: Explore new dimensions of human connection and shared experiences.

Submission Requirements:

  1. Product Deck: A PDF presentation of up to 12 slides covering the target user, problem, product experience, key use case, roadmap, business model, ethical safeguards, and success metrics.

  2. Team Video: A 2–5 minute video in which every team member appears on camera and explains the solution.

  3. Decision Log: A one-page document outlining three important decisions the team reconsidered, what changed their perspective, and the final choices they made.

  4. Optional Prototype: A clickable prototype, concept film, physical mock-up, or working demonstration can earn up to 5 bonus points.

Teams will be evaluated on human impact, product thinking, innovation, feasibility, ethics, scalability, and ownership of their decisions.

The top 8 teams will qualify for the Grand Finale.

Round 3: The Dais — The Grand Finale

Mode: Offline | Masters’ Union Campus, Gurugram

The top 8 teams will present their solutions before a jury comprising experienced product leaders, founders, deep-tech investors, accessibility experts, and industry professionals.

Each team will participate in:

  • Product Pitch — 8 minutes: Present the target user, product experience, key use case, and technological roadmap.

  • Jury Q&A — 5 minutes: Defend product decisions, feasibility assumptions, business strategy, and ethical considerations.

  • The Curveball — 3 minutes: Respond to an unexpected scenario that tests judgment, adaptability, and product leadership.

The jury will assess the strength of the solution, its measurable human impact, the team's reasoning, and its ability to navigate difficult real-world trade-offs.

The final ranking will be determined by combining the Round 2 score and Grand Finale score, each contributing 50%.

What Are We Looking For?

  • Human-Centred Innovation: Solutions that create measurable improvements in people's lives.

  • Strong Product Thinking: Clear problem definition, user journeys, thoughtful interactions, and meaningful product decisions.

  • Technical Feasibility: A credible roadmap explaining the breakthroughs required to make the solution possible by 2050.

  • Ethical Responsibility: An understanding of privacy, autonomy, accessibility, potential misuse, and unintended consequences.

  • Business Viability: A scalable and sustainable business model that serves the intended user.

  • Team Ownership: Original thinking, transparent use of AI, and the ability to defend decisions under questioning.

Prizes and Recognition

Winner

  • ₹60,000 cash prize

  • Potential pre-placement interview (PPI) or mentorship track with the sponsor, subject to confirmation

Runner-Up

  • ₹30,000 cash prize

Special Awards

  • Goodies and certificates for selected category winners

All Finalists

  • Certificates of recognition

  • Travel support for outstation teams, subject to confirmation

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to students from recognised universities and B-schools across India.

  • Undergraduate, postgraduate, and MBA students are eligible.

  • Students enrolled in working-professional programmes may also participate.

  • Each team must consist of 2–3 members.

  • Cross-college teams are permitted.

  • Each participant may register only once.

  • Masters’ Union students may participate; however, core members of the Product Management Club and their teams are not eligible.

Important Dates

The following dates are proposed and should be confirmed before publication.

  • 2 November 2026: Registrations open

  • 15 November 2026: Registrations close

  • 18 November 2026, 7 PM: Round 1 — Live Quiz

  • 19 November 2026: Round 1 results announced

  • 20 November 2026, 6 PM: Round 2 brief and Seed Constraint release

  • 29 November 2026, 11:59 PM: Round 2 submission deadline

  • 4 December 2026: Finalists announced

  • 12 December 2026: Grand Finale at Masters’ Union, Gurugram

Rules and Guidelines

  1. Teams must consist of 2–3 eligible participants.

  2. The Seed Constraint assigned to each team must be central to its proposed solution.

  3. The Round 2 product deck must not exceed 12 slides.

  4. The team video must be between 2 and 5 minutes, with every member appearing and speaking.

  5. AI tools may be used for research and visuals, but their use must be disclosed. AI-generated presenters, voice clones, and text-to-speech are not permitted in the team video.

  6. All submissions must reflect the team's own reasoning and decisions.

  7. Teams must be prepared to defend their product decisions during the jury interaction and respond to the live Curveball challenge.

  8. Late submissions, exceeding the permitted deck or video length, and other violations will attract penalties as specified in the competition guidelines.

  9. The organisers reserve the right to verify eligibility and disqualify teams that violate the competition rules.

  10. Detailed submission instructions, Seed Constraints, and round-specific guidelines will be communicated to shortlisted teams.

Why Participate?

Step beyond conventional case studies and build for a future that does not yet exist.

Challenge your product instincts, explore emerging technologies, solve meaningful human problems, and showcase your ideas before industry leaders.

The future of technology is not just about what we can build. It is about what we choose to build for humanity.

Are you ready to create The Genesis?

title: AI & Analytics: From Prediction to Decision
problem_statement:
Overview

Build an AI-supported business or system that can withstand the consequences of its decisions.

The AI & Analytics track at CaseUnion 4.0 explores how technology can address difficult operational and access problems. The submitted case pack contains four challenges.

The Fraud War Room

Redesign a bank or payment service provider’s UPI fraud detection and investigation workflow over a 90-day planning horizon. Connect detection to response, prioritise investigation and explain the tradeoffs between missed fraud and incorrectly flagged customers.

The Marketplace That Fixed the Wrong End

Design a claims-first AI health insurtech. Choose and defend a business model, explain the claims workflow and model its unit economics. Address human review, false rejections, appeals and hospital gaming.

The Mandi Decision

Design an AI advisor that helps smallholder farmers decide whether to sell, store, transport or contract-sell their harvest. Define the crops, states, delivery channels and revenue model. Model economics at a scale of 100,000 farmers and address the downside when recommendations fail.

The Justice Gap

Build a focused AI legal services company around one user group, one problem and one business model. Define the role of AI and licensed professionals, select two deployment states and establish a path to break-even within 24 months.

Submission Expectations

Follow the requirements of the assigned case. Explain the product or system, data requirements, operational workflow, economics and risk controls.

Rules

Clearly distinguish case inputs, external evidence and assumptions. Justify the relevant tradeoffs and specify where human oversight is required.

Process, Format and Eligibility

title: Marketing in the Age of AI
problem_statement:
Case Union 2026 – The Strategy

In a world where everyone can create more with AI, what can a brand truly own?

Case Union 2026, The Marketing Society’s flagship national case competition hosted by Masters’ Union, challenges participants to build an AI-first marketing strategy for an iconic Indian brand that strengthens its differentiation, consumer relationships and long-term competitive advantage.

The Challenge

  • Identify how AI is reshaping the brand’s competitive landscape and where it is vulnerable to imitation.
  • Uncover authentic consumer insights and brand truths through primary research.
  • Develop a distinctive, repeatable brand experience, ritual, cultural property or community that competitors cannot easily replicate.

Round 1: Mastermind Quiz

  • Financial Sheet: Costs, projected value, assumptions and base, upside and downside scenarios.
  • Research Appendix: Primary research findings, methodology, sample and supporting sources.
  • AI-Use Disclosure: Details of AI tools used and how outputs were validated.

Primary research through surveys, interviews, observation or social listening is mandatory.

Round 3: The Brand Room

  • The top six teams will present their strategies offline at Masters’ Union, followed by an 8-minute presentation and 7-minute jury Q&A. Teams will be evaluated on strategic distinctiveness, consumer insight, positioning, responsible AI use, execution and commercial viability.

title: ArTribute 2026
problem_statement:
Overview

ArTribute is Shaastra’s flagship nationwide online writing and painting submission competition, designed to channel creativity into gratitude. Every year, it brings together young artists, writers, dreamers and visionaries to express powerful ideas through creative expression.

Theme: SHADES OF HER

This edition is dedicated to celebrating every woman — ordinary, extraordinary, and everything in between. We honour their greatness and invite participants to immortalise their stories through artwork or the written word.

Event Modes

Mode: Fully online art submission competition

  • Painting Section: Express your artistic ideas through colours, brushstrokes and visual creativity inspired by Shades of Her.
  • Writing Section: Create compelling stories, recounts, or expressions through poetry or essay writing based on our broad themes.

Guidelines and Rules

  • Limit: Strictly one submission per registration (one payment ticket). Paying for the required payment ticket will give you access to submit.
  • Only one submission in either the painting section or writing section will be considered, even if two submissions are made.
  • If you want two submissions to be considered, please pay for the optional payment ticket as well.

Painting Section Guidelines

  • Original artwork only. Plagiarism will lead to disqualification.
  • Only one submission per registration.
  • Submission Format: Participants must upload a single PDF containing two images:
    1. A clear photo of the final artwork.
    2. A photo of the artist holding their artwork (face and artwork visible in the same frame).
  • Submissions that are not in this format will not be considered.
  • Restrictions: Digital artworks are strictly NOT accepted.

Writing Competition Guidelines

Word Limits & Categories

  • Poetry: 200–300 words OR up to 40 lines.
  • Essay Writing: 1000–1500 words.

Format

  • Entries must be submitted in PDF format.
  • Ensure the document is properly formatted, clearly readable, and includes the participant's name and category.

Rules

  • Entries must be original and written in English. Plagiarism or AI-generated content will result in disqualification.
  • Open to participants of all age groups.
  • Participants are free to engage with one or more of the themes provided.

Welcome to Ctrl + Alt + Escape at ESYA 2026, IIIT Delhi!

Think. Solve. Escape.

Step into an immersive escape room experience at ESYA 2026, the annual technical fest of Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology Delhi (IIIT-Delhi). Ctrl + Alt + Escape is a team-based competition that challenges your logical reasoning, problem-solving, creativity, and teamwork through a series of exciting puzzles, quizzes, clues, and treasure-hunt challenges.

Get ready to enter a world of mysteries, hidden clues, and mind-bending challenges! In Ctrl + Alt + Escape, teams must work together to uncover clues, solve puzzles, crack codes, and overcome obstacles to progress through the escape room.

Every challenge tests your ability to think critically, connect the dots, communicate effectively, and make decisions under pressure. With each solved puzzle bringing you closer to the final objective, teamwork and quick thinking will be the keys to success.
